items.title: [RFC]: Bound frontend drain latency for bulk aborts and long non-streaming completions
items.author: aoshen02
items.body_excerpt:
> **Revision 2026-10-07.** This RFC was rewritten around a model of where the time and > memory of an RL `pause(mode="abort")` go, and the PR stacks that follow from it. The previous > text is preserved verbatim in a comment below and in > [`history-original-rfc.md`](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/blob/rfc57479/docs/rfc-57479/history-original-rfc.md); its GPU evidence is > summarised in §9. Long derivations, full tables and reproduction commands are on the fork > branch [`aoshen02/vllm@rfc57479/docs`](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/tree/rfc57479/docs/rfc-57479), together with the > measurement harness ([`harness/`](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/tree/rfc57479/docs/rfc-57479/harness)). # 0. TL;DR An RL trainer pauses generation with `POST /pause?mode=abort` before a weight update, and then needs every partial rollout back. With long outputs and top-k logprobs, the default `/inference/v1/generate` response is several GB per request. Both frontends spend most of the post-pause time building and serialising it. The Python frontend can also run out of memory before the pause. We model the cost per (position, top-k slot) entry, derive which terms dominate, and propose two independent PR stacks, one per frontend. Each stack has one default-format change (same bytes as today) and one opt-in compact format for RL. **Workload:** 32 non-streaming requests in flight, 16,384 input tokens, 245,760 output tokens each, top-128 logprobs, aborted together. DP8 with one mock engine per rank and the real `DPCoordinatorProc`; EP8 is engine-side and not modelled by the CPU mock. Times are seconds from the pause until the client has parsed every response. Memory is the frontend peak RSS: per process for Python (32 API servers on one node), total for Rust (one process). | n = 32, DP8 | Base `0fd2e8d503` | Python stack | Rust stack | |---|---|---|---| | **Default format** (bytes identical to base) | Python: **FAIL**, node memory floor after ~8 min at 36 GiB per process [S2]
Rust: **32.9–33.2 s**, **199–202 GiB** [S2][S3] | **21.3 s**, **9.5 GiB** per process (round-24 tip, two build threads [S27]); 21.6 s / 6.0 GiB with one thread [S7] | **20.73 s**, **14.47 GiB** [S4] | | **RL compact format** (opt-in) | not available | **1.80 s**, **2.0 GiB** per process [S7] | **1.85 s**, **11.86 GiB** [S5] | | Response size per request | Python 2,199.6 MB, Rust 3,408.7 MB [S7][S6] | default 2,199.6 MB; compact 337.0 MB | default 3,408.7 MB; compact 337.0 MB | At bs = 256, base Rust aborted on a failed 4 GiB allocation (measured at DP4 [S20]), and the base storage path fails at DP8 at the node memory floor [S8] (base Python itself was not run at bs = 256). Both stacks complete: RL compact 10.87 s (Python) and 10.91 [10.88–10.97] s (Rust, measured on the previous Rust tip; see §5 for why this carries over) with the official 8-core client, which is the limit there [S7][S3]. **Proposed PRs.** All are on base `0fd2e8d503`. They are drafts in the submitter's fork for review; nothing is opened against `vllm-project/vllm` yet. | # | Frontend | PR | Product LOC (+/−) | Tests | Depends on | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | P1 | Python | [Frontend-only sample-logprobs container hook](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/pull/109) | +301 / −13 | +715 | — | | P2 | Python | [Public APIs for generate endpoint plugins](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/pull/110): `start_generate`, `replace_route` | +261 / −20 | +434 | stacked on P1 for review order (no code dependency) | | P3 | Python | [generate: keep sample logprobs as engine rows, render without objects](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/pull/111) | +871 / −34 | +495 | P1 (code); stacked on P2 | | — | Python | [`vllm-rl-compact` endpoint plugin](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/pull/112) (out of tree, not proposed for merge) | 0 in `vllm/` (+1,443 under `plugins/`) | +2,682 | P1–P3 | | R-A | Rust | [server: stream the default generate body from the request runtime](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/pull/107) | +380 / −46 | +496 | — | | R-B | Rust | [server: opt-in compact logprobs format for raw generate](https://github.com/aoshen02/vllm/pull/108) | +241 / −13 | +400 / −1 | R-A | **Merge order:** Rust R-A → R-B. Python P1 → P2 → P3; the plugin is released separately once P1 and P2 are in. The two stacks are independent. Two Rust changes with mock-only gains are kept as backup branches and are not proposed (§4). # 1. Problem and scope **The operation.** In RL training the rollout manager calls `pause(mode="abort")` on every API server before each weight sync. Engines abort the running requests and the frontends return each partial completion with `finish_reason="abort"`. The trainer cannot start the update until it has all partials, so the time from the pause to the last parsed response is on the critical path of every training step. The pause/resume API is from RFC #32103. **The workload.** It is the shape of our production RL rollout: - 245,760 output tokens per request, top-128 logprobs, 16,384-token input, non-streaming; - DP8 EP8, n = 32 per frontend node in the main cells and bs = 256 in the cohort cells; - `ignore_eos`, no stop strings, no prompt logprobs. **What RL needs from each response:** the output `token_ids`, and for every position the top-k token ids and their float32 logprobs. It does not need text, decoded token strings, the sampled slot or ranks. **Out of scope:** - **R3 (routed experts):** deferred by the submitter. The default `routed_experts` path is unchanged. - **Streaming:** RL here uses non-streaming requests. Streaming default responses are unchanged; the compact format rejects `stream: true` with 400 in Rust. Python compact streaming lives only in the out-of-tree plugin. - Engine-side pause semantics and DP consensus are unchanged. # 2. Theoretical model Each term below is derived first, then checked against a measurement. All constants are measured on GB200 nodes (Grace CPU). Full derivations are in [`theory.md`](https://github.com/aoshen02/

items.title: [Feature]: Shared per choice `ChatStreamProcessor` for chat serving and streaming derender
items.author: hickeyma
items.body_excerpt:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Tracking issue for a follow up from the #50550 review, where @sagearc asked whether streaming chat derender could use a shared `ChatStreamProcessor` (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50550#discussion_r3913908193).

#### Why

After #50550, streaming chat derender (`OnlineDerenderer._derender_chat_stream_parsed`) produces the same `reasoning` / `content` / `tool_calls` deltas that `/v1/chat/completions` streams for the same tokens. To do that it repeats the per choice post parse steps from `OpenAIServingChat.chat_completion_stream_generator`:

- building the parser (`parser_cls(tokenizer, tools, chat_template_kwargs=..., model_config=...)`)
- one `parse_delta` call per chunk
- tracking `tools_streamed`
- rewriting `finish_reason` to `tool_calls` unless a function was named in `tool_choice`
- `maybe_filter_parallel_tool_calls`

The two copies match today. Only code review keeps them that way until the streaming parity tests from #47161 PR3 land and any change to parser handling has to be made in both places. Streaming logprobs on the parsed derender path (after #55029) will add another shared rule drop: logprobs and token IDs when reasoning is hidden (`hide_stream_metadata` in serving).

#### Proposal

Pull a per choice processor out of `chat_completion_stream_generator`. It owns the parser and `tools_streamed` and handles one chunk per step: `parse_delta` → `finish_reason` → parallel tool call filter.

- **Chat serving** uses it for live output. The generator keeps what only serving needs:
  - skipping `None` deltas (unless it's the finish chunk or `return_token_ids` is set)
  - reasoning token counts for usage
  - delta logging
  - error finish reasons
  - `stop_reason` and `token_ids` on the chunk
- **Streaming derender** uses it for both replay and the current chunk. The derenderer keeps what only derender needs:
  - the replay loop over `output_chunk_lens`
  - tool call ID pinning via `last_tool_call_ids`
  - always returning a chunk
  - reading and returning `stream_state`

Responses API streaming stays out. It also calls `parse_delta` but emits a different event shape.

The shared part is thin, so getting the interface right matters more than how much code moves. For chat serving this is a pure refactor with no change to what `/v1/chat/completions` streams. ChatStreamProcessor` is the name from the review and it can change.

#### Sequencing

This should come after #50550 and streaming logprobs (#55029, then the parsed path), so the processor is shaped around both users as they end up. The chat streaming change can then be reviewed on its own. If this lands before the parser cache (#57571), the cache could hold this processor instead of a bare `Parser`.

#### Done when

- [ ] Processor extracted from `chat_completion_stream_generator`. Existing chat streaming and reasoning / tool parser tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] Streaming chat derender moved onto it. `test_derender_stream.py` passes unchanged.
- [ ] The hidden reasoning rule for logprobs and token IDs lives in the processor, so the parsed derender path applies it too.

### Alternatives

- **Do it before #50550 merges as a small PR that #50550 rebases on.** I proposed this in the review (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50550#discussion_r4005719757), then switched to a follow up (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50550#discussion_r4035126957). The code around the shared steps differs enough that it's easier to shape the processor once derender streaming and #55029 are in.
- **Keep the two copies.** Cheapest option. The streaming parity tests from #47161 PR3 would catch drift after the fact but every parser handling change would still have to be made twice.
- **Include the Responses API loop.** It emits a different event shape, so it's a bigger change for little gain.

### Additional context

- RFC #47161 (streaming derender), PR #50550
- #50550 review thread: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50550#discussion_r3913908193
- #55029: streaming logprobs for derender
- Parser cache / server side parser state: #57571

cc @sagearc @chaunceyjiang

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: custom all-reduce creates its NVLink multicast reduce-scatter buffer mid-serving (not at startup); the run then crashes (Xid + CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED)
items.author: almogx3
items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

In `CustomAllreduce` (`vllm/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce.py`), the NVLink-multicast ("multimem") reduce-scatter buffer is not created at startup. It is created the first time a reduce-scatter of a particular size happens, which can be many minutes into serving. On our 8× B300 node, the two runs that took this path both crashed right after the buffer was created. The many runs that never took it ran clean.

## Background

On NVLink-connected GPUs (MNNVL), custom all-reduce can run reduce-scatter on a low-SM "multimem" kernel. That kernel needs a dedicated multicast buffer: device memory mapped into an NVLink multicast object shared by all ranks. The other MNNVL buffers are set up when the communicator is constructed. This one is not.

## What the code does

1. `_select_reduce_scatter_backend` (`custom_all_reduce.py:621` on main at `242e4213f`) picks the `mnnvl_multimem` backend only when the reduce-scatter input is **larger than 16 MiB and at most 64 MiB**. These are `_DEFAULT_MNNVL_REDUCE_SCATTER_MAX_SIZE` and `_DEFAULT_MNNVL_MULTIMEM_REDUCE_SCATTER_MAX_SIZE` (lines 132–133).
2. The first time it picks that backend, it calls `_init_mnnvl_multimem_reduce_scatter_buffer()` (line 674). That allocates and maps the multicast buffer **in the middle of serving**, while other kernels and CUDA graphs are running.
3. It then logs `Using the low-SM MNNVL multimem reduce-scatter kernel.` (line 682).

Whether a run ever lands in the 16–64 MiB window depends on how many tokens are batched at runtime. So the same deployment can hit this path in one run and not in another. The two thresholds are hard-coded defaults; there is no setting to change them.

## What we observed

- **Setup:** 8× NVIDIA B300 (sm_103), one node with NVSwitch. NCCL 2.30.7, torch 2.13.0+cu130. Kimi-K3 with TP=8 + expert parallel + decode-context-parallel 8, MegaMoE, CUDA graphs on.
- **Run 1:** the log line above appeared 13–14 minutes into the run. In the same second the GPU raised an NVML Xid error and cuBLAS failed with `CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED`, and the engine died.
- **Run 2:** same log line at the same point, then `EngineDeadError`.
- **Every other run on the same GPUs** (dozens, same config family) never logged that line and finished cleanly. ECC errors stayed at 0 and there were no row remaps, so a faulty GPU is unlikely.

We have not proven causation. The lazy buffer creation is the only code path unique to the two failing runs, and it ran immediately before the fault.

## Suggested fix

Do either of these:
- Create the multimem reduce-scatter buffer at communicator setup, like the other MNNVL buffers, so it never happens during serving.
- Make the two size thresholds configurable, so a deployment can stay out of the 16–64 MiB window without disabling custom collectives altogether.

items.title: [good-first-issue] storage: convert f-string log calls in mooncakestore_connector.py to %-format
items.author: zilinfg
items.body_excerpt:
**Label**

`good first issue`, `documentation`/`chore` — filing under [[Onboarding 2026] Good first issues](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/3372) per the workflow in that thread.

**Describe the issue**

`lmcache/v1/storage_backend/connector/mooncakestore_connector.py` has 23 logger calls that build their message with an f-string, so the string is always interpolated even when the record is filtered out. Per @ApostaC's guidance in #3372, `%d`/`%s` style is preferred so the formatting is deferred until the record is actually emitted.

A few call sites in this file (the config-load and `setup()` paths) already use `%`-format, so this makes the file internally consistent.

Examples:

```python
logger.debug(f"Using batch_get_into for {len(keys)} keys (zero-copy mode)")
logger.error(f"batch_get_into threw exception: {str(exc)}")
```

become:

```python
logger.debug("Using batch_get_into for %d keys (zero-copy mode)", len(keys))
logger.error("batch_get_into threw exception: %s", exc)
```

Scope is one file, as suggested in #3372. No behavioral change.

---

**Side note that may be worth its own issue:** `[tool.ruff.lint]` in `pyproject.toml` sets no `select`, so ruff runs only its default rules (`E4`, `E7`, `E9`, `F`). Ruff's `G004` (`logging-f-string`) is exactly this check and is not enabled, which is why new f-string logging keeps landing. With `--select G004` it currently reports **396 violations under `lmcache/`**, and ruff has no autofix for it.

If maintainers are interested, enabling `G004` with a `per-file-ignores` list of the current offenders would stop new violations while the existing ones are burned down one good-first-issue at a time. Happy to file that separately — I didn't want to bundle a repo-wide lint config change into a single-file cleanup.

items.title: [Bug][MP] KV events are dropped in P/D disaggregation
items.author: bluayer
items.body_excerpt:
**Label**
bug

**Describe the bug**
KV-aware routers (Dynamo, llm-d) receive no LMCache CPU store/eviction events from P/D instances.

In disaggregated prefill (P/D) with LMCache MP, each vLLM instance runs `MultiConnector[NixlConnector, LMCacheMPConnector]`, as documented in `docs/source/mp/disaggregated_prefill.rst`; the operator's PD mode generates the same config. In this setup, LMCache's KV events never reach vLLM's KV event publisher, even though LMCache stores the KV.

LMCache MP sends worker-side events through `get_kv_connector_kv_cache_events()`. vLLM's `MultiConnector` does not override that method, so it returns the base default `None` and the LMCache child's implementation is never called.
  - vllm `multi_connector.py` still has `# TODO: Add a generic implementation of 'get_kv_connector_kv_cache_events' ... WIP: vllm#31811`.
  -  Related PR : vllm#31811 and vllm#34522 attempted upstream fixes; both were closed unmerged.
 
**To Reproduce**
Environment: LMCache `dev` @ 8c77a6f7, vLLM 0.29.0, NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`.
Reproduced with prefill and decode on one node, and across two nodes.
  
  1. Start two LMCache servers:
     `lmcache server --port 6555 --http-port 8090 --l1-size-gb 4 --chunk-size 256`
     `lmcache server --port 6556 --http-port 8091 --l1-size-gb 4 --chunk-size 256`
  2. Start prefill with config :
  --kv-transfer-config
  '{"kv_connector":"MultiConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_
  producer"},{"kv_connector":"LMCacheMPConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"lmcache.mp.host":"tcp://localhost","lmcache.mp.po
  rt":6555}}]}}'
       --kv-events-config '{"enable_kv_cache_events":true,"publisher":"zmq","endpoint":"tcp://*:5557","topic":"kv-events"}'
  
  3. Start decode the same way with
  `kv_role: kv_consumer` for MultiConnector/NixlConnector, `lmcache.mp.port: 6556`, and
  events on `tcp://*:5558`.
  4. Subscribe to both ZMQ endpoints and decode messages with
  `msgspec.msgpack.Decoder(type=vllm.distributed.kv_events.KVEventBatch)`.
  5. Send requests through the NIXL P/D flow (prefill with `do_remote_decode`, then decode),
  and count the received events.
  
  | Setup | LMCache L1 objects (prefill) | KV events on prefill ZMQ |
  |---|---|---|
  | Standalone `LMCacheMPConnector` (control) | 15 | `BlockStored(medium="CPU")`: 15 |
  | P/D `MultiConnector[Nixl, LMCacheMP]` | 15 | **0** (`_frames: 0`) |
  
  P/D itself works. Decode log:
  
  External prefix cache hit rate: 100.0% KV Transfer metrics: LMCacheMPConnector={'LMCache MP lookup count': 3, ...},   NixlPullConnector={'Num
  successful transfers': 3, 'Avg MB per transfer': 152.25, ...}

**Expected behavior**
With `enable_kv_cache_events=true`, the prefill instance in P/D should publish the same LMCache `BlockStored(medium="CPU")` events as standalone `LMCacheMPConnector`

items.title: [Bug]: HA snapshot recovery does not update applied sequence metric
items.author: Icedcoco
items.body_excerpt:
### Bug Report

### Summary

When an HA standby starts from a batch OpLog snapshot, the snapshot state and recovery cursor are restored successfully, but the exported `ha_oplog_applied_sequence_id` metric remains at its initial value. This makes the metric disagree with the standby's actual recovery position.

### Reproduction

The issue is reproducible with a snapshot whose recovered sequence is `117` and which has no incremental OpLog entries to apply after the snapshot:

1. Create and publish a valid batch OpLog snapshot covering sequence `117`.
2. Start an HA standby with snapshot bootstrap enabled.
3. Allow snapshot recovery to complete and the standby to enter `WATCHING`.
4. Read the standby metrics and synchronization status.

Observed result:

```text
recovery log:          snapshot/applied = 117
OpLogApplier expected:  118
snapshot applied batch: 51
standby state:          WATCHING
sync status applied:    117
ha_oplog_applied_sequence_id: 0
```

The standby's internal cursor and synchronization status show that sequence `117` has been recovered, while the exported applied-sequence gauge still reports `0`.

### Root cause

`OpLogApplier::Recover(last_applied_sequence_id)` updates only `expected_sequence_id` to `last_applied_sequence_id + 1`. It does not update the HA applied-sequence gauge.

The gauge is currently updated when an individual `ApplyOpLogEntry` succeeds. The snapshot bootstrap path installs the recovered baseline through `HotStandbyService::LoadBatchOpLogSnapshotBaselineLocked` and updates the standby's internal `applied_seq_id_`, but does not update `ha_oplog_applied_sequence_id`. Therefore, a snapshot with an empty incremental tail leaves the exported gauge at its initial value.

### Impact

- Monitoring reports an incorrect applied sequence immediately after snapshot recovery.
- Any alert, readiness check, or recovery validation based on `ha_oplog_applied_sequence_id` or derived lag can report a false failure or an incorrect recovery state.
- Operators cannot distinguish a metric reporting error from an actual OpLog replay failure using the exported metrics alone.

This is an observability and recovery-validation defect. The current evidence does not indicate data loss or incorrect recovered object metadata; the internal recovery cursor is correct.

### Expected behavior

After a successful snapshot recovery, `ha_oplog_applied_sequence_id` must equal the latest sequence represented by the recovered baseline, even when no incremental OpLog entries follow it:

```text
snapshot_applied_sequence = 117
ha_oplog_applied_sequence_id = 117
expected_sequence_id = 118
```

When incremental entries are subsequently applied, the metric must continue advancing to the latest successfully applied sequence.

### Scope of the fix

Synchronize the applied-sequence gauge with the recovered baseline during snapshot/bootstrap installation. Check all recovery paths that establish a baseline, including batch snapshot recovery, ordinary snapshot recovery, and local warm restart, so that the metric does not depend on at least one later OpLog entry being replayed.

Do not change the recovered cursor or treat the metric as the source of truth; the metric should reflect the already recovered cursor.

### Acceptance criteria

Add regression coverage for:

1. Snapshot recovery with no incremental OpLog tail.
2. Snapshot recovery followed by incremental entries.
3. A baseline at sequence `0`.
4. Consistency between the applied sequence, expected sequence, snapshot batch, and lag metrics.

The tests should verify both the internal synchronization status and the exported `ha_oplog_applied_sequence_id` metric.

### Additional context

The metric is defined as the "Latest OpLog sequence ID applied by Standby". A successful snapshot recovery already reports the recovered sequence in recovery logs and synchronization status, so the exported metric should expose the same value rather than remain at its process-start default.

items.title: [Roadmap][Feature] Support Moore Threads (MUSA) GPU
items.author: yeahdongcn
items.body_excerpt:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

## Motivation

Add first-class support for [Moore Threads](https://en.mthreads.com/) (**MUSA**) GPUs in **SGLang** (including `sglang`, `sgl-kernel`, and `multimodal_gen`), enabling SGLang to run efficiently and be optimized on MTGPU hardware while minimizing disruption to existing vendor backends and preserving upstream compatibility.

## Background

[Moore Threads](https://en.mthreads.com/) **MUSA** (Meta-computing Unified System Architecture) SDK provides a CUDA-compatible execution environment together with a vendor-specific runtime and software ecosystem. This design allows many CUDA-based projects to be ported to MUSA with limited source-level changes, while still enabling vendor-specific optimizations where necessary.

The proposed integration follows a **vendor-isolated branching model**, conceptually similar to how AMD integrates ROCm support into CUDA-centric projects. This comparison is made to clarify the architectural approach and does not imply any upstream NVIDIA-specific changes or dependencies.

By explicitly isolating MUSA-specific logic while preserving CUDA fallback paths, this approach aims to maintain upstream compatibility, minimize code churn, and keep vendor-specific optimizations well-scoped and maintainable.

### Why add MUSA support to SGLang

- Enable SGLang users to run models end-to-end on MTGPU.
- Preserve a single codebase that falls back to existing CUDA implementations.
- Provide targeted MUSA-optimized kernels for operators where performance is essential.

### Related MooreThreads repos referenced in this effort

- [torch_musa](https://github.com/MooreThreads/torch_musa): PyTorch extension for MTGPU.
- [mate](https://github.com/MooreThreads/mate): MUSA AI Tensor Engine, providing high-performance kernels and APIs compatible with FlashAttention / FlashInfer–style interfaces.
- [torchada](https://github.com/MooreThreads/torchada): A lightweight adapter layer that enables CUDA-style PyTorch extensions (`CUDAExtension`, build flags, etc.) to be reused on MUSA with minimal modification.
- [mthreads-ml-py](https://github.com/MooreThreads/mthreads-ml-py): Python bindings for MTML, providing GPU discovery, monitoring, and management capabilities. Functionally similar to `pynvml` for NVIDIA platforms.

## High-level approach

- Progressive vendor-branching: Add explicit `is_musa` device detection and `forward_musa` dispatch paths in Python layers. Default to existing CUDA paths as fallback so upstream compatibility is preserved.
- Compile-time adaptation for kernels: Use `torchada` and `setup_musa.py` to adapt build flags and extension metadata to compile existing CUDA extensions for MUSA where possible. Keep the original CUDA kernels as reference.
- Targeted MUSA optimizations: For performance-critical ops, implement MUSA-specific optimized kernels (fused kernels, different tiling, different intrinsics). Only change vendor-specific code paths; keep fallback implementations intact.
- CI & packaging: Add Dockerfiles and CI matrix entries for a MUSA-enabled build (or for cross-compilation steps), plus ops tests and model-level smoke tests.

```mermaid
flowchart TB

subgraph musa_libs [MUSA Optimized Libraries]
    deepgemm[DeepGEMM]
    flash_attn_3[Flash Attention 3]
    mt_deepep[MT-DeepEP]
    mate[MATE - MUSA AI Tensor Engine]

    mate --> deepgemm
    mate --> flash_attn_3
end

subgraph sglang_stack [SGLang]
    sglang[sglang]
    srt[srt]
    custom_op[MultiPlatformOp]
    models
    multimodal_gen

    forward[forward]
    forward_musa[forward_musa]
    forward_cuda[forward_cuda]

    attention_backend[Attention Backend]
    fa3_backend[FA3 - MATE]
    triton[Triton]
    torch_native[Torch.SDPA - Torch MUSA]

    deepseek[DeepSeek]
    layer_impl[layer_impl - is_musa customization]
    others[Others]

    musa_platform[MusaPlatform]
    fa3_platform[FA3 - MATE]
    torch_sdpa[Torch.SDPA - Torch MUSA]

    sglang_kernel[sglang_kernel]
    setup_musa[setup_musa.py]
    musa_ext[MUSA extension]
    musa_ops[MUSA kernels]
    cuda_ops[CUDA kernels - ported]
    fused_ops[fused kernels - e.g. silu_and_mul]
    misc_ops[allreduce / elementwise / kvcache]

    sglang --> srt
    srt --> custom_op
    srt --> models

    custom_op --> forward
    forward --> forward_musa
    forward_musa --> forward_cuda

    srt --> attention_backend
    attention_backend --> fa3_backend
    attention_backend --> triton
    attention_backend --> torch_native

    models --> deepseek
    deepseek --> layer_impl
    models --> others

    sglang --> multimodal_gen
    multimodal_gen --> musa_platform
    musa_platform --> fa3_platform
    musa_platform --> torch_sdpa

    sglang_kernel --> setup_musa
    setup_musa --> musa_ext

    musa_ext --> musa_ops
    musa_ext --> cuda_ops

    musa_ops --> fused_ops
    cuda_ops --> misc_ops
end
```

## Representative examples

### 1) sgl-kernel: build-time adaptation (example `setup_musa.py`)

```py
# Example: minimal change to compile as a MUSA extension via torchada wrappers
import torchada  # noqa: F401
from torch.utils.cpp_extension import BuildExtension, CUDAExtension

ext_modules = [
    CUDAExtension(
        name="sgl_kernel.common_ops",
        sources=sources,
        include_dirs=include_dirs,
        extra_compile_args={
            "mcc": mcc_flags,
            "cxx": cxx_flags,
        },
        libraries=libraries,
        extra_link_args=extra_link_args,
        py_limited_api=False,
    ),
]
```

### 2) MUSA-optimized fused op

```c
// Example C++ signature for a musa-optimized fused op
void musa_fused_add_rms_norm(
    torch::Tensor &input,
    torch::Tensor &residual,
    torch::Tensor &weight,
    double epsilon);
```

**Notes:** keep original CUDA implementation in repo; add `

items.title: [Bug]  DSV4.1 Flash + DSPARK: CUDA caching allocator exhausts GPU memory under sustained max-batch decode (OOM crash every 15–25 min), KV pool only 29% used
items.author: elain
items.body_excerpt:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with DSPARK speculative decoding on a single 8×B200 node is **stable under short benchmark windows (< 6 min) but crashes on a fixed ~15–25 minute cadence under sustained max-batch decode load**. Every crash has the same signature: all 8 TP ranks fail a 20 MB `expandable_segments` mapping with only 4–19 MB free, then the engine kills its own process tree. Docker restarts it, and it crashes again ~15–25 min later. Over a 2-hour sustained soak: **6 crashes, identical signature**.

Crucially this is **not a KV-cache capacity problem** — at crash time `full token usage: 0.29, swa token usage: 0.16` (KV pool `max_total_num_tokens=25,826,048`, ~71% of KV headroom unused). The PyTorch caching allocator's non-KV memory grows unboundedly under sustained load.

**Allocator failure — all 8 ranks within the same second (two shown):**

[rank0]:[W1010 01:38:17.257967532 CUDACachingAllocator.cpp:508] expandable_segments: memory mapping failed with OOM on device 0 while trying to map 20971520 bytes (free: 4718592, total: 191502876672).
[rank4]:[W1010 01:38:17.258494500 CUDACachingAllocator.cpp:508] expandable_segments: memory mapping failed with OOM on device 4 while trying to map 20971520 bytes (free: 19398656, total: 191502876672).

**Crash handler immediately after:**

[2026-10-10 01:38:23] kill_process_tree called: parent_pid=1, include_parent=True, pid=1
[2026-10-10 01:38:24] No live scheduler processes found; skipping py-spy and CUDA coredump.
[2026-10-10 01:38:24] SIGQUIT received. signum=None, frame=None. It usually means one child failed.

**KV pool NOT exhausted at crash time** (last scheduler lines before death):

Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 512, #cached-token: 48896, full token usage: 0.29, swa token usage: 0.16, #running-req: 195, #queue-req: 0

**Mitigation experiments we already ran (both failed, so this looks like unbounded growth, not headroom sizing):**

1. Removing `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` → the server crashes even under trivial load (single-digit concurrent probes) right after startup; the fixed-segment allocator is strictly worse here.
2. Lowering `--mem-fraction-static` 0.75 → 0.73 (frees ~3.8 GB/GPU for the allocator) → **crash cadence unchanged** (4 crashes in 5 sustained windows), same signature.

**Related issues checked and ruled out:**
- #36333 (zombie requests after client disconnect): zero occurrences of `"state was deleted in TokenizerManager"` in our logs.
- #37553 (unbounded `custom_mask` via `torch.cat` in EAGLE/DFlash): DSPARK's verify path passes `custom_mask=None` throughout (`dspark_components/dspark_verify.py`), so it does not use that code path.

Secondary observation: before each crash, sustained throughput degrades ~15–20% vs short-window burst and TTFT/ITL p95 drift up, consistent with growing allocator pressure. This makes the current V4.1 preview unfit for sustained saturated serving on our node (`--restart unless-stopped` recovers in ~8 min per crash as a stopgap). Sustained-load stability may be worth adding to the V4.1 roadmap (#42170) — short-window benchmarks cannot catch this bug class. Happy to provide full container logs / dmesg / workload details on request.

### Reproduction

1. Start the server with the command below.
2. Drive **sustained** saturating decode load at high batch — we replay real SWE agent traces at ~192 concurrent sticky sessions with continuous streaming requests (each request carries its full session prefix, up to ~300K tokens). Any sustained max-batch decode workload with DSPARK on should work.
3. Within 15–25 minutes the process dies with the allocator signature above; docker restarts it; it dies again every 15–25 min.
4. Note: 6-minute benchmark windows never trigger it — the failure only appears under sustained load, so a quick `bench_serving` pass will look clean.

Launch command:

```bash
docker run -d --name sglang_standalone --network host --ipc host --gpus all \
  --shm-size 67108864 --restart unless-stopped \
  -v /data/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash:/models:ro \
  -e SGLANG_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=60 -e PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \
  lmsysorg/sglang:dev-dsv41 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --tp 8 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --trust-remote-code \
  --context-length 1048576 --page-size 64 --mem-fraction-static 0.75 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 32768 --max-prefill-tokens 32768 \
  --max-running-requests 256 --enable-cache-report --enable-metrics \
  --enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 \
  --log-level info

Startup reference numbers: max_total_num_tokens=25826048, available_gpu_mem≈20.5 GB after init.

### Environment

```markdown
- Hardware: 8 × NVIDIA B200 (192 GB each, SM100), single node, NVLink, host network
- Driver / CUDA: 580.178.04 / CUDA 13.0.3 (in container); torch 2.13.0+cu130; NCCL 2.30.7
- SGLang: `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-dsv41@sha256:4a5d132a06a7` (sglang 0.0.0.dev1+gda64c5cbb) — this is still the newest V4.1 preview digest as of 2026-10-10
- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (476 GB, bundled 3-stage DSPARK draft, `num_nextn_predict_layers=3`)
- Workload: SWE agent-trace session replay — 400 sticky sessions replayed continuously, ~192 concurrent sessions, streaming (`stream=true`, `include_usage`), per-request prompts carry full session history (up to ~300K tokens)
- Quant/KV defaults: KV dtype fp8_e4m3, attention backend dsv
score_reasons: 匹配 KV 与存储、Serving 与评测、Kernel 与正确性、工程与测试

items.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (dsv4 + DSPARK): multi-turn prefix cache degrades to a constant ~11.5K-token hit — 60–80K conversation prefix re-prefilled every turn (GLM-5.3-Flash unaffected in the same   environment)
items.author: F0rtiter
items.body_excerpt:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (dsv4 / FlashMLA hybrid KV pool, DSPARK speculative decoding) for
  Claude Code traffic (Anthropic `/v1/messages` via a relay). Prefix reuse works correctly at the
  beginning of the run; after the server has been up for a while, **every turn of a long agentic
  session hits exactly 11,520 cached tokens and re-prefills the whole 60–80K-token conversation
  prefix**, and the state persists.

  Log excerpt — consecutive turns ~10 s apart (TP0, default `--chunked-prefill-size 4096`;
  `#cached-token: 0` on chunks 2..N of the *same* request is expected for chunked prefill — the
  problem is that the first chunk's hit never grows across turns):

  ```
  [21:51:38] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 4096, #cached-token: 11520, full token usage: 0.00, swa token usage: 0.00, ... #pending-token: 60864
  [21:51:38–45]  15 more chunks of the same turn, all #cached-token: 0, #pending-token: 60864 → 0
                 → turn total ≈ 76,480 prompt tokens, 64,960 recomputed
  [21:51:46] Prefill batch, #new-token: 4096, #cached-token: 11520, #pending-token: 62293   → turn ≈ 77,909 tokens (+~1.4K vs previous turn)
  [21:51:55] Prefill batch, #new-token: 4096, #cached-token: 11520, #pending-token: 66335   → turn ≈ 81,951
  [21:52:06] Prefill batch, #new-token: 4096, #cached-token: 11520, #pending-token: 67712   → turn ≈ 83,328
  ```

  Expected: turn N+1 is a strict append of turn N, so it should hit ≈ turn N's full prompt and
  prefill only the appended ~1–4K tokens. Observed: hit pinned at exactly 11520 (45 × 256-token
  pages — consistent with the stable system prompt), everything after it recomputed.

Key observations:

  - **GLM-5.3-Flash control:** with the *same* host, relay, and Claude Code client, GLM-5.3-Flash
    shows normal multi-turn prefix hits on comparable traffic. Only DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash degrades.
    This argues against the client-side causes documented in #35129 (`cch=` request mutation,
    task-list snapshot churn), since those would corrupt prefixes for any model behind the same
    relay.
  - `full token usage: 0.00` / `swa token usage: 0.00` while `#full token` ≈ 76–82K → the device
    pool is nowhere near full; plain capacity eviction should not produce a *stable* miss boundary.
  - The hit length is byte-stable at 11520 across turns → the effective divergence point sits right
    after the system prompt.
  - DSPARK speculative decoding is active (decode logs show `accept len` 3.4–4.8).
  - Earlier in the run, multi-turn hits were normal.

  Relation to #35129: same family (DSv4 + Flash + Claude Code agentic sessions; long multi-chunk
  requests lose prefix reuse). Of the three causes #35129 closed with, HiCache load-back eviction
  storms are ruled out by configuration here (no `--enable-hierarchical-cache`;
  `SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=1` only offloads the engram *embedding* hash table to host
  memory, not the KV path), and the two client-side causes are made unlikely by the GLM control
  above.

Suspected area (not yet verified — the dsv4.1-specific cache structures that GLM-5.3-Flash does
  not share):

  - the DSv4 compressed indexer sidecars (c4 / c128 pools, `deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`,
    `index_key_cache.py`, `deepseek_v4_compress_state.py`) — if a bounded auxiliary structure stops
    accepting or exposing entries once full, matches would get capped at a stable boundary exactly
    like this, while `full token usage` stays ~0;
  - SWA-tombstone match validation in the unified tree (`unified_cache/components/swa.py`);
  - radix-cache insertion on the DSPARK verify path (`speculative/dspark_components/`).

  Diagnostics (happy to post results):

  1. **Identical-body replay:** send the same >64K-token request twice back-to-back and compare
     `#cached-token` — distinguishes engine-side (second request still only hits 11520) from
     request-content drift.
  2. A/B with `--speculative-algorithm` removed, same traffic.
  3. Watch `evicted_tokens_total` / pool usage on `/metrics` across the degradation moment.

### Reproduction

- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, `--attention-backend dsv4` (`page_size=256` auto-forced), TP=8 / EP=1,
    `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK`, default `--chunked-prefill-size 4096`.
  - Workload: Claude Code sessions over `/v1/messages`; turn N+1 = turn N + appended messages;
    prompts grow 76K → 83K tokens. Degradation appears after the server has been running for a
    while and then persists.
  - Minimal form: any two consecutive append-only requests whose prompt spans several
    chunked-prefill chunks (~64K+ tokens here) sent seconds apart; in the degraded state every turn
    logs `#cached-token: 11520`.

  Launch command (Docker, image `lmsysorg/sglang:dev`):

 ```
  sglang serve \
    --model-path /models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
    --tp 8 --ep-size 1 \
    --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \
    --enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay \
    --attention-backend dsv4 \
    --moe-runner-backend marlin \
    --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 \
    --max-running-requests 64 \
    --reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto \
    --served-model-name reasoner \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --swa-prefix-tails 1024 \
    --enable-metrics --enable-cache-report \
    --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \
    --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 \
    --watchdog-timeout 3600

  # container env (not KV-cache related, listed for completeness):
  #   SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=

items.title: [Bug]: prefix caching + MTP still corrupts output on hybrid Mamba/GDN models in v0.28.0 (#43559 closed but unfixed)
items.author: ionut-anghelina
items.body_excerpt:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.13.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-6.8.0-1010-gcp-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 12.0.140 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0-7: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (single GPU used for this report, TP=1) Nvidia driver version : 580.173.02 ============================== CPU Info ============================== Architecture: x86_64 Model name: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8481C CPU @ 2.70GHz CPU(s): 208 Hypervisor vendor: KVM ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.28.0 vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled GPU Topology: NV18 all-to-all (8x H100 SXM), TP=1 used Relevant packages: vllm==0.28.0 torch==2.13.0 transformers==5.15.1 flashinfer-python==0.6.16.post3 compressed-tensors==0.17.0 xgrammar==0.2.3 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug **Summary.** `--enable-prefix-caching` together with MTP speculative decoding still corrupts output on hybrid (GDN/Mamba) Qwen3.5-class models in **v0.28.0**. A small fraction of responses degenerate into repeated punctuation (`!!!!…`) or come back empty. This is the same failure as #43559, which was closed as completed on 2026-08-06 — the merged scheduler-side fix (#51113) does not cover it, and the cache-manager-side fixes (#43650, #48375) are still open. **Model.** Qwen3.5-architecture dense 27B VLM (`Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, hybrid: Gated DeltaNet linear-attention layers + full attention every 4th layer, vision tower), FP8 W8A8 compressed-tensors (`FP8_DYNAMIC`), with an MTP head present in the checkpoint (`Qwen3_5MTP` resolves at startup). TP=1, single H100. **Server command** (paths redacted): ```bash export VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1 export VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 vllm serve \ --served-model-name path-mini \ --port 8000 \ --max-model-len 62768 \ --max-num-seqs 32 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --enable-chunked-prefill \ --limit-mm-per-prompt.image 10 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --mamba-cache-mode align \ --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 2}' ``` Startup confirms the configuration: `Resolved architecture: Qwen3_5MTP`, `enable_prefix_caching=True`, `num_spec_tokens=2`, `GPU KV cache size: 576,637 tokens`, attention block size 800 (forced up to match the mamba page size), async scheduling enabled (default). **Workload.** Multi-step GUI-agent traces: each request is a conversation of prior steps plus 1–3 screenshots (sliding 2-image history), ~4k–12k prompt tokens, ~20–100 output tokens, `temperature=0`, client concurrency up to 32. Consecutive steps of the same episode share a long prefix, so prefix-cache hit rate climbs through a run. **Observed.** | vLLM | prefix caching | MTP | final prefix-cache hit rate | malformed responses | |---|---|---|---|---| | 0.26.0 | on | k=2 | 27.5% | 25 / 2,636 (0.95%) | | **0.28.0** | **on** | **k=2** | **31.7%** | **4 / 495 (0.81%)** | | 0.28.0 | on | k=2, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` | ~10% (see note) | 0 / 1,135 | Malformed = response is a run of repeated `!` characters, or empty content. `finish_reason` is normal; no HTTP 5xx, no crash, no traceback — the engine stays healthy and every other response in the same run is correct. Two observations that point at the prefix cache rather than at MTP alone: 1. **Rate tracks cache hit rate.** Corruption appears only once the prefix cache starts hitting, and scales with the hit rate. 2. **`--kv-cache-dtype fp8` appears to avoid it, but only by destroying the cache.** With fp8 KV, vLLM raises the attention block size 800 → 1600 (`platforms/interface.py`, so that one attention page covers one mamba page). Our requests share ~1,700 tokens of prefix, so at a 1600-token matching unit almost nothing is reusable: hit rate collapses from 31.7% to ~10%, and malformed responses go to 0/1,135. That is consistent with reduced exposure, not with fp8 fixing the underlying defect. (For the same reason `--block-size 800` cannot be used to compensate: the value is derived and only ever raised.) **Suspected cause** (already described in #43650 / #48375): `MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit` in `vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py` accepts `drop_eagle_block` and never acts on it, so the final matched block — which can hold recurrent state written over draft positions that verification later rejected — stays reachable through the prefix cache and is reused by subsequent requests sharing that prefix. `FullAttentionManager` drops that block. In v0.28.0 the caller (`kv_cache_coordinator.py`) additionally skips the eagle margin for `MambaSpec` with the comment *"its finder never drops"*, i.e. caller and manager disagree about who is responsible. Applying **#43650** (6 lines, `max_num_blocks -= 1` when `use_eagle`) on top of v0.28.0 starts cleanly and shows no regression on an unrelated accuracy check (100 grounding requests at concurrency 32: 76% vs 75% unpatched, identical coor

items.title: [Bug]: Speculative decoding (mtp and dflash) silently disables prefix-cache hits for hybrid GDN models on nightly; worked on v0.24.0
items.author: cgoudie
items.body_excerpt:
(analysis by Fable 5)
### Your current environment

- DGX Spark (GB10, `sm_121`/`sm_121a`, aarch64, 128 GB unified memory), Docker `--network host --gpus all --ipc host`
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` → reports `v0.28.1rc1.dev43+g6f7df92a8`
- Comparison baseline on the same host: `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.24.0`
- Model: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (hybrid GDN: 48 linear-attention + 16 full-attention layers, built-in MTP head). Also reproduced with `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` + `incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (rev `dedf8df`).
- `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 65536`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.30`, env `CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_121a`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

On the current nightly, enabling **any** speculative decoding method (built-in `mtp` or `dflash`) on a hybrid GDN model silently drops `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` to **0** — align-mode prefix caching engages at startup (log: `Mamba cache mode is set to 'align' for Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`) but never hits, and repeated long prompts pay full re-prefill. The identical command minus `--speculative-config` hits normally. No crash, no warning — the caching is just inert, so this is easy to miss in production.

A/B on the same host, same model, same 18,219-token prompt sent twice (`max_tokens=10`):

| nightly config | TTFT req1 → req2 | `prefix_cache_hits_total` delta |
|---|---|---|
| APC only (no spec) | 9.46 s → **0.64 s** | **17,248** |
| APC + `{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}` | 23.6 s → 13.9 s* | **0** |
| APC + `{"method":"dflash", ..., "num_speculative_tokens":7}` | 12.9 s → 12.5 s | **0** |

\* the MTP row also shows a large decode regression on this platform (10.5 tok/s vs 19.7 on v0.24.0 with the same flags — possibly a separate sm_121 issue; noting it for context, not the subject of this report).

**On `v0.24.0`, MTP + align-mode APC coexist correctly** on the same host/model: repeated 9,901-token prompt → 8,000 tokens hit, TTFT 7.27 s → 1.33 s, with `mtp` k=3 active. So spec+APC coexistence for hybrids existed and regressed somewhere between v0.24.0 and the current nightly.

Repro (nightly):

```bash
docker run --rm --init --network host --gpus all --ipc host \
  -v /opt/models:/models -e CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_121a \
  vllm/vllm-openai:nightly /models/qwen3.8-27b-nvfp4 \
  --served-model-name bench --port 10099 \
  --max-model-len 65536 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.30 \
  --max-num-seqs 1 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
# send any >3,300-token prompt twice; watch vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total stay 0
# drop --speculative-config and the second send hits ~all full blocks
```

Possibly related but distinct: #53670 (hits occur but recompute per hit), #41884 (DFlash+APC IndexError crash — we see silent zero-hit, not a crash), #26201 (tracking).

Is the suppression intentional (spec-decode + hybrid APC support not yet wired on the new path), or a regression? If intentional, a startup warning like the align-mode one would save users from silently losing their cache. Happy to run further diagnostics on this hardware.

items.title: Feature Request: Graceful reasoning budget termination. Avoid mid-sentence cutoff.
items.author: CleStil
items.body_excerpt:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

PR #20297 (merged ~2025-03-11) added `--reasoning-budget-message`, which injects
a string at the hard token cutoff to signal the model to wrap up. The injection
still happens at exactly token N with zero warning. The model gets no time to
finish its current thought before the `</think>` boundary.

Graceful termination before the cutoff is expected to improve reasoning
performance. See Motivation and Possible Implementation for details.


### Motivation

Raw truncation of the thinking trace measurably reduces answer quality compared
to graceful termination. Muennighoff et al. (s1: Simple test-time scaling,
arXiv:2501.19393) showed that appending an end-of-thinking delimiter with
"Final Answer:" before the hard cut outperforms naïve truncation. This was
confirmed by follow-up work (arXiv:2505.05315), which states directly that
"the S1 approach performs better than directly truncating the full reasoning
trajectory, underscoring the importance of preserving the solution segment."

The current --reasoning-budget-message implementation injects a wrap-up message
at exactly token N, leaving the model zero tokens to actually act on it. This is
functionally equivalent to truncation with a cosmetic suffix — the model cannot
produce a meaningful conclusion within 0 remaining tokens.

### Possible Implementation

Three approaches in increasing complexity:

Option A — message offset
Inject the budget message at `budget - offset` instead of `budget`, giving the
model `offset` tokens to act on the wrap-up signal. The s1 paper
(https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19393) shows this outperforms raw truncation.
Change in the COUNTING state of reasoning-budget.cpp:

    if (ctx->remaining <= ctx->warn_offset)  // was: <= 0

Files: reasoning-budget.cpp, reasoning-budget.h, common.h, arg.cpp,
sampling.cpp. Default 0 preserves current behavior.

Option B — separate budgeting
Split total budget into thinking (t) and conclusion (s) phases, t + s = budget.
Force `</think>` at token t, leave s tokens for a conclusion before the answer.
Follow-up work on s1 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.05315) shows this outperforms
the basic offset approach. Would add a second parameter, e.g.
--reasoning-budget-conclusion M.

Option C — logit biasing toward `</think>`
Ramp up the logit weight of `</think>` as the budget runs low, then force it at
the hard limit. No dependency on an injected phrase, model-agnostic. NVIDIA NIM
uses this approach with a 10% extension window for sentence completion. More
invasive (sampler changes) but cleanest long-term.

Options A and B build on the existing message injection architecture. Option C
is a parallel approach that could coexist with either.

items.title: Eval bug: llama-server crashes (stack overflow / access violation) on hybrid recurrent models (qwen3_5_moe) with mmproj vision when alternating text and image turns
items.author: IvanAndreychikov
items.body_excerpt:
### Name and Version

```
E:\lamma-cpp\llama-bin-win-cuda-x64>llama-server.exe --version
version: 0.3.0-dev (build 10679, commit 50f068fff) built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x64
```

Also reproduced on b10639 and on current master sources (checked `src/llama-memory-recurrent.cpp` and `tools/server/server-context.cpp` — identical in master).

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

CUDA, CPU

### Hardware

Ryzen 9 9950X3D, 96 GB RAM, RTX 4080 16 GB + RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB (tensor-split across both, `-sm tensor -ts 1,1`)

### Models

Ornith-1.5-35B Q8_0 (qwen3_5_moe architecture: 48 Gated DeltaNet layers + 10 attention layers, embedded MTP) + mmproj BF16 vision projector

https://huggingface.co/ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-GGUF

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

When using llama-server with a hybrid (recurrent/DeltaNet) multimodal model, the server dies mid-request in real workloads where text messages and image recognition requests alternate (my agent client re-sends the full conversation history each turn, cache_prompt on). The process exits silently; Windows Event Log records `0xc00000fd` (STACK_OVERFLOW) or `0xc0000005` (ACCESS_VIOLATION) in ggml-base.dll, or `0xc0000409` (fail-fast) in ucrtbase.dll.

Key observations:

1. Right before dying, the log fills with repeated warnings from `llama_memory_recurrent::find_slot`:
```
W find_slot: non-consecutive token position 49799 after 49798 for sequence 0 with 128 new tokens
W find_slot: non-consecutive token position 49799 after 49799 for sequence 0 with 128 new tokens
(repeats ~20x at the same frozen position, then)
W find_slot: non-consecutive token position 49853 after 49799 for sequence 0 with 4 new tokens
I slot print_timing: ... prompt processing, progress = 1.00
<process exits>
```

2. Deterministic reproducer: with `-b 1024 -ub 1024` the crash happens on the FIRST image turn (access violation in ggml-base.dll at offset 0x1c620, before "encoding image slice" is even logged). 100% reproducible across b10639 / b10679 / master. With `-ub 128` the same workload instead produces a fixed number of `non-consecutive` warnings per image turn (+18 with `--image-min-tokens 1024`, +4 without) and the server survives short tests, but real agent sessions (~50K context, multiple images, streaming) eventually crash the same way.

3. Server command for the deterministic repro (any CUDA GPU works; two-GPU split is not required for the warning storm):
```
llama-server -m Ornith-1.5-35B-Q8_0.gguf --mmproj mmproj-Ornith-1.5-35B-BF16.gguf ^
  -c 249856 --flash-attn on --split-mode tensor --tensor-split 1,1 -ngl 99 ^
  -np 1 -t 16 -b 1024 -ub 1024 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 --jinja --reasoning-preserve
```
Then: (a) send one ~38K-token text turn via /v1/chat/completions, let it finish; (b) send a second request with full history plus one small image (base64 data URL). The server dies during step (b) right after `launch_slot_`.

A self-contained reproduction script is attached (**repro-server-crash.sh**, bash + curl only, no other dependencies; the test image is embedded as base64). Run it while the server is up:

```
./repro-server-crash.sh killer   # expects: [turn 1] http=200, then SERVER DIED on image turn
./repro-server-crash.sh soak     # alternating turns; grep the server log for
                                 # "find_slot: non-consecutive token position" (grows per image turn)
```

Verified output on my machine (killer mode):

```
[turn 1] sending text preamble (~1350 items, ~38K tokens)...
[turn 1] http=200
[turn 2] sending image turn (the server dies here with -b 1024 -ub 1024)...
[turn 2] http=000
SERVER DIED on image turn (expected in killer mode)
```

4. Root-cause analysis (from reading the source):

- The warning is emitted at `src/llama-memory-recurrent.cpp:651`, where the comment admits: "Clearing the state mid-batch would require special-casing which isn't done."
- `llama_memory_recurrent::seq_rm` (`src/llama-memory-recurrent.cpp:150-193`) returns `false` when a partial rollback is larger than the snapshot ring (`n_rs_seq`) or a pending rollback exists. The caller does not handle this failure: the stale recurrent tail is never rolled back, and subsequent ubatches walk over stale cells (the frozen-position warning storm).
- In `tools/server/server-context.cpp` (~line 3233) the divergence path only restores a context checkpoint / forces full re-processing when `pos_min >= pos_min_thold`. For a non-SWA hybrid model `pos_min` stays 0, so this safety net never fires; `slot.prompt.tokens.keep_first(n_past)` truncates the token list, but the recurrent state keeps the discarded tail.
- Independently of cache divergence, every image turn injects non-consecutive positions into the recurrent memory via the mtmd embedding-decode passes (this happens even in a fresh conversation with a single image), which is where the warnings and the state pollution originate.
- Net effect: the SSM/DeltaNet state silently continues from a position that includes discarded tokens (visible output degradation: the model "sees" stale content), and with certain batch geometries (`-ub 1024` observed) the process crashes inside ggml-base.dll.

5. What does NOT help (all tested): removing `--reasoning-preserve`; `--cache-reuse 64`; `--ctx-checkpoints 4`; `--image-min-tokens 512` instead of 1024. `--cache-reuse` is explicitly disabled for mtmd prompts in server-context.cpp (`can_cache_reuse = ... && !slot.prompt.tokens.has_mtmd`), so it cannot apply here.

6. The same warning pattern appears in multimodal smoke-test logs of third-party projects (e.g. elizaOS plugin-local-inference verify JSONs: `find_slot: non-consecutive token position 4 after 3 ...`), which suggests the mtmd + recurrent path is generally affected, not specific to my setup. A llama.cpp-derivative build (beellama v11207) shows identical warnings with the same model.

7. Note on `llama-completion`: the issue lives in the server's slot/prompt-cache handling, so it cannot be re

items.title: Feature Request:  `--n-cpu-mode` FFN band selection for `--n-cpu-ffn`
items.author: John-194
items.body_excerpt:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description


This is a continuation of https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/26622. The PR was simple, this might be more complex. 

I would like to propose performance improvements for `--n-cpu-ffn` by automating `--override-tensor` band selection. It is possible to do this by hand, but this makes the process much easier. Currently `--n-cpu-ffn` selects sequentially from layer 0. 

My idea would be to create `--n-cpu-mode` with modes being:
* "largest" - pick layers with the largest FFNs;
* "top" - start from the top layer sequentially going down;
* "bottom" - current default, start from 0 sequentially;
* "smallest" - opposite of largest; 

"largest", "smallest", and "top" should exclude the MTP layer(s) (`nextn_predict_layers`): they return the least performance per byte. Anyone who wants the MTP layer on the CPU too could use mode "bottom" with a large N.

"largest" provides the most performance for me because the cost is per layer, not per byte. I would make it the default (instead of the current "bottom"), because at the same N it offloads more bytes, so existing setups would end up with some free VRAM while speed barely changes, which is harmless. Other options, like "smallest", might be useful for someone else using other quants.

I also tested `--n-cpu-moe` on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: its experts are all the same size, so `largest` does nothing there, but `top` gained ~3% with MTP on (average of prose and code). I don't know why, and the gain is small, so it doesn't matter much.

Most performance improvements happen when using MTP. All MTP runs used `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1`, because with MTP + CPU offload the CUDA graphs get re-captured every step (no measured speedup) and the recapture can OOM at a tight VRAM margin. Output is identical either way.

### Motivation

I created `--n-cpu-ffn` because driving `--override-tensor` needs more technical knowledge, thus it is not as widely used as a simplification like `--n-cpu-moe`. For those seeking the best performance out of their setup a `--n-cpu-mode` would help a lot by simplifying layer counting, which is unique to each quant.

**Here are some benchmarks showing the gains:**

MTP acceptance differs while generating prose and code. For simplicity I merged the two numbers:

```
MTP_tg = (prose_tg + code_tg) / 2
```

The speeds were tested at context prefill of 50k.

MTP costs VRAM, so the `-ot` band size differs when using it to keep a consistent VRAM usage amount. If you don't compensate for MTP's VRAM usage then the results are more exaggerated.

I tried to keep the CPU layer sizes similar between 'modes' and quants (that is why they have similar tg speeds).

Model: Qwen3.8-27B (Unsloth UD3 quants below).

HW: RTX 4070 Ti Super 16 GB; 32 GB DDR5; i5-13600KF;

Version: build 10280 (`0345d3a18`)

(The current `--n-cpu-ffn` implementation equates to using mode "bottom")

#### UD-Q4_K_S

**MTP on**

| --n-cpu-mode | --n-cpu-ffn | CPU FFN size | tg | pp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `largest` | 25 | 3847 MiB | **21.7** | 877.7 |
| `smallest` | 31 | 3873 MiB | 15.1 | 872.7 |
| `top` | 25 | 3791 MiB | 21.1 | 881.2 |
| `bottom` | 30 | 3796 MiB | 15.5 | 878.6 |

**MTP off**

| --n-cpu-mode | --n-cpu-ffn | CPU FFN size | tg | pp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `largest` | 17 | 2734 MiB | **15.8** | 999.2 |
| `smallest` | 23 | 2789 MiB | 13.9 | 987.8 |
| `top` | 18 | 2835 MiB | 15.4 | 986.1 |
| `bottom` | 23 | 2813 MiB | 13.7 | 985.0 |

#### UD-Q4_K_M

**MTP on**

| --n-cpu-mode | --n-cpu-ffn | CPU FFN size | tg | pp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `largest` | 23 | 3840 MiB | **21.7** | 878.4 |
| `smallest` | 29 | 3860 MiB | 18.7 | 876.4 |
| `top` | 24 | 3813 MiB | 21.7 | 877.1 |
| `bottom` | 28 | 3881 MiB | 18.9 | 869.8 |

**MTP off**

| --n-cpu-mode | --n-cpu-ffn  | CPU FFN size | tg | pp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `largest` | 16 | 2764 MiB | **15.5** | 992.6 |
| `smallest` | 21 | 2755 MiB | 15.1 | 995.8 |
| `top` | 17 | 2825 MiB | 15.2 | 983.4 |
| `bottom` | 21 | 2790 MiB | 14.9 | 986.4 |


#### UD-Q4_K_XL

**MTP on**

| --n-cpu-mode | --n-cpu-ffn | CPU FFN size | tg | pp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `largest` | 21 | 3806 MiB | **22.3** | 872.4 |
| `smallest` | 28 | 3878 MiB | 19.6 | 864.3 |
| `top` | 22 | 3806 MiB | 21.9 | 869.0 |
| `bottom` | 26 | 3793 MiB | 20.1 | 868.9 |

**MTP off**

| --n-cpu-mode | --n-cpu-ffn | CPU FFN size | tg | pp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `largest` | 15 | 2754 MiB | **15.2** | 983.8 |
| `smallest` | 21 | 2837 MiB | 14.9 | 973.8 |
| `top` | 15 | 2741 MiB | 15.1 | 980.7 |
| `bottom` | 20 | 2786 MiB | 14.9 | 977.4 |

#### Summary (both sides `largest`)

| model | MTP off tg | MTP on tg | MTP gain | `largest` vs current (MTP on) | `largest` vs current (MTP off) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| UD-Q4_K_S | 15.8 | 21.7 | +37% | +40% | +15% |
| UD-Q4_K_M | 15.5 | 21.7 | +40% | +15% | +4% |
| UD-Q4_K_XL | 15.2 | 22.3 | +47% | +11% | +2% |

`largest` wins all six tables, while `top` trails it closely. Though this is Unsloth UD3 specific; older UD2 quants had a different size profile.

Smaller bands prefill ~10-12% faster.

### Possible Implementation

* "largest" and "smallest" need per-layer FFN sizes, but the offload args are resolved before the model is loaded. Where should this live?
* Is `--n-cpu-mode` a good name, and are the four modes OK?
* Can "largest" become the default?
* Should this also apply to `--n-cpu-moe`?

items.title: server: recurrent/hybrid seq_rm partial-rollback (n_rs_seq) unreachable outside speculative decoding — crash or unbounded memory growth
items.author: jaczagi
items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

For recurrent/hybrid-memory architectures that support state rollback (e.g. `LLM_ARCH_QWEN4EXP`, per `llm_arch_supports_rs_rollback()` in `src/llama-arch.cpp`), the rollback mechanism (`n_rs_seq`, checked in `llama_memory_recurrent::seq_rm()`) is only ever populated by `common_params_speculative::need_n_rs_seq()` (`common/common.h`), which returns a nonzero value **only** when `--spec-type` is one of `draft-mtp` / `draft-eagle3` / `draft-dflash` / `draft-dspark`.

In ordinary `llama-server` usage without speculative decoding (the common case for a hybrid/recurrent model serving multi-turn chat), `n_rs_seq` is always `0`. This means:

```cpp
// src/llama-memory-recurrent.cpp, seq_rm()
if (0 < p0 && p0 <= cell.pos && p1 > cell.pos) {
    const llama_pos rollback = cell.pos - (p0 - 1);
    const bool pending = rs_idx[seq_id] != 0;
    if (!pending && rollback >= 1 && rollback <= (llama_pos) n_rs_seq) {
        ...
        return true;
    }
    return false;  // <-- always hit when n_rs_seq == 0
}
```

`seq_rm()` cleanly returns `false` whenever a caller asks for a partial trim (`p0 > 0`) on one of these architectures with no speculative decoding enabled — which is exactly what happens whenever the server's prompt-cache reuse ("LCP similarity" prefix matching in `tools/server`) finds a partial prefix match and tries to trim the KV/recurrent state back to a shared prefix instead of reprocessing the whole prompt.

## Impact

1. The server's prompt-cache-reuse path in `tools/server/server-context.cpp` does not check the return value of this particular `llama_memory_seq_rm()` call before proceeding as if the trim had succeeded. Since it silently returns `false` for these architectures, `n_past` bookkeeping goes out of sync with the actual recurrent/SSM state, and the next decode step reads/writes out of bounds, producing a hard GPU fault:
   ```
   Memory access fault by GPU node-X ... Reason: Page not present or supervisor privilege.
   ```
   Reproducible on the second request that shares a prefix with a previous one (any multi-turn conversation, or even two back-to-back identical requests), with `--cache-prompt` on (default) and `--spec-type none`.

2. A local workaround (checking the return value and forcing `n_past = 0` / full reprocess whenever the partial trim fails) avoids the crash, but every such forced full reprocess appears to leave a small, non-recovering amount of device memory allocated (a few MB per occurrence, observed consistently across all devices in a multi-GPU tensor-split setup). This accumulates over a long multi-turn conversation — since essentially every turn hits this same "partial trim requested, always fails, force full reprocess" path — until the available device memory margin on the tightest device is exhausted, at which point generation degrades to 1-5 tokens per response for the remainder of the session. Confirmed via repeated *identical, fixed-size, independent* requests (no growing context at all) that per-request device memory usage decreases monotonically and plateaus exactly at the point generation starts degrading — which rules out KV-cache/context-size growth or the server's context-checkpoint mechanism (`--ctx-checkpoints`) as the cause.

## Suggested fix directions

- At minimum, guard the general (non-speculative) partial-trim call path in `tools/server/server-context.cpp` the same way the speculative-decoding path already does: check the return value of `llama_memory_seq_rm()` and force a full reprocess when it fails, instead of assuming success. This would at least turn the crash into the (already observed) degraded-but-non-fatal behavior.
- Longer-term: wire `n_rs_seq` for the general server "prompt cache reuse" case too, not only via `common_params_speculative::need_n_rs_seq()`, so architectures that support rollback (per `llm_arch_supports_rs_rollback()`) can use genuine partial rollback outside of speculative decoding, avoiding the repeated full-reprocess + memory-growth pattern entirely.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Serve a GGUF model whose architecture is in `llm_arch_supports_rs_rollback()` (e.g. qwen4exp / Qwen3.8-Flash-Next family) with `llama-server`, `--spec-type none`, default `--cache-prompt`.
2. Send two `/v1/chat/completions` (or `/completion`) requests where the second shares a prefix with the first (e.g. same system+user message, or a growing multi-turn conversation).
3. Without any patch: the second request that hits a partial-prefix cache match crashes the server with a GPU memory access fault.
4. With a patch that checks the `seq_rm()` return value and forces a full reprocess on failure: the crash is avoided, but repeating step 2 many times (even with a constant-size, non-growing prompt) shows device memory usage decreasing monotonically per request, eventually causing generation to degrade to a handful of tokens per response.

## Environment

- llama.cpp build 522 / commit `4d91760` (tag `b10818`), 2026-09-05
- Backend: HIP (ROCm), multi-GPU tensor-split
- Architecture: `qwen4exp` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next family), `--spec-type none`, `--cache-prompt` default (enabled)

items.title: [RFC]: [Store] Split snapshot orchestration and serialization logic from MasterService
items.author: Aionw
items.body_excerpt:
## Motivation

Snapshot is not part of the core master data path. Conceptually, it is a persistence and recovery capability that observes, captures, and restores master state, and should be modeled as a separate subsystem rather than intrinsic master request-processing logic.

Keeping snapshot orchestration and serialization inside `MasterService` blurs this abstraction boundary. It also makes snapshot format evolution difficult, since part of the snapshot serialization logic is implemented as a private nested component of `MasterService`.

This RFC proposes splitting snapshot orchestration and snapshot state serialization into dedicated components while preserving the current snapshot behavior and runtime semantics.

## Proposed Changes

### 1. Move snapshot orchestration out of `MasterService`

Introduce a dedicated snapshot manager module, for example:

- `ha/snapshot/master_snapshot_manager.h`
- `ha/snapshot/master_snapshot_manager.cpp`

This component will own snapshot-specific orchestration:

- periodic snapshot scheduling
- snapshot ID generation
- snapshot descriptor construction
- child process lifecycle management
- timeout handling
- snapshot payload upload
- catalog publish
- retention cleanup
- snapshot metrics updates

`MasterService` should only provide the state capture/restore hooks needed by the snapshot manager.

### 2. Extract snapshot state serialization from `MasterService`

Move master snapshot state serialization into standalone modules instead of keeping part of the snapshot format inside `MasterService`.

The current snapshot payload is composed of multiple state files:

- `metadata`: object metadata shards, discarded replicas, and replica ID state
- `segments`: mounted memory segments, client-to-segment mappings, allocator ordering, and local disk segment/offloading state
- `task_manager`: persisted client task manager state
- `manifest.txt`: snapshot serializer type, version, and snapshot ID

The refactor should model these as one master snapshot state bundle, with dedicated serializers for each sub-state. `MasterService` should remain responsible for owning live runtime state, while the snapshot serialization layer should own the persisted representation and format compatibility.

### 3. Define explicit snapshot data structures

Introduce explicit snapshot DTOs for the full master snapshot state, such as:

- metadata snapshot state
- segment manager snapshot state
- task manager snapshot state
- snapshot manifest metadata

These structures should represent the persisted snapshot format independently from the internal layout of `MasterService`, `SegmentManager`, and `ClientTaskManager`.

This will make future snapshot format evolution easier and reduce accidental coupling to private master internals.

### 4. Keep restore behavior unchanged

Restore should continue to support the current snapshot storage layout and manifest validation behavior.

The proposed refactor should only move restore selection, download, decoding, and application logic into clearer components. The externally visible behavior should remain unchanged.

A possible split is:

- snapshot repository: list, download, upload, publish, cleanup
- snapshot codec: encode/decode snapshot payloads
- master state restorer: apply decoded snapshot data to `MasterService`

### 5. Preserve existing configuration and compatibility

Existing snapshot flags and environment variables should continue to work:

- `--enable_snapshot`
- `--snapshot_interval_seconds`
- `--snapshot_child_timeout_seconds`
- `--snapshot_retention_count`
- `--snapshot_object_store_type`
- `--snapshot_catalog_store_type`
- `--snapshot_catalog_store_connstring`
- `--snapshot_backup_dir`
- `--enable_snapshot_restore`
- `MOONCAKE_SNAPSHOT_LOCAL_PATH`

Existing snapshots should remain restorable unless a later RFC explicitly proposes a format migration.

## Expected Benefits

- Clearer abstraction boundary between core master request-processing logic and snapshot persistence/recovery logic
- Smaller and easier-to-review `MasterService`
- Clear ownership boundary for snapshot code
- Easier snapshot format testing across metadata, segment, and task-manager payloads
- Easier restore testing without constructing a full master lifecycle
- Reduced reliance on private nested classes and test-only friendships
- Lower risk when adding new fields to snapshot format

## Non-goals

This RFC does not propose changing the snapshot consistency model.

This RFC does not propose changing the current HA design.

This RFC does not propose changing snapshot storage backends or catalog semantics.

This RFC does not propose changing user-facing configuration.

## Testing Plan

Add or update unit tests for:

- full snapshot state encode/decode round trip
- metadata snapshot encode/decode compatibility
- segment snapshot encode/decode compatibility
- task manager snapshot encode/decode compatibility
- snapshot manager descriptor construction
- snapshot manager publish/cleanup behavior
- restore fallback across multiple candidate snapshots
- restore failure handling and state reset

Keep existing snapshot integration tests passing, including:

- master snapshot/restore tests
- SSD snapshot tests
- promotion snapshot tests
- catalog-backed snapshot provider tests
- snapshot child process tests

## Migration Plan

1. Introduce standalone snapshot manager and serializer modules.
2. Move code from `MasterService` into the new modules without behavior changes.
3. Replace direct private serializer usage with explicit state capture/restore hooks.
4. Keep existing tests passing after each step.
5. Remove obsolete private nested serializer definitions and unnecessary test friendships once callers are migrated.

items.title: [RFC]: DrainJob bandwidth rate limiting
items.author: liangxu2000
items.body_excerpt:
### Changes proposed

### Changes proposed

## 1. Current State: DrainJob Performance Parameters

After reading through the `mooncake-store` source, here are the existing control parameters related to DrainJob:

| Parameter | Location | Default | Purpose |
|-----------|----------|---------|---------|
| `max_concurrency` | `CreateDrainJobRequest` | 4 | Max concurrent MoveTasks per DrainJob |
| `task_thread_pool_` | Client constructor | 4 | Client-side task execution thread pool |
| `kJobDispatchThreadSleepMs` | Master dispatch loop | 500ms | Master DrainJob scheduling interval |
| TaskPollThreadMain interval | Client poll loop | 1000ms | Client task fetch interval |
| `kTaskBatchSize` | Client poll loop | 16 | Max tasks per `FetchTasks` RPC |
| `kMaxDrainUnitRetries` | Master drain logic | 3 | Max retries per key move |

**All existing controls operate on the "count" dimension. There is zero rate/bandwidth limiting.**

Key observations from the transfer path:

- In `ExecuteReplicaTransfer`, the entire object is `split_into_slices` and submitted to Transfer Engine in a single batch via `submitTransfer`. No pacing between slices.
- Drain MoveTasks share the same RDMA link and client thread pool as regular read/write operations. No priority isolation.
- A single object can be several GB. With `max_concurrency=4`, tens of GB could be in-flight on the RDMA link simultaneously.

## 2. Discussion Topic

Does the community see a need for DrainJob bandwidth/rate limiting? Are there any existing plans?

From a usage perspective, an aggressive DrainJob could saturate shared RDMA bandwidth and impact read latency for online workloads. I'd like to understand:

- Has anyone encountered this as a pain point in production?
- Any thoughts on the design direction from the community?

## 3. Possible Directions (high-level)

- **Master-side**: Track recent throughput via a sliding window (e.g., 5s) over completed task byte counts. Skip scheduling new MoveTasks when the current rate meets the configured limit. Leverages the existing 500ms dispatch loop as a natural pacing mechanism.
- **Client-side**: Split large object transfers into sub-batches (e.g., 64MB each). Insert a token bucket between sub-batches for precise pacing.
- **API**: Add an optional `bandwidth_limit_mbps` field to `CreateDrainJobRequest` (0 = unlimited, backward compatible).

The concrete design choice — single-layer vs. dual-layer, where to place it, whether to go adaptive — depends on real community needs. This RFC is intended to start that discussion.
