items.title: TunableOp wildcard fallback returns wrong mm results when a split-K cuBLASLt solution is reused at a different shape
items.author: aorenste
items.body_excerpt:
I was looking into why `test_dynamic_tunable_ops.py` keeps failing in periodic despite being disabled, and it turned out to be a real wrong-results bug rather than a flake. I had an AI assistant (Claude) do the investigation and draft the writeup below; I've reviewed it and reproduced the failure locally.

> **Summary**
>
> When TunableOp tuning selects a split-K cuBLASLt solution at the tuned shape, reusing that solution through the wildcard fallback (`torch.cuda.tunable.wildcard_fallback_enable(True)`) at a different M/N/K silently produces incorrect `mm` results. This is the root cause of the "flaky" `LayoutCoverageWildcardTest` failures tracked by the bot-filed disable issues:
>
> - #194899 `test_layout_TN_dynamic_k`
> - #194900 `test_layout_TT_dynamic_k`
> - #196405 `test_layout_TT_dynamic_n`
> - #196670 `test_layout_TT`
>
> **Evidence**
>
> Running `LayoutCoverageWildcardTest.test_layout_TT` (bf16, tuned shape `tt_257_53_251`, runtime shape `tt_257_65_251`, dispatched via wildcard `tt_257_*_251`) with `PYTORCH_TUNABLEOP_VERBOSE=3`:
>
> | Winner at tuned shape | Result via wildcard at runtime shape |
> |---|---|
> | `Gemm_Cublaslt_id_24_tile_11_stages_7_splitk_3_red_4_swizzle_0_custom_0_inner_0_cluster_0` | wrong |
> | `Gemm_Cublaslt_id_24_tile_15_stages_0_splitk_3_red_4_swizzle_0_custom_0_inner_0_cluster_0` | wrong |
> | `Default` | correct |
>
> Every failing run gives a bit-identical wrong output (739 / 16705 elements mismatched, max abs diff 0.125, same index each time), so it is deterministic given the chosen solution, not tolerance noise. Pass/fail across runs depends only on which of the 6 candidates benchmarks fastest, which is why CI history looks flaky and does not bisect to any commit. Locally (A100-class GPU, CUDA 13.0) the TT layout tests fail in roughly 12/80 runs. In CI, the same `AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close! ... wildcard-fallback dispatch output must match tunable-disabled reference` appears across the cuda13.0/13.2/13.4 periodic, trunk, and slow configs, going back at least to 2026-09-25.
>
> Hypothesis (not yet confirmed by reading the dispatch code): the wildcard fallback replays the tuned cuBLASLt algo at the new shape without re-validating it (e.g. `cublasLtMatmulAlgoCheck`, or split-K / workspace requirements that depend on the problem size).
>
> **Repro**
>
> ```
> for i in $(seq 15); do
>   PYTORCH_TUNABLEOP_VERBOSE=3 python test/inductor/test_dynamic_tunable_ops.py LayoutCoverageWildcardTest.test_layout_TT
> done
> ```
>
> Failing runs show a `splitk_` solution on the "found fastest for GemmTunableOp_BFloat16_TT(...)" line.
>
> **Why the disable issues didn't stop the failures**
>
> Every test class in `test_dynamic_tunable_ops.py` overrides `setUp()` without calling `super().setUp()`, so `common_utils.TestCase.setUp()` → `check_if_enable()` never ran and the disables above were no-ops (the disable bot has been commenting "disable bot might be broken" on them for weeks). A fix for that is in progress; once it lands the tests will be skipped, which hides this bug, so this issue tracks the actual fix.
>
> cc @csarofeen @ptrblck @eqy @nWEIdia @adelesun (author of the wildcard-fallback series #191658 / #192144)

items.title: [Testing] Triage of red tests that still need a fix (90-day sweep)
items.author: bolubo
items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

A 90 day sweep of the Actions history (2026-06-26 to 2026-09-25) turned up 455 failed runs. Most of them are already fixed, tied to a PR branch that was still iterating, or environmental. This issue is about what is left: tests that are still going red and do not have a fix, with enough evidence attached that someone can pick one up without redoing the whole investigation.

Two of the items reproduce locally on main today (A). Four more keep showing up in CI across branches, where the mechanism is narrowed down but there is no local repro yet (B). The appendices cover the one-off flakes and the families that are already fixed, so nobody has to dig through them again.

The coverage side already has tracking issues (#2637, #2708, #2737); this list is a different axis, tests that are failing right now.

If you want to take one, please comment on the item first so two people do not end up on the same thing, and link the PR here when it is up. Small focused PRs are the easiest to review.

## Items

- [ ] A1. Gateway rate limiter windows follow the wall clock, and three tests flake on the bucket boundary.
- [ ] A2. Two tests have been skipped since April 2025, and both pass when re-enabled.
- [ ] B1. The SLO queue spec times out on the release path.
- [ ] B2. The RoleSet topology spec hits a 409 conflict.
- [ ] B3. Batch e2e: a restored job does not reach `completed` within the 60s budget.
- [ ] B4. The planner unit test hangs and trips the 10 minute package timeout.

Grading:

- A: reproduced locally on main (`544204ae`), with a measured failure rate over repeated runs.
- B: repeated red in CI on main or across branches; no local repro yet.
- Watch: seen once; kept for reference.
- Fixed: already covered by a merged PR; do not re-triage.

## A. Reproduced locally on main

### A1. Gateway rate limiter windows follow the wall clock

`pkg/plugins/gateway/ratelimiter/redis.go:77` builds the counter key as `name:key:<unix/window % 64>`, so the counter changes on wall-clock bucket boundaries. A pair of calls that should share one window can land in two buckets instead, and the second call gets a fresh counter and is admitted. The TTL side is already anchored to the first write (`incrAndExpireScript`), so the key rotation is the remaining race.

- Affected tests: `pkg/plugins/gateway/replica_rps_test.go:96` (`TestModelReplicaRPS_Half_AllowsOneRequestEveryTwoSeconds`), `pkg/plugins/gateway/replica_inflight_test.go:335` (`TestHandleRequestBody_ReplicaInflightCoexistsWithReplicaRPS`), and `pkg/plugins/gateway/gateway_ratelimit_test.go:270` (`TestEnforceModelRPS_RejectDoesNotPostponeNextWindow`, added with #2726).
- How often it fails on main (one process per run, `-count=1`): 3 red in 100 runs for the first pair, 14 red in 450 runs for the third test, so roughly one run in thirty. The failure messages are "a second request within the same 2s window should be rejected" and "immediate retry should be rejected by the still-open window".
- CI hit: [run 35654425095, job 106514390571](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/actions/runs/35654425095/job/106514390571), Go Race Tests on 09-21, same assertion at `gateway_ratelimit_test.go:270`.
- Repro: `for i in $(seq 1 50); do go test ./pkg/plugins/gateway -run 'TestModelReplicaRPS_Half_AllowsOneRequestEveryTwoSeconds|TestHandleRequestBody_ReplicaInflightCoexistsWithReplicaRPS' -count=1; done`
- Two ways to fix it, and this is a real tradeoff: (1) anchor the window at the first write so every call in the same window computes the same key, which is what the tests already assume, at the cost of changing behavior at bucket boundaries; or (2) keep the wall-clock bucket and make the tests independent of it by injecting the clock, which is a smaller change but leaves the boundary burst in the product.

### A2. Two tests skipped since April 2025

- `pkg/utils/prefixcacheindexer/tree_test.go:33` (`Test_LPRadixCacheE2E`) and `:71` (`Test_RadixMatchPrefix`) have carried `t.SkipNow()` since `d546795a` (#933, April 2025). Removing the two lines makes both pass locally, in under 0.1s including subtests.
- `apps/console/api/resource_manager/provider/kubernetes/catalog_test.go:33` skips unconditionally with `t.Skip("skip for now")`, which also makes the kubeconfig checks below it dead code. Either delete the line or gate it on the environment with a stated reason.
- Repro: `go test ./pkg/utils/prefixcacheindexer -run 'Test_LPRadixCacheE2E|Test_RadixMatchPrefix' -v`

## B. Repeated red in CI, no local repro yet

### B1. SLO queue spec times out on the release path

- `pkg/plugins/gateway/algorithms/slo_test.go:253` ("Queue router should be blocked and released successfully") fails with `context deadline exceeded` at `:270`, after the 10s per spec budget.
- Hits since June: 06-28 `exclusive_topology`, 08-17 `route-dev` and `feat/align-job-time-window`, 09-05 `ui-aiconfigurator`, 09-09 `feat-pd-hybrid-cache-load`, 09-12 `roshpr/feat-stormservice-pooled-scale`, 09-20 `andreafeat/disable-gateway-rate-limiting` (race job). #2335 reported this spec in June and was closed after #2328 and #2353 merged, but it still recurs.
- A 150 run local loop is green, so it needs a CI style repro first. Fixing it likely means either making the assertion event driven or making the fixed wait budget explicit and generous.

### B2. RoleSet topology spec hits a 409 conflict

- `test/integration/controller/roleset_test.go:1062` ("applies topology policy updates only to newly created pods") fails at `:1118` with `Operation cannot be fulfilled on rolesets... the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again`. Latest hit: [35814726502](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/actions/runs/35814726502) on main, 09-23, 89 of 90 specs passed. Two more on 08-04.
- The spec updates the RoleSet while a reconcile is in flight, so `retry.RetryOnConflict` around the update (or `Eventually`) should close the race. Test side, no product change expected.

items.title: [Testing] Triage of tests that never run: disabled specs and suites that no CI job compiles
items.author: bolubo

## Summary

A read-only sweep of the tree at `4be9a600` (2026-09-27) looked for tests that cannot protect anything because they never execute. One family is disabled in place, some of it for two years. Another sits behind build tags that no test job passes, so its suites never run. A third family quietly skips itself on CI hosts.

This is a different axis from #2805, which tracks tests that are going red right now. A skipped test cannot go red, which is how these stayed invisible. One overlap (the console catalog skip, already named in #2805 A2) is listed in the appendix instead of repeated as an item.

The sweep grepped for skip markers across the Go and Python trees and cross-referenced every test file behind a build tag against every workflow under `.github/workflows`. Line numbers are against `4be9a600`.

If you want to take one, please comment on the item first so two people do not end up on the same thing, and link the PR here when it is up. Small focused PRs are the easiest to review.

## Items

- [ ] A1. The oldest in-place skip: the rayclusterfleet reconcile spec, skipped since 2024-09.
- [ ] A2. Roleset and StormService scaffold specs skip themselves in `BeforeEach` (2025-06).
- [ ] A3. ModelAdapter controller suite: all 18 specs parked behind `XDescribe` (2025-08).
- [ ] A4. OpenAI compatibility e2e: `TestCompletionStreaming` carries a bare fix-me TODO with no explanation (2025-10).
- [ ] A5. Two kvcache Python files skip at import time with no reason string (2025).
- [ ] A6. One storage factory test skips because a network probe is treated as flaky (2026-06).
- [ ] B1. `-tags zmq` test suites (9 files, 48 test functions) are run by no CI job (needs a wiring decision).
- [ ] B2. `-tags integration` tests under `pkg/controller` have no runner (needs a decision on where they belong).
- [ ] C1. Three rate limiter tests skip themselves in CI because no Redis is listening.

Grading:

- A: the skip is unconditional in the source; the fix is to re-enable and repair, or remove.
- B: no CI entry compiles the tag; the fix needs a wiring decision first.
- C: the test runs but skips itself under CI conditions; a green run hides it.

## A. Disabled in place

### A1. rayclusterfleet: the oldest skip

`pkg/controller/rayclusterfleet/rayclusterfleet_controller_test.go:112` is the only spec of its suite, and it skips under a deferral note that waits for the integration test to land:

- Verify: `go test ./pkg/controller/rayclusterfleet/... -v` (the suite uses envtest, so run it via `make test` or with `KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS`).

### A2. Roleset and StormService scaffold specs

`pkg/controller/roleset/roleset_controller_test.go:45` and `pkg/controller/stormservice/stormservice_controller_test.go:45` both skip inside `BeforeEach` with `Skip("skip this test and revisit once main logic is implemented")`. Both skips came in `8fd23efa` (#1226, 2025-06-25) and were never revisited. Each file has exactly one spec, so the skip takes the whole suite to zero.

- Acceptance: the specs pass against the current controllers, or the scaffold specs are deleted so the suites are empty on purpose.
- Verify: `go test ./pkg/controller/roleset/... ./pkg/controller/stormservice/... -v`.
- Size: S; both files share one origin, so one PR can carry both.

### A3. ModelAdapter: 18 specs behind XDescribe

`pkg/controller/modeladapter/modeladapter_controller_test.go:37` disables the whole suite with `var _ = XDescribe("ModelAdapter Controller", func() {`, under the comment "Disable Ginkgo tests that require Kubernetes environment". A separate integration suite lives at `test/integration/controller/modeladapter_test.go`.

`test/e2e/gateway/api/openai_api_compatibility_test.go:29` holds 18 tests, and line 30 skips the first one with a bare fix-me TODO and no explanation. The file was added with that skip in `af635f2b` (#1678, 2025-10-18) and moved to the new layout in `fe7db93e` (#2676, 2026-09-07). items.title: [RFC]: Unified Artifact I/O for Model Weights, KV Cache, and RL Checkpoints
items.author: cursor
items.body_excerpt:
## Motivation Mooncake Store already supports in-cluster tensor storage and high-bandwidth weight distribution (Transfer Engine, P2P Store, checkpoint-engine). However, **loading artifacts from external sources** is fragmented today: | Source | Status on `main` | |--------|------------------| | **Local safetensors** | Partial — `load_tensor_from_safetensor` / `save_tensor_to_safetensor` (local paths only, C++ binding) | | **S3** | Not for weights — S3 exists only for master HA snapshot storage (`S3SnapshotObjectStore`) | | **OSS (Alibaba Cloud)** | Not supported | | **Hugging Face Hub** | Not supported — HF appears only in downstream integration docs (vLLM/SGLang model download) | Use cases that need a unified path: 1. **LLM serving cold start** — load model weights from S3/OSS/HF into Mooncake Store, then RDMA-distribute to inference nodes. 2. **KV cache persistence** — save/load prefill KV tensors to remote object storage for HiCache L3 or cross-session reuse. 3. **RL checkpoint handoff** — persist training weights to object storage and load into rollout engines (complements existing P2P hot-path sync). A prototype exists on branch `feature/kv-cache-file-persistence` (`store_file_io.py` + design docs). This RFC proposes merging and extending that work into a stable, documented API. --- ## Goals 1. **Unified read/write API** for KV cache, RL checkpoints, and model weights with consistent parameters. 2. **Multi-backend paths** via a single `save_path` / `load_path` parameter: - Local: `/data/ckpt/`, `file:///data/ckpt/` - S3: `s3://bucket/prefix/` - OSS: `oss://bucket/prefix/` (via `ossfs` / fsspec) - Hugging Face Hub: `hf://org/repo/path/` (via `huggingface_hub`) 3. **Format support**: `safetensors` (default/recommended), `torch` (`.pt`/`.pth`, `weights_only=True` by default). 4. **Tensor-parallel sharding**: `tp_rank` / `tp_size` for multi-file layouts (`manifest.json` + `rank_00000.safetensors`, ...). 5. **Backward compatibility** with existing `load_tensor_from_safetensor` / `save_tensor_to_safetensor` (local C++ path). 6. **Optional P2P hot path** after cold load — integrate with P2P Store / checkpoint-engine for cluster-wide distribution. ## Non-Goals (initial phase) - Replacing Hugging Face `from_pretrained()` inside vLLM/SGLang — Mooncake provides storage/transfer, not model class instantiation. - Full `WeightManager` with automatic `model.load_state_dict()` — callers remain responsible for applying loaded tensors. - OSS/HF authentication policy beyond `storage_options` passthrough. --- ## Current State ### `main` — local safetensors only ```python store.load_tensor_from_safetensor("weights/key", "/local/path/model.safetensors") # → safetensors.torch.load_file → put_tensor → available for RDMA get ``` Implemented in `mooncake-integration/store/store_py.cpp`; tested in `mooncake-wheel/tests/test_safetensor_functions.py`. ### Prototype (`feature/kv-cache-file-persistence`) `mooncake-wheel/mooncake/store_file_io.py` monkey-patches `MooncakeDistributedStore` at import: - `save_tensor_to_file` / `load_tensor_from_file` — fsspec-backed, `torch` + `safetensors` - `save_kv_cache_to_file` / `load_kv_cache_from_file` — aliases - Upgraded `save_tensor_from_safetensor` / `load_tensor_from_safetensor` — delegate to fsspec layer Tested: local paths, `file://` URIs, `.pt` and `.safetensors`. **Not tested**: `s3://`, `oss://`, `hf://`. Design docs (prototype branch, commit `ca9100d8`): - `docs/source/design/usage_unified_artifact_io.md` - `docs/source/design/usage_model_weights.md` - `docs/source/design/usage_kvcache.md` --- ## Proposed Design ### 1. Unified API (Python) ```python from typing import Any, Dict, Literal, Optional ArtifactKind = Literal["kv_cache", "rl_checkpoint", "model_weights"] class MooncakeArtifactIO: """Facade over MooncakeDistributedStore; optional separate class or mixin.""" def save_artifact( self, kind: ArtifactKind, name: str, obj: Any, # dict[str, Tensor] | Tensor | bytes manifest save_path: str, *, format: str = "auto", # auto | safetensors | torch storage_options: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, tp_rank: Optional[int] = None, tp_size: int = 1, use_p2p: str = "auto", # auto | true | false ) -> Dict[str, Any]: ... def load_artifact( self, kind: ArtifactKind, name: str, load_path: str, *, format: str = "auto", storage_options: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, map_location: str = "cpu", weights_only: bool = True, # torch format only tp_rank: Optional[int] = None, tp_size: int = 1, use_p2p: str = "auto", ) -> Any: ... ``` ### 2. items.title: [Roadmap]Fast Engine Recovery: Weight Cache Daemon
items.author: liusy58
items.body_excerpt:
# [Roadmap] Fast Engine Recovery: Weight Cache Daemon 
@liusy58 @QiuMike @alexnails 
Phase 1 landed in #27139 — a per-rank daemon holds post-quantized weights and serves them over CUDA IPC; weight load drops from ~306–327s to <1s on Qwen3-235B FP8 ([blog](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-08-21-sglang-fast-recovery)). This issue tracks the next steps. Contributions and feedback are welcome.

Related: #27052 (Fast Recovery framework), #27310 (GPU Memory Service / VMM)

Goals: <10s cold restart and <1s warm standby switch; broaden model & quant coverage; make the cache outlive the daemon; make resident weights usable beyond the one GPU they sit on.

Where Phase 1 stands: TP + PP, single-node and multi-node launch (each node spawns its share of ranks and joins one dist group), zero-copy IPC per GPU, unquantized + block-wise FP8. Not yet: cross-node daemon coordination / failover, DP & EP shard keying, spec-decoding draft models, weight update / sleep-wake, cache surviving daemon death.

## Model & quantization coverage

- [ ] parity harness — disk-load vs daemon-load `state_dict` diff (names / shape / dtype / stride / byte hash) + short GSM8K gate; required evidence for every new allowlist entry
- [ ] carry post-processing metadata in the manifest (final shape/stride, layout tag, whitelisted module attrs) instead of reproducing `process_weights_after_loading` on a meta-init model — this is what blocks most quant methods today
- [ ] quant methods: per-tensor fp8 / w8a8 int8 / mxfp8 / nvfp4 / compressed-tensors / awq / gptq-marlin #32398 
- [ ] archs: MoE (DeepSeek V3/V4, Ling, Kimi K3) / hybrid linear attention / multimodal (vision tower + projector) / LoRA base weights https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33684
- [ ] MTP & EAGLE draft models (per-rank draft daemon), removing the `--speculative-algorithm` rejection in `server_args.py` #32744
- [ ] generic post-map rebuild hook to replace the hardcoded `_rebuild_stale_views`; make tied storages, param→buffer flips and non-persistent buffers explicit in the manifest
- [ ] publish the support matrix in docs; unsupported combinations keep hard-erroring (no silent wrong numerics)

## Transport: CUDA VMM shareable handles (#27310 §4.2)



- [ ] `vmm_fd` backend (skeleton already in `weight_cache/transport.py`): `cuMemCreate` + FD handles over `SCM_RIGHTS`, VA reservation on import, `torch_ipc` stays the fallback, `--weight-cache-transport {auto,torch_ipc,vmm_fd}` #33279
- [ ] `mooncake` backend https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36293


## Weight update without reload

- [ ] epoch handoff on stable VAs: readers unmap → writer commits → readers remap at the same VAs, so captured CUDA graphs stay valid
- [ ] daemon as the weight delivery agent for trainer pushes (NCCL/RDMA); un-gate the `update_weights_*` rejections in `weight_updater.py`
- [ ] colocated RL: engine itself takes the writer role, same protocol, no daemon in the loop

## Multi-instance & cross-GPU sharing

- [ ] key the cache by physical GPU UUID + config fingerprint (plus optional `--weight-cache-namespace`) under a configurable runtime dir. Today the socket is `/tmp/sglang_weight_cache_rank{global_rank}.sock`, so 2× tp=4 on one 8-GPU node collide and rank 0 of the second instance attaches to the GPU 0 daemon
- [ ] discovery: replace static socket paths with a lightweight registry (file-based dir, optionally etcd) so an engine rank selects a daemon by `CacheConfig` match rather than by process rank, and locates daemons across nodes without a manual `--weight-cache-socket`
- [ ] `--weight-cache-peer-copy` — when no daemon holds the shard on the local GPU, `cudaMemcpyPeerAsync` it from a peer-GPU daemon (NVLink-domain check, chunked on a low-priority stream, bandwidth cap so a serving neighbour is not disturbed). 1× memory per instance, sub-second over NVLink vs ~300s from disk
- [ ] preference order local zero-copy > peer copy > disk, reported per rank
- [ ] fleet fill: a daemon fills itself from a peer daemon instead of disk (P2P on-node, NCCL/RDMA cross-node), so a fleet cold start pays one disk read per shard group — the real bottleneck for 1T+ models on shared FS; align with the checkpoint-engine broadcast path
- [ ] out of scope for now: resharding across TP/EP topologies (tp=4 daemon → tp=8 engine)

## Multi-node, DP & EP

- [ ] primary–secondary daemon coordination for multi-node TP (e.g. TP=16 = 2 nodes × 8 GPUs): primary orchestrates daemon startup, cross-node NCCL process-group formation and readiness signalling; secondaries load their local shards in parallel and serve IPC handles to engines on their own node. Basic multi-node launch already works via `--nnodes/--node-rank/--dist-init-method`; what is missing is the cluster state machine
- [ ] cross-node daemon lifecycle: primary tracks which secondaries are alive, triggers coordinated restarts, signals engines on a dead secondary's node to fall back to disk; promote a secondary when the primary dies
- [ ] DP support: every DP rank on a GPU maps the same daemon's handles, so a model is read from disk and quantized exactly once per GPU regardless of DP degree (today each DP rank disk-loads independently). This is about supporting SGLang's DP deployment model, not cross-GPU sharing
- [ ] EP support: expert shards differ per EP rank, so cache and key them by `ep_rank`; handle partial expert loading when a rank owns a subset of experts
- [ ] `CacheConfig`: add `ep_rank`, `dp_rank` and `node_rank` for correct shard identification under EP and multi-node (`dp_size`/`ep_size` are already there)

## Ops & reliability

- [ ] `daemon status` command + Prometheus metrics (resident bytes, attached clients, load time, hit / mismatch / fallback), and an engine endpoint reporting how each rank got its weights
- [ ] runtime dir with owner-only permissions + `SO_PEERCRED` check before handing out handles (no world-writable `/tmp` sockets)
- [ ] `protocol_version` in the handshake with a documented skew policy (the env stamp alrea

items.title: [Gateway] Reject PD routing for unsupported inference endpoints
items.author: googs1025
items.body_excerpt:
Parent issue: #2989

## Problem

The Gateway validates whether a routing strategy is recognized, but not whether it is compatible with the request endpoint.

The PD router mutates generation-specific fields such as `max_tokens`, `max_completion_tokens`, `stream`, `stream_options`, and `min_tokens`. Applying this transformation to embedding, ranking, scoring, multimodal, or engine utility endpoints can create invalid requests or undefined behavior.

## Supported PD endpoints

Initially permit PD only for:

- `/v1/chat/completions`
- `/v1/completions`

Reject PD for every other endpoint, including Responses, Messages, Embeddings, Rerank, Classify, Decisions, SystemOne, Score, image/video/audio APIs, Tokenize, and Pooling.

Responses and Messages may be enabled later after dedicated PD compatibility tests exist.

## Proposed behavior

Add a small focused compatibility check, for example:

```go
func validateRoutingStrategyForPath(
    requestPath string,
    strategy types.RoutingAlgorithm,
) error
```

A switch or allowlist is sufficient. Do not introduce an endpoint registry.

For an unsupported endpoint, return `400 Bad Request` with an OpenAI-compatible error:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "routing strategy 'pd' is not supported for endpoint '/v1/score'",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": "unsupported_routing_strategy"
  }
}
```

Do not silently fall back to another router.

## Validation order

Run the check:

1. after removing the query string from the path;
2. after resolving header, model-profile, and environment routing configuration;
3. after effective multi-strategy resolution when it resolves to PD;
4. before model RPS accounting;
5. before Pod selection;
6. before replica in-flight accounting;
7. before any prefill request.

## Testing

Cover:

- Chat Completions and Completions with PD: accepted.
- Responses and Messages with PD: rejected.
- Other supported endpoints with PD: rejected.
- Query-string variants.
- PD selected by request header or model profile.
- Locked profile behavior.
- Non-PD strategies remain unchanged.
- Rejected requests do not modify RPS or in-flight state.
- Rejected requests do not send a prefill request.

## Non-goals

- Do not add PD support to Responses or Messages.
- Do not modify PD request transformation.
- Do not change non-PD router behavior.
- Do not modify HTTPRoutes.
- Do not introduce endpoint or engine capability discovery.

## Acceptance criteria

- PD is accepted only for the two approved generation endpoints.
- Unsupported endpoint-PD combinations return `400 Bad Request`.
- The error identifies the endpoint and strategy.
- Rejection happens before routing and accounting side effects.
- Existing non-PD behavior remains compatible.

items.title: [Bug]: `/metrics` (iteration-stats) route blocks the serve event loop — a 2 s Prometheus scrape inflates request latency 5–60× and cuts prefill throughput ~5× (4× RTX 5060 Ti TP4, Qwen3.5 hybrid-GDN NVFP4 27B, 1.3.0rc29)
items.author: sean640112
items.body_excerpt:
> **Update (2026-10-09): the root cause is not sm120.** The "fixed" per-request cost comes from the `/metrics` iteration-stats route blocking the serve event loop: a 2 s Prometheus scrape inflates request latency 5–60× and cuts prefill throughput ~5×. Controlled A/B, py-spy stacks and the Prometheus-side numbers are in the [follow-up comment](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/issues/19623#issuecomment-6076428189) below.

# ~6 s fixed per-request latency floor on sm120 (4× RTX 5060 Ti, TP4) with a Qwen3.5 hybrid-GDN 27B NVFP4 checkpoint

## Summary

On a 4× RTX 5060 Ti (sm120) box serving a **dense hybrid GDN + full-attention 27B** NVFP4 checkpoint with `trtllm-serve` (PyTorch backend, TP4), we measure a **~6 s per-request floor on time-to-first-token that is independent of prompt length**. A 212-token request takes **6.06 s** to first token (8.0 s total), and the floor persists at every length we tested (212 → 59,571 tokens). Requests are reproducible to ±5 ms across 12 measurements in 3 separate server starts.

The same hardware, same checkpoint, same prompt, same client, served by SGLang gives **0.26–0.30 s** for the identical request. `trtllm-serve` therefore looks ~20× slower on short requests, while its *marginal* prefill throughput is only ~2.6× lower (~2,143 tok/s vs ~5,600 tok/s).

We have ruled out MTP/spec-decode, scheduler policy, `max_seq_len`, chunked prefill, the CUDA caching allocator, and thinking-mode as causes (details below). We would like to know whether this per-request floor is **expected on sm120 for hybrid GDN models**, or a bug — and which knob/diagnostic we should look at next. We are happy to run any instrumentation you suggest.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU | 4× NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB, compute capability **12.0 (sm120)**, TP=4 |
| Driver | 610.57.04 |
| CUDA toolkit | 13.3 (`nvcc` 13.3, `CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-13.3`) |
| OS / Python | Linux, Python 3.12.11 (venv) |
| TensorRT-LLM | **1.3.0rc29.dev202609240000** (nightly from 2026-09-24; PyPI 1.2.1 does not contain `modeling_qwen3_5.py`, hence nightly) |
| torch | 2.14.0+cu132 |
| flashinfer-python | 0.6.18 |
| triton | 3.8.0 |
| nvidia-cutlass-dsl | 4.8.0.dev0 |
| tensorrt / tensorrt_cu13 | 10.14.1.48.post1 |
| MPI | OpenMPI 5.0.10 (`mpi4py` bootstrap path) |
| Model | `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` — `architectures: ["Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration"]`, `model_type: qwen3_5`; 64 layers, hidden 5120, 24 Q heads, 4 KV heads |
| Quantization | ModelOpt `MIXED_PRECISION`: **FP8 per-tensor on 208 layers** (`block_size` absent) + **NVFP4 `group_size: 16` on 193 layers**, `kv_cache_quant_algo: null` |

Note on the attention backend: your hardware support matrix lists sm120 as supporting NVFP4 / MXFP4 / FP8 (per-tensor) / FP8 KV cache, which covers this checkpoint's formats — so the quantization scheme itself should be fully supported on sm120.

## How to reproduce

Server (the `mpirun -n 1` wrapper and `OMPI_MCA_*` are needed on this host because `import tensorrt_llm` otherwise blocks in the mpi4py `MPI.COMM_WORLD` initialization, and this host's own hostname resolves to loopback only):

```bash
export CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-13.3
export OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=lo OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=lo
mpirun -n 1 --oversubscribe trtllm-serve serve /path/to/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 1234 --tp_size 4 \
  --max_seq_len 140000 --max_batch_size 8 \
  --served_model_name qwen3.8-27b \
  --free_gpu_memory_fraction 0.80 \
  --extra_llm_api_options opts.yaml
```

`opts.yaml`:
```yaml
enable_chunked_prefill: true
max_num_tokens: 8192
speculative_config:
  decoding_type: MTP
  max_draft_len: 3
  speculative_model: /path/to/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4
```

Client — a minimal stdlib-only streaming client (this is the "probe" used for every number below; it measures the first chunk that carries `choices[0].text`/`delta.content`):

```python
import json, time, urllib.request
prompt = open("/path/to/corpus.txt").read()[:600]          # → 212 tokens
body = {"model": "qwen3.8-27b", "prompt": prompt, "max_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0, "stream": True}
req = urllib.request.Request("http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1/completions",
        data=json.dumps(body).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
t0 = time.time(); ttft = None
with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=900) as r:
    for raw in r:
        s = raw.decode().strip()
        if not s.startswith("data: "): continue
        if s[6:] == "[DONE]": break
        d = json.loads(s[6:])
        ch = d.get("choices") or []
        if ch and ch[0].get("text"):
            ttft = time.time() - t0; break
print("TTFT", ttft)
```

## Measured results (same probe, same prompts, same box)

| prompt tokens | path | TRT-LLM stream TTFT | TRT-LLM non-stream total | SGLang stream TTFT | SGLang non-stream total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **212** | completions | **6.053–6.062 s** (n=5) | 7.995–8.035 s | **0.262 s** | 0.304 s |
| 222 | chat (medium template) | 12.11 – **22.21 s** (unstable across restarts) | 14.06 – 26.19 s | 0.268 s | — |
| 7,172 | completions | 10.10 s | 12.02 s | 0.243 s *cached* | 1.84 s *cached* |
| 12,131 | completions | 12.12 s | 14.06 s | — | — |
| 28,008 | completions | — | 20.13 s | — | 6.15 s *cached* |
| 59,571 | completions | — | 36.26 s | — | — |
| 65,032 | chat | 56.52 s | 56.45 s | — | — |

*("cached" = the SGLang side hit its radix prefix cache on the shared corpus prefix, so those cells are not a like-for-like prefill comparison.)*

Least-squares fit of the completions path (`total = C + N/R`, 5 points spanning 212 → 59,571 tokens):
**C = 8.10 s, R = 2,143 tok/s, R² = 0.9966** — i.e. a very large constant plus a modest rate term. (The streaming TTFT is ≈ 1.9 s lower at every point, i.e. TTFT ≈ 6.1 s + N/2143.)

For reference, an independent client (vLLM's `bench serve` against the same server) measured prefill throughput of **453 / 1,014 / 1,302 tok/s** at 8K / 32K / 64K with meanTTFT 16.15 / 29.28 / 46.44 s, i.e. the same

comments.author: LaelaZorana
comments.body:
Probe done, single GPU numbers below. This isolates the GDN prefill cost independent of the TP4, mpirun and NVFP4 27B variables.

Env is TensorRT-LLM 1.3.0rc29, torch 2.14.0, single RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell sm120. Model is Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B, qwen3_5, same hybrid GDN family, served via trtllm-serve at TP1.

Results, TTFT over 5 runs

With FlashInfer prefill on, the default, the 212 tok prompt with max_tokens 1 took 16.1 to 17.5 ms and the 4096 tok prompt took 49.6 to 53.9 ms. With FlashInfer prefill off, TLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_GDN_PREFILL=0, they took 17.8 to 19.1 ms and 49.9 to 52.5 ms.

Stream closes within 0.1 ms of TTFT, single token responses. FlashInfer is the default, see the server log.

Takeaways

On one card, GDN prefill is measured in milliseconds, nowhere near the 6.1 s floor. That floor comes from the TP4 path, the mpirun loopback setup, or something about the NVFP4 27B ckpt.

FlashInfer toggle moves latency only about 2 ms either way here.

Server log also flags an Autotuner cache miss, falling back, for nvfp4_gemm on shape 4 by 2560, which fits a small M shape, just FYI.

Next steps to nail down the 6.1 s

Serve the same 2B at TP4 on the same box, which shows if it is the TP4 path.

Short nsys capture around a single 212 tok request, where GPU busy vs. wall clock shows GDN kernels vs. gaps.

If the GPUs are idle for about 6 s, py-spy dump on rank 0 should show exactly where the wall clock goes.

comments.author: sean640112
comments.body:
**Follow-up: the per-request latency floor and the prefill throughput cap are both caused by scraping the `/metrics` route, not by sm120**

Thanks for the earlier guidance. Following it, we ran controlled A/Bs on the same binary and found that the "fixed per-request cost" comes from the **Prometheus scrape of `/metrics`**, and that it degrades more than first-token latency.

Setup: TRT-LLM 1.3.0rc29, sm120, 4× RTX 5060 Ti 16G, TP4, `Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (hybrid GDN), `mpirun -n 1 trtllm-serve ... --tp_size 4`.

**A. Short requests** (212-token prompt, reproducible ±5 ms)

| | engine on `127.0.0.1:1234` (Prometheus scrapes every 2 s) | same engine on `127.0.0.1:1235` (nothing scrapes it) |
|---|---|---|
| 212-token, non-stream | **7.74 / 8.07 / 8.07 s** | **0.137 / 0.137 / 0.178 s** |
| stream TTFT | **6.060 / 6.060 / 6.060 s** | **0.139 / 0.138 / 0.140 s** |

**B. Prefill throughput** (canonical `vllm bench serve`, `--dataset-name random`, 2 prompts, concurrency 1, output len 1)

| input len | scrape active | not scraped |
|---|---|---|
| 8,192 | 488 tok/s (Mean TTFT 14,996 ms) | **2,514 tok/s (2,911 ms)** |
| 32,768 | 1,081 tok/s (27,476 ms) | **2,386 tok/s (12,449 ms)** |
| 65,536 | 1,452 tok/s | **2,177 tok/s** |

So a 2-second monitoring scrape costs anywhere from ~5× to ~60× depending on the request shape.

Prometheus side (`job_name: llm`, `scrape_interval: 2s`, `scrape_timeout: 1500ms`, `metrics_path: /metrics`), its own `scrape_duration_seconds{job="llm"}`:

* with our TRT-LLM server up: every scrape **times out at 1.5003–1.5012 s** (`up=0`)
* with our SGLang server on the same port: 0.060–0.063 s (`up=1`)

Mechanism: the single serve event loop is blocked inside the `/metrics` handler, which awaits engine stats through a blocking RPC. py-spy from the frontend process shows the same stack at 0.6 s / 3 s / 6 s into a request:

```
get_iteration_stats (serve/openai_server.py) -> get_stats_async (llmapi/llm.py)
  -> aget_stats (executor/proxy.py) -> _call_sync (executor/rpc/rpc_client.py) -> Future.result()
```

TTFT ≈ 3 × 2.02 s and non-stream total ≈ 4 × 2.02 s — the scrape interval *is* the quantum. It also explains why the engine looked idle while requests were slow: GPUs at ~0% util, rank 0's executor parked in `queue.get()`, and the other ranks spinning in the per-iteration request-count broadcast — the request had not reached the engine yet.

Mitigations we tested:

1. **Not scraping the port** → full recovery (tables above).
2. `enable_iter_perf_stats: true` in the extra LLM API options → **short requests recovered** (0.184 s / TTFT 0.140 s) while Prometheus kept scraping every 2 s, **but prefill did not** (8K stayed at 488 tok/s vs 2,514 clean). So that flag is not a substitute for fixing the route.

The underlying hazard looks like the stats route awaiting a blocking RPC on the serve event loop (the source comment in that path mentions nvbug 6102381). Making `/metrics` non-blocking by default — or documenting that Prometheus should scrape `/prometheus/metrics` rather than the JSON stats route — would prevent a monitoring scrape from inflating latency and prefill cost by 5–60×.

Happy to share py-spy dumps, full server args, or run a patched build on this exact setup (4× sm120 consumer cards, TP4) if that helps.

Thanks again, @LaelaZorana — this was filed half expecting it to go unanswered, so your reply was a pleasant surprise, and it is what led us to run the A/B that found the real cause.

items.title: CUTLASS 4.8.0
items.author: Junkai-Wu
items.body_excerpt:
### CuTe DSL
* New features
  - Initial Rubin support to accelerate dense GEMMs. The following features are available:  
    - CuTe DSL and CuTe extensions
      - Support for higher-throughput FP8 (MMA_K=64) and FP4 (MMA_K=128) Tensor Core MMA instructions
      - B collector reuse 
      - Extended TMEM size from 512 COL to 576 COL
      - Larger shared memory allocations (328KB)
      - Enhanced mixed precision throughput (FP8/FP4)
      - Softmax acceleration related features
    - Primitives
      - Support for higher-throughput FP8 (MMA_K=64) and FP4 (MMA_K=128) Tensor Core MMA instructions
      - B collector reuse
      - Extended TMEM size from 512 COL to 576 COL
      - Larger shared memory allocations (328KB)
      - Enhanced mixed precision throughput (FP8/FP4)
      - Softmax acceleration related feature
      - 2:4 sparsity support for FP4

  - CuTe DSL extensions has several new features:
    - CTA-V maps are now inferred automatically for `cute_ext` TMA load, store, multicast, and reduce-store operations. Explicit CTA-V maps remain supported as overrides.
    - Added asynchronous atomic TMA reduce-store and sparse MMA operations.
    - Added reusable `cute_ext` GEMM mainloop and TMA epilogue helpers.
    - Added opt-in TMEM accumulator-buffer planning, including overlapping ping-pong storage for capacity-constrained kernels.
    - Improved device-side TMA descriptor updates and grouped GEMM performance through SMEM-staged updates, workspace reuse, and reduced prologue and synchronization overhead.
  - This release includes an opt-in preview of the CuTe DSL extensions (`cute_ext`) compiler pipeline for ordinary Cute DSL kernels. This pipeline lets user mix `cute_ext` APIs directly into `@cute.jit` and `@cute.kernel` code and is required for kernels that mix the two API surfaces. You may test this feature with the following:
  `CUTE_DSL_USE_EXTENSION_COMPILER=1 python your_program.py`
The pipeline is expected to preserve program behavior and performance, but generated PTX/SASS may differ.  Note that this pipeline will become the default in the future, no earlier than 4.10.
  - Added examples for better control over Primitives' compiler warnings/errors introduced in 4.7.0.  See the `CuTeDSL/experimental/compiler_diagnostic/` directory.
  - IKET Profiler Tool

items.title: Refactor: Split up ggml-vulkan.cpp
items.author: 0cc4m
items.body_excerpt:
### Background Description

The ggml-vulkan.cpp file is still following the old one-file-per-backend approach, and has grown pretty unwieldy as a result (~17500 lines now!). I would like to break it up into a number of easier-to-work with files. I'm opening this issue to discuss mainly with @jeffbolznv, but if anyone else has suggestions or opinions, feel free to add them as well.

### Possible Refactor Approaches

Currently the file contains all this (line numbers may be outdated):
| Section | Lines | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Types, structs, constants | 1–1650 | Push constants, pipeline structs, device struct, enums, context |
| Buffer management | 1987–2060, 2541–2933 | Create/destroy/copy/read/write buffers, host memory, staging |
| Pipeline & shader loading | 2109–2264, 3096–4736 | Pipeline creation, `ggml_vk_load_shaders` (~1600 lines) |
| Device & instance init | 4739–5967 | Physical device probing, logical device, instance creation |
| Pipeline selection & dispatch | 5967–7138 | Pipeline getters, command buffer mgmt, dispatch helpers |
| Matrix multiply ops | 7335–8700 | GEMM, GEMV, mul_mat_id, p021/nc variants |
| Flash attention | 8707–9069 | FA implementation + shmem support checks |
| Op pipeline selection | 9069–9754 | `ggml_vk_op_get_pipeline` — maps ggml_op to pipeline |
| Op dispatch & wrappers | 9754–11808 | `ggml_vk_op_f32` + ~60 individual op functions |
| Debug/test utilities | 11808–12577 | Test matmul/dequant, print helpers |
| Graph build & compute | 12577–13348 | `build_graph`, `compute_forward`, cleanup |
| Backend interface | 13348–15060 | Buffer type, backend functions, `graph_compute`, `supports_op` |
| Device/registry interface | 15061–15909 | `ggml_backend_vk_device_*`, `ggml_backend_vk_reg_*` |
| Deferred utilities | 15909–16032 | Extension/layer availability checks |
| Debug validation | 16032–16754 | `check_results_0/1`, CPU reference comparison |

This is mostly already following a structure, so much can likely be just split up along those lines. Here's a possible structure. I'm not sure if it would work out exactly like this or whether some dependency issues would come up.

`ggml-vulkan-types.h` for all the structs and types.
`ggml-vulkan.h` for functions used internally (e.g. those that are already forward-declared) and for globals
`ggml-vulkan-instance.cpp` for the main instance and its initialization functions.
`ggml-vulkan-shaders.cpp` for shader loading (mainly `ggml_vk_load_shaders`).
`ggml-vulkan-buffers.cpp` for the buffer management functions.
`ggml-vulkan-pipelines.cpp` for the pipeline loading and dispatch functions.
`ggml-vulkan-matmul.cpp` for the matmul host functions.
`ggml-vulkan-flash-attn.cpp` for the flash attention host functions.
`ggml-vulkan-operators.cpp` for `ggml_vk_op_f32` and the operator functions calling it.
`ggml-vulkan-graph.cpp` for the graph building and compute functions.
`ggml-vulkan-backend.cpp` for the backend interface functions.
`ggml-vulkan-debug.cpp` for the debug and internal benchmark functions.

I would also like to use the opportunity to move from `static` functions to namespaces, if possible.

The most tricky part is getting a PR up and finding the right moment where merging it would not disrupt much work.

items.title: Should LMCacheMPConnector honor kv_transfer_config.kv_role — or is MP mode intentionally always-kv_both?
items.author: kezboard233
items.body_excerpt:
## Context

We run a production-shaped POC on 8×V100 (two vLLM TP4 instances of Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 sharing one LMCache MP server with a CPU L1 tier) and filed #5143 with a runtime-verified repro: an engine launched with `kv_role="kv_consumer"` still stores every request's KV into the shared L1 — a single 32K-token cold request produced `168 × "Stored 784"` lines (= full prefix × 4 TP ranks), and the only engine that received any request in that window was the `kv_consumer` one.

We later found #4665 (closed by its author without maintainer response) reporting the same mechanism from the CacheBlend angle: the single-process connector honors `kv_role` / `skip_save`, the MP connector honors neither. As of today's `dev`, `lmcache_mp_connector.py` still contains no occurrence of `kv_role` / `kv_consumer` / `kv_producer` / `force_skip_save`.

## The design question

Before we contribute a patch, we want to check intent: **is MP mode intentionally "every connected engine writes"?** Two readings:

1. **Contract gap** — vLLM makes `kv_role` mandatory, documents it as "Whether this vLLM instance produces, consumes KV cache, or both", and exposes `is_kv_producer` / `is_kv_consumer` for connectors to branch on; LMCache's own single-process adapter honors it (`force_skip_save` in `vllm_v1_adapter.py`). Under this reading we'd gladly contribute a small PR that skips store-metadata generation when `is_kv_consumer` (mirroring the single-process gate), so warm-then-read-only fleets and PD-style topologies become possible on the MP path.

2. **Intentional always-kv_both** — the MP tier is a shared scratch space where every connected engine contributes. Under this reading we'd instead ask for the intent to be documented, plus ideally a one-line warning at connector init when `kv_role != "kv_both"`, so users aren't misled (we only noticed via instrumented counter evidence ourselves).

Happy to do either — a steer from maintainers decides which.

(Impact context: no correctness issue — stored content is identical — but a consumer-role engine burns D2H bandwidth and shared-L1 capacity; a 32K prefix on our model is ≈8.6 GB across 4 ranks.)

items.title: [Bug]: Kimi Linear / Kimi K3 fail to load from the release container: No module named 'fla'
items.author: vsabavat
items.body_excerpt:
## System Info

- TensorRT-LLM release container `1.3.0rc28` (and any plain `pip install tensorrt_llm` from the wheel)
- Models: Kimi Linear, Kimi K3 (Kimi Delta Attention layers)

## Who can help?

@juney-nvidia

## Reproduction

Load Kimi Linear or Kimi K3 in the release container (or a fresh environment with only the wheel's runtime requirements):

```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fla'
```

`tensorrt_llm/_torch/modules/kimi_kda/kimi_kda_mixer.py` imports `fla.modules.ShortConvolution` at load time (line 26 in 1.3.0rc28). Short prefill and the decode / verify fallbacks also call `fla.ops.kda.chunk_kda` and `fla.ops.kda.fused_recurrent_kda`.

## Expected behavior

Both models load from a standard install.

## Actual behavior

flash-linear-attention is listed only in `requirements-dev.txt`. CI installs that file in every test stage, so CI passes. The release container and `pip install` of the wheel install only `requirements.txt`, so the import fails.

## Additional notes

Fix proposed in #19837: add `fla-core==0.5.2` to `requirements.txt`. It is the same version `requirements-dev.txt` already installs (via `flash-linear-attention==0.5.2`) and is MIT-licensed. The new-dependency license/vulnerability scan still needs the maintainers' tooling.

items.title: moe_cute_util.cuh: util_convert_type returns a tensor that points at a local array
items.author: BwL1289
items.body_excerpt:
In `cpp/tensorrt_llm/cutlass_extensions/include/cutlass_extensions/gemm/kernel/moe_cute_util.cuh`:

```cpp
auto frag = convert_op(*reinterpret_cast<cutlass::Array<From_type, numel> const*>(tensor.data()));
return cute::make_tensor(cute::make_rmem_ptr<To_type>(&frag), tensor.layout());
```

The returned tensor is a view of `frag`, a local of `util_convert_type`. `frag` is gone once the function returns, so
reading the result is undefined behaviour. Both routines in `fused_moe_kernel_routine.cuh` read it
(`util_convert_type<...>(accum)`, then the copy to shared memory).

With nvcc this happens to work. With clang (device code at -O3, sm_121a) the conversion and the SwiGLU that feed it are
removed, ptxas then removes the MMAs whose results are no longer used, and the kernel stores registers nothing wrote.
SASS counts (HMMA / LDSM / F2FP / FMUL) for the bf16 32x128x64 SwiGLU instantiation of
`fused_moe::run_global<Fused_Moe_Kernel_sm80<...>>`:

- nvcc (NVIDIA's flashinfer-jit-cache 0.7.0+cu130 wheel): 96 / 64 / 12 / 72
- clang: 64 / 40 / 0 / 48
- clang with the change below: 96 / 64 / 12 / 72

A bf16 or fp16 MoE call through this kernel (DeepSeek-V2-Lite shapes, 256 and 8192 tokens) then gets every row wrong
(NaN or values up to 1e37), and the output changes from call to call. With the change, the output matches the nvcc build
to every printed digit (max abs error against a float32 reference: 1.6e-05 for bf16 at 256 tokens, as with nvcc).

Suggested change, which returns a fragment that owns its registers (same layout, same element order):

```cpp
static_assert(cute::cosize_v<Layout> == numel, "util_convert_type: the fragment must be contiguous");
auto frag = convert_op(*reinterpret_cast<cutlass::Array<From_type, numel> const*>(tensor.data()));
auto out = cute::make_tensor<To_type>(tensor.layout());
CUTLASS_PRAGMA_UNROLL
for (int i = 0; i < numel; ++i) {
  out.data()[i] = frag[i];
}
return out;
```

To see the lifetime problem without a GPU: compile the function against small stand-ins for the CuTe/CUTLASS types it
uses, read the returned tensor after the call, and run it under AddressSanitizer with
`ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_stack_use_after_return=1`. The current code is reported as a stack-use-after-return; the change
above is not.

FlashInfer's own `include/flashinfer/attention/hopper/utils.cuh` (`convert_type`) has the same pattern.

items.title: [Bug] calculate_nvfp4_global_scale returns wrong per-token scales for hidden sizes above 8192 that are not multiples of 8192
items.author: builtin-pb
items.body_excerpt:
### System Info

- TensorRT-LLM 1.2.1 wheel, torch 2.9.1+cu130, A100 80GB PCIe (driver 610.57).
- The kernel is unchanged on main `b031dbe`: `cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/quantization.cu` and `cpp/tensorrt_llm/common/reduceKernelUtils.cuh`.

### Who can help?

_No response_

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [x] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

`torch.ops.trtllm.calculate_nvfp4_global_scale(x, None)` on a bf16 `x` of shape `[m, n]` should return `448 * 6 / max|x[i]|` for each token. When the hidden size is above 8192 and not a multiple of 8192, many tokens get a wrong scale once a CTA handles more than one token (for a 2-D input, `m` above the SM count).

A minimal script:

```python
import torch
import tensorrt_llm  # registers torch.ops.trtllm

m = 512
torch.manual_seed(0)
rows = torch.arange(m)
amp = 2.0 ** ((rows * 5) % 11 - 3) * (1 + (rows * 3 % 8) / 8)  # per-token maximum
for n in (12288, 8192):
    x = (torch.rand(m, n) - 0.5) * amp[:, None]
    x[rows, torch.randint(n, (m,))] = amp
    x = x.bfloat16().cuda()
    ref = 2688.0 / x.double().abs().amax(1, keepdim=True)
    got = torch.ops.trtllm.calculate_nvfp4_global_scale(x, None)
    bad = ((got.double() - ref).abs() > 1e-4 + 2e-6 * ref.abs()).sum().item()
    print(f"n={n}: {bad} of {m} tokens have a wrong global scale")
```

On an A100 (SXM4 80GB) it printed:

```
n=12288: 309 of 512 tokens have a wrong global scale
n=8192: 0 of 512 tokens have a wrong global scale
```

Results with the 1.2.1 wheel:
- each call was checked in full against a float64 reference;
- a call counts as wrong if any token's scale is non-finite or off by more than 1e-4 + 2e-6 · |ref|.

| x shape (bf16) | wrong calls | wrong tokens in sampled calls |
|---|---|---|
| [512, 12288] | 914302 / 914302 | 301–318 of 512 |
| [256, 28672] | 920766 / 920766 | 101–114 of 256 |
| [512, 8192] | 0 / 924832 | |
| [1024, 4096] | 0 / 914518 | |

For example, in the first call at [512, 12288], token 3 got 28.0 instead of 42.0.

### Expected behavior

Each token's global scale is `2688 / max|x[i]|`, for any `n` the operator accepts. The launcher checks only `n % 256 == 0`.

### actual behavior

In `computePerTokenGlobalScaleForFP4QuantizationKernel` (`quantization.cu:351–374`), `getMaxAbs` calls `blockReduceMaxV2`, which contains a `__syncthreads()`, inside the per-thread loop:

```cpp
for (int vecIdx = threadIdx.x; vecIdx < n / ElemsPerVec; vecIdx += blockDim.x)
{
    float4 vec = reinterpret_cast<float4 const*>(input + tokenIdx * n)[vecIdx];
    float maxAbsVal = getMaxAbs<T>(vec);   // blockReduceMaxV2 -> __syncthreads()
    perTokenMaxAbsVal = cuda_max(perTokenMaxAbsVal, maxAbsVal);
}
```

The launcher uses `blockDim.x = min(n / 8, 1024)`. When `n / 8` is above 1024 and not a multiple of it, threads with `threadIdx.x < (n / 8) % 1024` run one more iteration per token than the others. CUDA requires a `__syncthreads()` in conditional code to be reached by all threads of the block, and here it is not.

The warps with fewer iterations run ahead. Each barrier instance then joins warp 0's reduction of one token with the other warps' reductions of later tokens handled by the same CTA. After those warps exit, it joins with the values they left in shared memory. The reduced maximum mixes tokens. In a standalone copy of the kernel, run without Compute Sanitizer, every wrong value matched the one predicted from this pairing.

A second, smaller problem: `blockReduceMaxV2` has no barrier between warp 0's read of `shared[lane]` (`reduceKernelUtils.cuh:281`) and the next call's write of `shared[wid]` (line 269). On the standalone copy, Compute Sanitizer racecheck reports hazards between these two lines at every shape we tested, including `n` = 4096 and 8192. Under racecheck or synccheck, those two shapes also returned wrong scales (one launch each), though they were correct in every plain run.

### additional notes

Suggested fix: reduce once per token, after the loop, followed by a barrier.

```diff
@@ -343,7 +343,6 @@ __device__ float getMaxAbs(float4& vec)
     {
         absMaxVal = static_cast<float>(cuda_max(absMaxVec.x, absMaxVec.y));
     }
-    tensorrt_llm::common::blockReduceMaxV2<float, 1>(&absMaxVal);
     return absMaxVal;
 }
 
@@ -365,6 +364,11 @@ __global__ void computePerTokenGlobalScaleForFP4QuantizationKernel(
             float maxAbsVal = getMaxAbs<T>(vec);
             perTokenMaxAbsVal = cuda_max(perTokenMaxAbsVal, maxAbsVal);
         }
+        // Reduce once per token, outside the per-thread loop: threads make different numbers of loop iterations
+        // when n / ElemsPerVec is not a multiple of blockDim.x.
+        tensorrt_llm::common::blockReduceMaxV2<float, 1>(&perTokenMaxAbsVal);
+        // blockReduceMaxV2's shared slots are rewritten by the next token's reduction.
+        __syncthreads();
         float globalScaleVal = 448.f * 6.f / perTokenMaxAbsVal;
         if (threadIdx.x == 0)
         {
```

A standalone copy of the kernel with the equivalent change gave no wrong scales on A100 and A40, and is clean under racecheck and synccheck.

**Reach.** Callers in the tree:
- the opt-in NVFP4 low-precision MoE combine in `nccl_ep.py:460` (`use_low_precision_moe_combine`, default off). It requires NVFP4 and a hidden size that is a multiple of 512, so sizes such as 10240 or 12288 can reach it. items.title: flashMLA utils.h: convert_type returns a tensor that points at a local array
items.author: peter941221
items.body_excerpt:
In `cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/flashMLA/utils.h` (line 277-286):

```cpp
auto frag = convert_op(*reinterpret_cast<cutlass::Array<From_type, numel> const*>(tensor.data()));
return make_tensor(make_rmem_ptr<To_type>(&frag), tensor.layout());
```

Same defect as #19943. `make_rmem_ptr` on a raw pointer is the identity, so the returned tensor is a view of `frag`, a local of `convert_type`; reading the result after the call is undefined behaviour. Both live call sites are in `flash_fwd_mla_kernel.h`:

- line 271 (store epilogue): `Tensor rO = flash::convert_type<ElementO>(tOrO);`, then `retile_S` and `cute::copy` read through the pointer; `tOrO` is the `partition_fragment_C` accumulator.
- line 817 (splitkv combine kernel): `Tensor rO = flash::convert_type<Element>(tOrO);`, then `cute::copy(rO, gO)` reads it.

`convert_type_out` in the same file takes the output by reference and is fine; its comment already notes that the output can be wrong when the result is allocated and returned inside the helper, so the returning variant looks like a known hazard that was not fixed.

With nvcc the read returns stale values (registers/local memory), so it is silent in practice; it is still the same lifetime bug that was fixed in `cutlass_extensions` by #20017.

Reproduction without a GPU: compile the function verbatim in a host translation unit, read the returned tensor after the call, run under AddressSanitizer with `ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_stack_use_after_return=1`. The current code is reported as a stack-use-after-return pointing at `frag` inside the `convert_type` frame. Returning `make_tensor<To_type>(tensor.layout())` (an owning ArrayEngine) with the elements copied in is clean. The contiguity the HACK comment assumes can be enforced with `static_assert(cosize_v<Layout> == numel, ...)`, which holds for both real instantiations: the `partition_fragment_C` layout has cosize 128 == size 128, and the combine kernel's `make_tensor<ElementAccum>(shape(...))` layout has cosize 4 == size 4.

This helper is a copy of FlashInfer's `include/flashinfer/attention/hopper/utils.cuh` (`convert_type`), which still has the same pattern at line 153.

items.author: VaggelisGian
items.body_excerpt:
### Description

examples/64_ada_fp8_gemm_grouped/ada_fp8_gemm_grouped.cu (~line 1107) gates execution on exactly compute capability 8.9:

```cpp
if (!(properties.major == 8 && properties.minor == 9)) {
    std::cerr << "... requires a device of compute capability 89." ...
```

The grouped FP8 kernels here compile cleanly for newer architectures, and the sibling example 58_ada_fp8_gemm uses the inclusive form:

```cpp
if (properties.major < 8 || (properties.major == 8 && properties.minor < 9))
```

On an RTX 5060 Ti (sm_120a, CUDA 12.8.1) the stock binary exits immediately with the capability message; with the gate relaxed to the sibling's form the example builds and runs to completion including device-reference verification (`Passed`). Example 64 is therefore refusing capable hardware for no functional reason.

### Suggested fix

Use the same `major*10+minor < 89` / `major < 8 || (major == 8 && minor < 9)` inclusive check as example 58.

items.author: RobotGF

comments.author: RobotGF
comments.body:
Update: I retested the public reproducer with **CUDA Toolkit 13.4 Update 1**, released on 2026-09-09. Its NVCC component reports:

```
Cuda compilation tools, release 13.4, V13.4.59
Build cuda_13.4.r13.4/compiler.38657139_0
```

Using the same CUTLASS `main` commit (`147295a3d4b75f3aeff247c25b8927cea9a7006a`) and GCC 12.3.1:

| NVCC | Source form | Result | Generated `repro.cudafe1.cpp` |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| 13.4.59 | structured binding | stopped after exceeding the 64 MiB safety limit in 22.24 s | >64 MiB |
| 13.4.59 | `std::get` workaround | succeeds in 36.65 s | 13,232,759 bytes |

So the `cudafe++` expansion regression is still present in CUDA 13.4 Update 1; the workaround remains effective.

comments.author: RobotGF
comments.body:
Further isolation points to the tuple-like structured-binding type printer in `cudafe++`, rather than CUTLASS/CuTe semantics or the host compiler.

I passed the exact same public repro preprocessed input (`repro.cpp4.ii`) directly to each `cudafe++` binary:

| `cudafe++` | EDG front end | Result | Generated host C++ |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| 13.0.88 | 6.7 | succeeds | 13,135,720 bytes |
| 13.1.115 | 6.7 | succeeds | 13,136,458 bytes |
| 13.2.86 | 6.7 | succeeds | 13,133,760 bytes |
| 13.3.33 | 6.8 | stopped at safety limit | >64 MiB |
| 13.3.73 | 6.8 | stopped at safety limit | >64 MiB |
| 13.4.59 | 6.8 | stopped at safety limit | >64 MiB |

The first observed regression is therefore the initial CUDA 13.3 compiler build. The EDG 6.7 to 6.8 change correlates with its introduction, although this alone does not establish whether the defect is in EDG itself or NVIDIA's CUDA-specific integration.

Generated-code comparison on the identical input is particularly revealing:

* 13.2.86 emits a 2,415-byte kernel-instantiation line containing concrete `cute::TiledCopy<...>` types. The entire file contains 151 occurrences of `tuple_element`.
* 13.3.33 emits an incomplete 56,050,392-byte kernel-instantiation line beginning with `std::tuple_element<0, std::tuple<...>>`. That partial file already contains 660,490 occurrences of `tuple_element`.

Additional syntax tests with NVCC 13.4.59 and the current CUTLASS `main`:

| Form | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `std::tuple` + structured binding + `decltype(binding)` | fails / expands |
| `cute::tuple` + structured binding + `decltype(binding)` | fails / expands |
| Plain aggregate return + structured binding + `decltype(binding)` | succeeds |
| `std::apply` with deduced lambda parameters | succeeds |
| Helper function that deduces the kernel template arguments from values | succeeds |

This matches the C++ structured-binding rules: tuple-like decomposition gives each binding a referenced type based on `tuple_element<I, E>::type`, while aggregate decomposition uses the declared member type. In 13.3+, `cudafe++` appears to preserve and recursively print the former type expression instead of canonicalizing it before serializing the explicit CUDA kernel template-id.

A compiler-friendly workaround that preserves the original call-site syntax is therefore to return a plain aggregate rather than a tuple:

```cpp
template<class Q, class KV, class Y>
struct TmaBundle { Q q; KV kv; Y y; };

auto [q, kv, y] = make_tma_bundle(...);
auto kernel = probe<decltype(q), decltype(kv), decltype(y)>;
```

I also tested this form in the larger source: NVCC 13.3.73 host generation succeeds and returns to the normal ~13 MiB output size; a full NVCC 13.4.59 compile succeeds as well.

items.title: [BUG] [BUG] `cute.arch.store` doesn't work with fp8 vector
items.author: gau-nernst
items.body_excerpt:
### Which component has the problem?

CuTe DSL

### Bug Report

**Describe the bug**
A clear and concise description of what the bug is.

`cute.arch.store` documents `val` as "scalar Numeric or vector ir.Value". Storing a `TensorSSA` vector works for f32, bf16, f16, u8, i8 and i16, for example `cute.arch.store(ptr, x.load().to(BFloat16))`; each lowers to a single `st.global.v8.b32`. With an fp8 element type (`Float8E4M3FN` or `Float8E5M2`), the same call passes tracing, but backend compilation fails with an internal error:

```
error: NVVM backend compilation failed
error: libNVVM failed while compiling generated device IR.
       LLVM Translation failed for operation: builtin.unrealized_conversion_cast
       Failed creating the llvm::Module.
```

It is not about bit width: 8-bit integer vectors work, and so does the same fp8 vector after `.bitcast(Uint8)` (also a single `st.global.v8.b32`). It looks like a vector of fp8 has no type conversion in the LLVM lowering of the store. `Tensor.store()` of the same fp8 vector does work, but it emits extra byte shuffles (`PRMT`) compared with the bitcast path.

**Steps/Code to reproduce bug**
Follow this guide http://matthewrocklin.com/blog/work/2018/02/28/minimal-bug-reports to craft a minimal bug report. This helps us reproduce the issue you're having and resolve the issue more quickly.

Compile-only (no GPU run needed):

```python
# CuTeDSL MRE: cute.arch.store of an fp8 vector fails in the NVVM backend.
#
# cute.arch.store documents `val` as "scalar Numeric or vector ir.Value". An
# f32 / bf16 / u8 / i8 TensorSSA stores fine (one st.global.v8.b32), but an
# fp8 one (x.to(Float8E4M3FN) or Float8E5M2) traces and then fails while
# lowering:
#   LLVM Translation failed for operation: builtin.unrealized_conversion_cast
# Not a bit-width issue: the same fp8 vector bitcast to Uint8 stores fine.
#
# Compile-only; prints one line per variant.
#   python arch_store_fp8_vector.py
import importlib.metadata

import cutlass
import cutlass.cute as cute
from cutlass import BFloat16, Float8E4M3FN, Float8E5M2, Float32, Int8, Uint8

N = 32  # elements per thread


def make(dtype, via_u8):
    @cute.kernel
    def kernel(out: cute.Tensor):
        tid, _, _ = cute.arch.thread_idx()
        x = cute.make_rmem_tensor(N, Float32)
        for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(N):
            x[i] = Float32(tid + i)
        v = x.load().to(dtype)
        dst = out[tid, None].iterator
        if cutlass.const_expr(via_u8):
            cute.arch.store(cute.recast_ptr(dst, dtype=Uint8), v.bitcast(Uint8))
        else:
            cute.arch.store(dst, v)

    @cute.jit
    def run(out: cute.Tensor):
        kernel(out).launch(grid=(1, 1, 1), block=(32, 1, 1))

    return run


print("nvidia-cutlass-dsl", importlib.metadata.version("nvidia-cutlass-dsl"))
for dtype, via_u8 in (
    (Float32, False),
    (BFloat16, False),
    (Uint8, False),
    (Int8, False),
    (Float8E4M3FN, False),
    (Float8E5M2, False),
    (Float8E4M3FN, True),
):
    t = cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(dtype, (32, N), stride=(N, 1), assumed_align=32)
    name = f"{dtype.__name__:13s} {'bitcast->u8' if via_u8 else 'direct'}"
    try:
        cute.compile(make(dtype, via_u8), t)
        print(f"  {name}: ok")
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        msg = " ".join(str(e).split())
        key = "unrealized_conversion_cast"
        print(f"  {name}: FAILED ({key if key in msg else msg[:200]})")
```

Output on 4.8.0:

```
nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0
  Float32       direct: ok
  BFloat16      direct: ok
  Uint8         direct: ok
  Int8          direct: ok
  Float8E4M3FN  direct: FAILED (unrealized_conversion_cast)
  Float8E5M2    direct: FAILED (unrealized_conversion_cast)
  Float8E4M3FN  bitcast->u8: ok
```

**Expected behavior**
A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen.

`cute.arch.store(ptr, fp8_vector)` lowers to a vector store of the packed bytes, the same as the `Uint8` bitcast path. If fp8 vectors are intentionally unsupported, the DSL should raise a clear error at trace time, not an ICE in libNVVM.

**Environment details (please complete the following information):**
 - Environment location: [Bare-metal, Docker, Cloud(specify cloud provider)] 

 - Environment location: Bare-metal
 - GPU: NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a), driver 610.43.02
 - OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (aarch64), Python 3.12.13
 - nvidia-cutlass-dsl: 4.8.0

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here.

items.title: torch.compile silently drops a custom autograd.Function backward when graph returns a view of its output
items.author: man2machine
items.body_excerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug


### Description

When a compiled graph returns a further view of a custom `autograd.Function`'s output, and that output is itself a view of a graph input, the Function's backward is skipped. There is no error; the gradient is wrong.

#102970 (fixed in #102992) covers the direct case. AOTAutograd classifies an output that aliases a graph input as `OutputType.custom_function_view`, and traces its custom backward, when the output's own `grad_fn` is a custom Function (`BackwardCFunction` / `CppFunction`). A view of that output (for example `fn.apply(x).unsqueeze(0)`) has an ordinary view `grad_fn`, so `collect_metadata_analysis.py` classifies it `alias_of_input` instead. `AliasOfInputHandler` then regenerates it from the input at runtime (`gen_alias_from_base`), so its autograd history is plain views of the input and the custom backward never runs.

The real-world trigger I encountered is DTensor's public gradient-hint API: `DTensor.from_local(x, mesh, (Replicate(),)).to_local(grad_placements=(Partial(),))`. It is identity in the forward (`view_as`) and all-reduces the gradient in the backward, i.e. Megatron's "copy to model parallel region" (`f`) operator. Applied to a compiled module's input and followed by views (unsqueeze, expand, indexing) before a graph break, the all-reduce is silently dropped. Graph breaks here are common: for example an FSDP2-wrapped submodule inside the compiled module, whose hooks are dynamo-disabled. We hit this in a model-parallel MoE, where a compiled transformer block's input fans out to per-rank submodules: the input's gradient came out at exactly 1/world_size.

The custom Function's backward probably needs to be honored for any output whose view chain passes through a custom Function, not only when the output's own `grad_fn` is the Function.

### Reproduction

Standalone, CPU only, imports only torch (attached: `aot_custom_function_view_repro.py`).
- `python aot_custom_function_view_repro.py`: four single-process cases with `aot_eager` and
  `inductor`.
- `python aot_custom_function_view_repro.py --dtensor`: also the DTensor version, 2 processes over
  gloo.

Cases:
- `returns_function_output` (the #102992 case): correct.
- `returns_view_of_function_output`: wrong.
- `view_then_graph_break`: wrong.
- `view_consumed_inside_graph` (control, a non-view op consumes the view inside the graph):
  correct.

Script to reproduce the bug:
```python
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Created on Sun Oct 11 17:38:19 2026

@author: Shahir

Standalone reproduction (imports only torch): torch.compile drops a custom autograd.Function's
backward when a compiled graph returns a *further view* of the Function's output, and that output is
itself a view of a graph input.

pytorch/pytorch#102970 (fixed by #102992) covered the direct case: AOTAutograd classifies an output
that aliases a graph input as OutputType.custom_function_view (and traces its custom backward) when
the output's own grad_fn is a custom Function (BackwardCFunction / CppFunction). A view of that
output has an ordinary view grad_fn (e.g. UnsqueezeBackward0), so it is classified alias_of_input
instead and regenerated from the input at runtime (AliasOfInputHandler, gen_alias_from_base): its
autograd history becomes plain views of the input, and the custom backward is skipped. No error,
wrong gradient.

Real-world trigger: DTensor.from_local(x, mesh, (Replicate(),)).to_local(grad_placements=(Partial(),))
is identity in the forward (view_as) and all-reduces the gradient in the backward (the Megatron "f"
operator). Applied to a compiled module's input and followed by views (unsqueeze, expand, indexing)
before a graph break (e.g. an FSDP2-wrapped submodule, whose hooks are dynamo-disabled), the
all-reduce is silently dropped.

Usage:
    python aot_custom_function_view_repro.py            # single process, CPU
    python aot_custom_function_view_repro.py --dtensor  # also the DTensor version, 2 processes, gloo, CPU

Expected (eager) vs observed under torch.compile on torch 2.12: the cases marked "gap" give the
gradient without the custom backward's effect.
"""

import sys

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
import torch.multiprocessing as mp


class ScaleGradientIdentity(torch.autograd.Function):
    """
    Identity forward returning a view of the input (as DTensor's from_local / to_local do); the
    backward doubles the gradient, standing in for an all-reduce over 2 ranks.
    """

    @staticmethod
    def forward(ctx, x):
        return x.view_as(x)

    @staticmethod
    def backward(ctx, grad):
        return grad * 2


def returns_function_output(x):
    # Covered by #102992: the graph output's grad_fn is the custom Function
    return ScaleGradientIdentity.apply(x)


def returns_view_of_function_output(x):
    # Gap: the graph output is a view of the custom Function's output

items.title: [CPU][MKLDNN] FP8 _scaled_mm with K=0 can return uninitialized output under torch.compile
items.author: yoshua2077
items.body_excerpt:
### Bug description

On an x86 CPU with AMX INT8 and MKLDNN enabled, the CPU FP8 `_scaled_mm_v2` zero-dimension test fails under `torch.compile`, while eager execution passes.

For `M=32, K=0, N=32`, the operands have shapes `[32, 0] @ [0, 32]`. The expected result is a **nonempty `[32, 32]` tensor filled with zeros**. Instead, compiled execution returns varying garbage values, including NaNs (e.g., 478/1024 mismatched elements). This is a silent correctness issue, not a GPU computation issue.

### Reproduction

On an x86 CPU exposing AMX INT8, with PyTorch built with MKLDNN and `torch.backends.mkldnn.enabled == True`:

```bash
pytest -vs --tb=long   test/test_scaled_matmul_cuda.py::TestFP8MatmulCPU::test_zero_dim_tensorwise_which_dim_zero_1_use_torch_compile_True_cpu
```

The existing test uses FP8 E4M3 inputs, scalar FP32 scales, and BF16 output. It compares the result against a regular FP32 matmul.

Observed:
- `use_torch_compile=False`: PASS; output is all zeros.
- `use_torch_compile=True`: FAIL with nonzero/NaN results, varying between runs.
- Disabling MKLDNN before running the compiled case makes it PASS.

### Root cause (source-level investigation)

1. Eager `_scaled_mm_v2` CPU execution handles `M == 0 || K == 0 || N == 0` explicitly, including `out.zero_()` for `K == 0`: [ScaledBlas.cpp](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/aten/src/ATen/native/ScaledBlas.cpp).
2. The Inductor lowering of a supported `_scaled_mm_v2` configuration can select the existing `aten._scaled_mm.out` (v1) extern kernel: [mm.py](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/torch/_inductor/kernel/mm.py). The generated code preallocates `empty_strided_cpu((32, 32), ...)` and passes it as `out`.
3. The v1 CPU `_scaled_mm_out_cpu` selects `mkldnn_scaled_mm` when MKLDNN is enabled, scales are scalar, and the CPU supports AMX INT8 (for same-dtype inputs). **It does not exclude zero-numel operands**.
4. The PyTorch `mkldnn_scaled_mm` wrapper has no `K == 0` zero-initialization. In the vendored upstream oneDNN v3.12 implementation, x64 BRGEMM rejects zero-dimensional memories ([brgemm_matmul.cpp](https://github.com/uxlfoundation/oneDNN/blob/v3.12/src/cpu/x64/matmul/brgemm_matmul.cpp)), while the reference matmul's `execute_ref` returns `status::success` on zero-dim source/weights/destination **without writing the destination** ([ref_matmul.cpp](https://github.com/uxlfoundation/oneDNN/blob/v3.12/src/cpu/matmul/ref_matmul.cpp)). This explains how the previously uninitialized nonempty output can be returned unchanged. The exact primitive selected in the failing process was not independently logged.

### Suggested fix

Constrain the MKLDNN fast-path eligibility in `_scaled_mm_out_cpu`:

```cpp
if (at::globalContext().userEnabledMkldnn() &&
    scale_a.numel() == 1 &&
    scale_b.numel() == 1 &&
    mat1.numel() != 0 &&
    mat2.numel() != 0) {
    // existing AMX dispatch / mkldnn_scaled_mm
}
```

This preserves the optimized MKLDNN route for nonempty matrices and sends zero-numel cases to the existing CPU `_scaled_mm_out_cpu_emulated` fallback, which correctly uses `at::matmul` for `K=0`.

### Validation and environment

Reproduced on a PyTorch 2.14.0-derived downstream CPU build on x86 with AMX INT8, MKLDNN enabled, using upstream-equivalent `ScaledBlas.cpp`/oneDNN logic before the fix. After applying only this dispatch guard and rebuilding `libtorch_cpu.so`, the original failing case passed and the six CPU zero-dim combinations (`M/K/N=0` × eager/compile) all passed.

I have **not** independently reproduced the failure on an official upstream wheel; however, the affected unguarded MKLDNN branch is also present in the upstream `main` source. The issue is independent of the CUDA/ROCm GPU backend, despite the test filename.

items.title: [Feature Request] Generalize the compile-during-graph-capture guard in Dynamo to non-CUDA accelerators
items.author: WangJieCS
items.body_excerpt:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

`torch/_dynamo/convert_frame.py` has a guard in `trace_frame()` that raises a
clear `TorchRuntimeError` when a user tries to JIT compile during graph capture
(e.g. inside a CUDA Graph). This matters: compiling during stream capture is
illegal, and without the guard the user hits an opaque driver error.
Today the guard is hardcoded to CUDA:
```python
if (
    torch.cuda.is_available()
    and hasattr(torch._C, "_cuda_isCurrentStreamCapturing")
    and not isinstance(torch._C._cuda_isCurrentStreamCapturing, type)
    and torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()
    and not _in_hop_compile()
):
    raise exc.TorchRuntimeError(
        "torch.compile cannot JIT compile during CUDA graph capture. "
        "Execute warmup iterations outside of CUDA graph capture to trigger "
        "compilation, then capture the graph after compilation has completed."
    )
Third-party accelerators (e.g. XPU, NPU) that support graph capture therefore
get no such protection: the compile-during-capture condition is silently
missed and the user hits a raw backend error instead of an actionable message.
Pitch / Proposed solution
Generalize the guard to reuse the existing accelerator abstraction:
accel = torch.accelerator.current_accelerator()
if accel is not None and not _in_hop_compile():
    device_module = torch.get_device_module(accel)
    if (
        device_module.is_available()
        and hasattr(device_module, "is_current_stream_capturing")
        and device_module.is_current_stream_capturing()
    ):
        accel_name = accel.type.upper()
        raise exc.TorchRuntimeError(
            f"torch.compile cannot JIT compile during {accel_name} graph capture. "
            "Execute warmup iterations outside of graph capture to trigger "
            "compilation, then capture the graph after compilation has completed."
        )
Design choices:
- Use torch.get_device_module(accel) + a hasattr capability probe instead
  of requiring each backend to add a new DeviceInterface method. Any backend
  whose torch.<type> module exposes is_current_stream_capturing is covered
  automatically; backends that don't expose it are safely skipped.
- Derive the name from accel.type.upper() rather than
  device_module.__name__ (which for e.g. torch_npu would produce the wrong
  TORCH_NPU).
- Keep device_module.is_available() so the "compiled in but unavailable at
  runtime" case is skipped exactly as before.

### Alternatives

- CUDA behavior is unchanged; CPU is unaffected (no accelerator -> skip).
- Pure refactoring of an existing guard; no new public API.
- Tests: make test_compile_during_capture_errors device-generic via
  instantiate_device_type_tests so it runs on cuda/xpu/mtia/npu.

### Additional context

Add is_current_stream_capturing to DeviceInterface (a new capability
  method). More formal, but forces every backend to implement a new method.
  The get_device_module + hasattr approach is lighter-weight and follows
  the capability-probe pattern already used elsewhere in Dynamo.
