items.title: Tier-aware prefix scoring follow-ups from #2587
items.author: Jeffwan
items.body_excerpt:
Follow-up to #2587. Tracking the open items from @varungup90's [review](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/pull/2587#pullrequestreview-5463866402).

- [ ] Tier is only set when a (prefix, pod) entry is created, and `ProcessBlockRemoved` drops the pod whatever tier is removed. With CPU offload, vLLM copies a block to CPU while the GPU copy is still there, so `Stored(GPU) → Stored(CPU) → Removed(GPU)` ends with the pod removed instead of scored as CPU. Just overwriting `Medium` doesn't work either, since blocks still on GPU would score as CPU. Plan: track the set of tiers per (prefix, pod) and score with the best one.
- [ ] Decide whether removals should also be scoped by `group_idx`.
- [ ] Fix the `DecodeEventBatch` doc comment. vLLM sends one `EventBatch` per message (`[ts, [map events], dp_rank]`), not one event per message.
- [ ] Add a decoder test fixture in that shape.
- [ ] Share the optional-field parsing between `parseBlockStoredArray` and `parseEventMap`.
- [ ] From @bolubo: should `MatchPrefix` weight the longest match instead of taking the max weighted score?

No impact without offloading, since GPU and empty `medium` both weigh 1.0.

items.title: [CI] Installation E2E test step grew from ~9 min to ~41 min since July
items.author: Jeffwan
items.body_excerpt:
**Area:** Testing (E2E)

## Summary

In the `Installation Tests` workflow, the `Run installation e2e tests` step went from 9m15s in mid-July to 40m36s now, and the whole workflow from about 20 minutes to 54. The `installation-test` job has a 75-minute timeout.

Measured on two runs of the same workflow:

- July 13: https://github.com/Jeffwan/aibrix/actions/runs/29281096831/job/86923371188
- October 8, `a228471` (main at #2930): https://github.com/Jeffwan/aibrix/actions/runs/37735233267/job/113174859334

## Numbers

| | Jul 13 | Oct 8 |
|---|---|---|
| Whole workflow | 20.5 min | 54 min |
| `Run installation e2e tests` step | 9m15s | 40m36s |
| Test packages | 1 (`./test/e2e`) | 13 |
| Top-level tests | 44 | 180 |
| Sum of test time | 486s | 2,123s |
| Compile time before the first test | 47s | 3m08s |

October 8 time per package. All packages run one after another (`go test -p 1`):

| Package | Time |
|---|---|
| gateway/routing | 527s |
| controller/roleset | 360s |
| controller/stormservice | 257s |
| gateway/pd | 218s |
| controller/podset | 206s |
| controller/modeladapter | 169s |
| controller/modelclaim | 163s |
| controller/raycluster | 117s |
| controller/modelwarmup | 46s |
| gateway/api | 32s |
| controller/modelrouter | 25s |
| controller/autoscaling (+ external-metrics) | ~5s |

## Why it grew (about +31 min)

### 1. New controller lifecycle E2E tests: about +19 min

Controller tests went from about 204s (only `TestRoleSetInPlaceUpdate`) to 1,348s. Every new package runs on the same kind cluster, one after another, so each one adds its full time to the step.

| Change | Package time now |
|---|---|
| StormService E2E (#2733, Sep 16) | 257s |
| PodSet lifecycle E2E (#2751, Sep 20) | 206s |
| ModelAdapter E2E no longer skipped (#2657, Sep 3) | 169s |
| ModelClaim E2E (#2460 Jul 18, expanded through #2929 Oct 8) | 163s |
| RayClusterFleet lifecycle E2E (#2753, Sep 20) | 117s |
| ModelWarmup E2E (#2769, Oct 2) | 46s |
| ModelRouter lifecycle E2E (#2743, Sep 19) | 25s |
| RoleSet historical-node (#2628) and drain (#2736) tests enabled in CI | roleset 202s → 360s |

### 2. Gateway tests: about +8 min

Gateway tests went from about 282s to 777s.

- **Each request to the mock is about 3.3× slower (#2383, Jul 14).** That change turned on capacity-aware latency in the mock by default. A request with no `max_tokens` now sleeps about 0.03s + 2ms × `randint(10, 500)` output tokens. That averages about 0.55s, where it used to be a fixed 0.2s.
  - 30 pod-discovery requests: 6.3s → 20.8s.
  - The 8 routing tests present in both runs: 163s → 351s in total. `TestRandomRouting` went 21s → 67s; the VTC tests went from about 21s to 52–61s.
- **New tests:**
  - power-of-two routing: 137s
  - PD failure, bucketing and watchdog tests: `gateway/pd` is 218s now
  - backend-request and API endpoint tests

### 3. Build overhead: about +4 min

#2676 (Sep 8) split the suite into packages and added `go test -p 1`. The `-p` flag limits concurrent compile actions as well as test binaries, so all compilation is now serial:

- compile time before the first test: 47s → 3m08s
- about 5–9s of compiling and linking before each of the 13 packages

I want to write my own fused fp16xfp16 gemm kernel with CUTE, but I can not find a tutorial/sample code with a performance comparable to cublas. 

I noticed there are some tutorials in https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/tree/main/examples/cute/tutorial, which has fp32xfp32 and int8xint8 gemm. So I wonder whether CUTE can give an official fp16xfp16 gemm kernel with good performance, so that I can develop based on that?

comments.author: Bogumil-Sapinski-Mobica
comments.body:
Hi,
I have added PR https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/pull/1843
I added it because:
- torch::kBFloat16 is a best match for bf16 type
- torch::kBFloat16 is used in pytorch benchmarks (pytorch/benchmarks/static_runtime/test_static_runtime.cc) and unit tests (pythorch/test/cpp/api/functional.cpp TEST_F(FunctionalTest, ELU))
- bf16 is already mapped to kBFloat16 in other place of cutlass (cutlass/python/cutlass/utils/datatypes.py is_torch_available()) in library_to_torch_dict. However it has different value types than _CUTLASS_TYPE_TO_TORCH_TYPE

However I have some doubts:
- as I mentioned in PR description in pytorch/test/cpp/api/support.h void assert_tensor_equal() kBFloat16 type is cast to kFloat32 because some tensor operations are not available for kBFloat16
- at::kBFloat16 is not exposed explicitly in torch namespace in pytorch/torch/csrc/api/include/torch/types.h.

I was not able to run 02_pytorch_extension_grouped_gemm.ipynb with my changes so I have no living proof that it works at least in this example. Any advice how to import pytorch from local repo will be welcome.

### Before submitting

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this request has not been filed yet.

### Problem

Diffusion inference needs row-wise FP8 GEMM with communication overlapped, following the approach of ByteDance's FLUX library. The goal is to reduce time spent waiting for tensor-parallel outputs to be combined.

FlashInfer already has relevant GEMM and collective components. This request is for a supported combination of row-wise scaling and all-reduce overlap.

### Requested outcome

Provide a callable row-wise FP8 GEMM + all-reduce path that starts communicating completed output chunks while other chunks are still being computed.

Handle each rank's quantization scales correctly when combining contributions, and return the summed output on every participating rank.

### Target hardware

SM90 (H100, H200, H20), SM100 (B200, GB200), SM103 (B300, GB300)

### Inference engine

Custom / other

### Affected model or model family

Flux 

### Workload and configuration

- Data type: FP8 with row-wise scaling.
- Hidden sizes requested: 3k, 4k, 6k and 8k.
- Sequence lengths requested: 4k–128k.
- Earlier setup: single-node tensor parallelism on 2, 4 and 8 GPUs.
- The customer says the earlier GPU/model/input context still applies.


### Current workaround

_No response_

### Impact

_No response_

### Acceptance criteria

- Match a reference that dequantizes each rank's inputs, computes its partial GEMM and sums the partial outputs. Include different scales across rows and ranks.
- Verify that every rank receives the complete reduced output. A reduce-scatter-only result is insufficient.
- Cover the agreed shapes and 2/4/8-GPU configurations.
- Demonstrate overlap in a GPU trace.
- Measure full GEMM-plus-communication time, including preparation and synchronization.
- Agree numerical tolerances and a performance threshold from the baseline before declaring completion.

### Related work, dependencies, or suggested scope

PrimsTS already supports scaled FP8 linear operations:
https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/flashinfer/prims_ts/gemm/api.py

The existing CuTe DSL GEMM + two-shot all-reduce implementation does not expose runtime row/channel scale tensors in its call signature:

https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/2359

items.title: [BUG] CuTe DSL: export_to_c fails for a --gpu-arch other than the current GPU's
items.author: hwanseoc
items.body_excerpt:
### Which component has the problem?

CuTe DSL

### Bug Report

**Describe the bug**

`export_to_c` fails on the plain C path (no `--enable-tvm-ffi`) when the function was compiled for a different arch than the current GPU. For example, `--gpu-arch sm_90a` on a B200:

```text
JIT session error: Symbols not found: [ _cuKernelGetAttribute, _cudaDeviceGetAttribute, _cudaFuncSetAttribute, _cudaGetDevice, _cudaKernelSetAttributeForDevice, _cudaLaunchKernelEx, _cudaLibraryGetKernel, _cudaLibraryLoadData ]
error: Error dumping object file: Failed to dump object file with PIC relocation
```

The same export works for the native arch, and it also works if I load the runtime libraries `RTLD_GLOBAL` first. My guess is that no execution engine gets built for an arch the GPU can't run, so `libcute_dsl_runtime.so` never gets loaded before the object dump.

**Steps/Code to reproduce bug**

```python
import ctypes, sys, tempfile

import cuda.bindings.driver as cuda
import cutlass
import cutlass.cute as cute
from cutlass.cute.runtime import make_fake_stream


@cute.kernel
def noop_kernel(x: cutlass.Int32):
    pass


@cute.jit
def noop(x: cutlass.Int32, stream: cuda.CUstream):
    noop_kernel(x).launch(grid=(1, 1, 1), block=(32, 1, 1), stream=stream)


if "--preload" in sys.argv:
    for lib in cute.runtime.find_runtime_libraries(enable_tvm_ffi=False):
        ctypes.CDLL(lib, mode=ctypes.RTLD_GLOBAL)
fn = cute.compile(noop, cutlass.Int32(0), make_fake_stream(), options="--gpu-arch sm_90a")
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    fn.export_to_c(tmp, "noop", function_prefix="noop")
print(f"cutlass-dsl {cutlass.__version__}: exported", flush=True)
```

```console
$ python repro.py
JIT session error: Symbols not found: [ _cuKernelGetAttribute, ... ]
$ python repro.py --preload
cutlass-dsl 4.8.0: exported
```

**Expected behavior**

`export_to_c` works for any `--gpu-arch` the compiler accepts, with no manual preloading.

**Environment details (please complete the following information):**
 - Environment location: Bare-metal
 - nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0 and 4.7.0 (cu13), cuda-python 13.4.1
 - B200, driver 580.159.03, Ubuntu 22.04, Python 3.12

**Additional context**

#2859 had the same error on the TVM-FFI path and was fixed in 4.3.3; the TVM-FFI path does export cross-arch now. The plain C path still fails. Workaround: preload `cute.runtime.find_runtime_libraries()` with `RTLD_GLOBAL`.

items.title: [BUG] SM90 TMA GEMM mainloops rely on elect_one_sync() electing lane 0 (TMA issuer vs. PipelineTmaAsync is_leader)
items.author: builtin-pb
items.body_excerpt:
### Which component has the problem?

CUTLASS C++

### Bug Report

**Describe the bug**

Most SM90 TMA GEMM mainloop collectives work only if `elect.sync` elects lane 0. Paths and lines are at main `0b55a2f`.

Two threads are chosen by different rules.

**The TMA issuer is the elected lane.** These collectives call `producer_acquire` and issue the TMA copies only inside `if (lane_predicate)`, where `lane_predicate = cute::elect_one_sync()`, that is, `elect.sync` with a full mask:

| Collective (`include/cutlass/gemm/collective/`) | elect / `producer_acquire` lines |
|---|---|
| `sm90_mma_tma_gmma_ss_warpspecialized.hpp` | 320 / 374 |
| `sm90_mma_tma_gmma_ss_warpspecialized_fp8.hpp` | 318 / 372 |
| `sm90_mma_tma_gmma_rs_warpspecialized.hpp` | 401 / 457 |
| `sm90_sparse_mma_tma_gmma_ss_warpspecialized.hpp` | 415 / 458 |
| `sm90_sparse_mma_tma_gmma_ss_warpspecialized_fp8.hpp` | 426 / 469 |
| `sm90_mma_array_tma_gmma_ss_warpspecialized.hpp` | 370 / 425 |
| `sm90_mma_array_tma_gmma_ss_warpspecialized_fp8.hpp` | 368 / 422 |
| `sm90_mma_array_tma_gmma_ss_warpspecialized_fp8_blockwise_scaling.hpp` | 463 / 543 |

The non-warp-specialized `sm90_mma_tma_gmma_ss.hpp` (lines 365 and 504) and the SM90 implicit-GEMM conv collective (`conv/collective/sm90_implicit_gemm_gmma_ss_warpspecialized.hpp:558–559, 612`) have the same pattern.

**The producer's arrival comes from warp-group thread 0.** `PipelineTmaAsync::producer_acquire` performs `arrive_and_expect_tx` only when `params_.is_leader` is set (`include/cutlass/pipeline/sm90_pipeline.hpp:533–535`, and 555–557 in the token overload). This arrival is the stage's only producer arrival. The kernels set `is_leader = warp_group_thread_idx == 0`:
- `sm90_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:324`;
- `sm90_gemm_tma_warpspecialized_cooperative.hpp:471`;
- `sm90_gemm_tma_warpspecialized_pingpong.hpp:463`;
- the array cooperative and pingpong kernels, lines 522 and 531;
- `sm90_mma_tma_gmma_ss.hpp:334`.

The mainloop warp is warp 0 of the producer warp group, so warp-group thread 0 is its lane 0.

**Why lane 0 matters.** PTX ISA 9.4 (§9.7.15.15, `elect.sync`) promises only that the election is deterministic, with the same leader for the same `membermask` every time. It does not say which lane. If another lane were elected:
- that lane would call `producer_acquire` without being the leader, so nothing arrives on the full barrier;
- lane 0 would not enter the `if` at all;
- the TMA's complete-tx would only drive the transaction count negative.

The phase would never complete. Consumers would block in `consumer_wait`, then the producer in `producer_acquire` once every stage is used, and the kernel would hang.

The kernels run today, so current hardware evidently elects lane 0 here. The code also states that intent:
- `sm90_mma_tma_gmma_ss.hpp:356` says "Set predicate for the lowest lane_id in the warp";
- `sm90_pipeline.hpp:286` says "We have exactly one thread elected in the Producer as the 'leader'";
- CuTe's fallback without `elect.sync` returns `(threadIdx.x % 32) == 0` (`include/cute/arch/cluster_sm90.hpp:197`).

**Unaffected collectives.** Some collectives call `producer_acquire` from all 32 lanes and issue TMA only from the elected lane, so lane 0 always arrives:
- the mixed-input collectives (`sm90_mma_tma_gmma_rs_warpspecialized_mixed_input.hpp:684/694`, and the array variant at 774/784);
- the non-array FP8 blockwise collective (577/587–588).

The epilogue's TMA loads are also unaffected, because one elected lane both posts the expect-tx and issues the copy.

**Steps/Code to reproduce bug**

Found by reading the source against the PTX ISA. There is no runtime reproduction.

**Expected behavior**

The lane that issues the TMA loads is the lane that arrives with the expected bytes. In-tree code already derives the leader from the election:
- on the same `PipelineTmaAsync`, `examples/88_hopper_fmha/kernel/fmha_kernel_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:205, 210` and `sm120_gemm_tma_warpspecialized_cooperative_asymmetric_dma.hpp:443, 448`;
- in the SM100 kernels, e.g. `sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:465`.

For the SM90 kernels, that would be:

```cpp
mainloop_pipeline_params.is_leader =
    warp_group_role == WarpGroupRole::Producer &&
    producer_warp_role == ProducerWarpRole::Mainloop && lane_predicate;
```

Restrict it to the mainloop warp. The `MainloopAux` warp in the blockwise kernels also has the Producer role and calls `producer_acquire` from all lanes. Giving it a leader would add a second `arrive_and_expect_tx` per stage.

This works because the kernel's `elect_one_sync()` and the collective's later one use the same full mask, and PTX guarantees the same leader for the same mask. Two more changes go with it:
- `sm90_mma_tma_gmma_ss.hpp` would need `lane_predicate` computed before `is_leader` is set;
- the debug-build `brkpt` checks in `producer_acquire` (`sm90_pipeline.hpp:542–544` and 564–566), which fire when the leader is not lane 0, would need to go. They already assume lane 0 for the FMHA and SM120 kernels above.

The alternative is to gate the TMA issue in each affected collective on lane 0 instead of `elect_one_sync()`.

**Environment details**

Source analysis; no runtime environment involved. Hopper (sm_90a).

items.title: [Store] Does Mooncake store plan to support awareness of layers, chunk ordering, and TP?
items.author: Hadigan
items.body_excerpt:
It looks like the current Mooncake store does not have awareness of layer granularity, chunk order (earlier vs. later chunks), or TP ranks. This can cause problems during cache eviction:

1. The store might evict KVs for only some layers, forcing prefill to recompute all layer KVs for those tokens.
2. The store might evict the KVs corresponding to the earliest chunk(s) of a token sequence, forcing prefill to recompute KVs for all chunks/tokens.
3. The store might evict KVs produced by some TP ranks, forcing all TP ranks to recompute KVs.

I think the Mooncake store should be aware of layers, chunk ordering, and TP. On eviction, it should evict a token’s KV caches for all layers and for all TP ranks together (i.e., keep KV state complete per token). 
From the chunk-order perspective, eviction policies should prefer removing KVs for later chunks first rather than evicting early-chunk KVs that make prefill expensive.

items.title: DTensor: torch._foreach_norm(..., dtype=...) crashes in sharding propagation
items.author: ppwwyyxx
items.body_excerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

  ```python
     import torch
     import torch.distributed as dist
     from torch.distributed.tensor import Shard, distribute_tensor, init_device_mesh

     dist.init_process_group(backend='gloo', init_method='tcp://127.0.0.1:29501',
                             world_size=1, rank=0)
     mesh = init_device_mesh('cpu', (1,))
     x = distribute_tensor(torch.arange(1, 6, dtype=torch.float32), mesh, [Shard(0)])

     norms = torch._foreach_norm([x], 2.0, dtype=torch.float64)
     print('OK:', norms[0].full_tensor())
     dist.destroy_process_group()
```

  Actual behavior (torch 2.14.0)

   ```
     RuntimeError: '>=' not supported between instances of 'torch.dtype' and 'int'

     Sharding propagation failed for aten._foreach_norm.Scalar([DTensorSpec(
     mesh=DeviceMesh((1,), 'cpu', stride=((),)), placements=(Shard(dim=0),),
     tensor_meta=TensorMeta(shape=torch.Size([5]), stride=(1,), dtype=torch.float32), ...)],
     2.0, torch.float64) on None)
   ```

   Full inner traceback: vector_norm_single_dim_strategy → _infer_reduction_dims(dim, ndim) → normalize_dims → normalize_dim → dim if dim >= 0 else ... where dim is actually torch.float64.

   Expected behavior

   Returns per-tensor float64 norms (torch 2.12.1 output):

```
     OK: tensor(7.4162, dtype=torch.float64)
```

## Root cause

The two ops sharing `vector_norm_single_dim_strategy` have incompatible argument layouts:

- `linalg_vector_norm.default(Tensor self, Scalar ord=2, int[]? dim=None, bool keepdim=False, *, ScalarType? dtype=None)` — position 2 is `dim`
- `_foreach_norm.Scalar(Tensor[] self, Scalar ord=2, ScalarType? dtype=None)` — position 2 is `dtype` (positional-capable, no `*` marker)

`vector_norm_single_dim_strategy` (`torch/distributed/tensor/_ops/_math_ops.py`) unconditionally does:

```python
dim = args_schema[2] if len(args_schema) > 2 else None
```

so `_foreach_norm`'s `dtype` is fed into `normalize_dim()`. This appears since #179201 cc @awgu @wanchaol @fegin @fduwjj @wz337 @wconstab @d4l3k @pragupta @msaroufim @dcci @aditvenk @weifengpy @kapilsh @tianyu-l @XilunWu @SherlockNoMad @anshul-si .

### Versions

torch 2.14

items.title: SM120 (RTX PRO 6000) MoE backend gaps: MoeConfig.backend schema missing MegaMoE entries, and no EP-capable path for this hardware
items.author: ItamarTerem
items.body_excerpt:
Hi TensorRT-LLM team,
Deploying a large MoE model (Kimi-K2.7-Code-NVFP4, 384 experts) on 8x RTX PRO 6000 (SM120) via the pytorch backend, trtllm-serve, version 1.3.0rc20. Two related findings we wanted to raise:

1. MoeConfig.backend's pydantic Literal doesn't include MEGAMOE_CUTEDSL/MEGAMOE_DEEPGEMM, even though create_moe.py's dispatch logic already handles both as real branches. Setting moe_config.backend: MEGAMOE_CUTEDSL in extra_llm_api_options.yaml fails pydantic validation before create_moe.py is ever reached, even though the underlying backend selection logic supports it. This looks like the config schema hasn't caught up to the dispatch logic yet.
2. More fundamentally: none of the EP-capable MoE backends currently work on SM120 in this build.
 - MEGAMOE_CUTEDSL / MEGAMOE_DEEPGEMM: both explicitly require SM100/SM103 ("MegaMoECuteDsl requires SM100 family (SM100 or SM103); got SM120"), and fall back to CutlassFusedMoE.
 - WIDEEP: not SM-gated, but its GEMM compute still routes through the same CUTLASS kernel that produces silently incorrect output on SM120 in our testing, and additionally hit a binding mismatch in this build (run_moe() is missing value for argument '_37') before we could evaluate EP itself.
 - CUTEDSL (b12x): the only backend we've confirmed produces correct output on SM120, but has no EP support at the flashinfer level (num_local_experts != num_experts raises NotImplementedError in b12x_fused_moe).

Net result: there is currently no correct + EP-capable MoE path for SM120 in this stack, which limits per-GPU memory headroom for large-expert-count models on this hardware class.
Questions:

1. Is SM120 support planned for any of the MegaMoE/WideEP paths, or is SM100/SM103-first prioritization intentional for the near term?
2. Should we file the MoeConfig.backend schema gap as a separate, smaller issue, since that looks like a straightforward fix independent of the larger EP question?
3. Is there a recommended path for SM120 users running large MoE models today, or is CUTEDSL/no-EP the expected configuration for this hardware class in the current release?

Happy to share full repro steps/configs if helpful. Thanks for your work on this — appreciate the pointers.

items.title: [Feature]: Wire SM107 into nvfp4_gemm CuTe DSL dispatcher (cute_dsl_nvfp4_gemm_rubin has no caller)
items.author: farazkh80
items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

`trtllm::cute_dsl_nvfp4_gemm_rubin` (added in #19272) has no caller. The generic `nvfp4_gemm` dispatcher's CuTe DSL backend is still SM100/SM103-only, so SM107 (Rubin) can never select the Rubin NVFP4 CuTe DSL kernel through `nvfp4_gemm`.

## Details

- In `tensorrt_llm/_torch/custom_ops/torch_custom_ops.py` (`NVFP4GemmUnifiedRunner`), the `cutedsl` tactics are only collected when `get_sm_version()` is 100 or 103. On any other SM, an explicit `cutedsl`-only request raises "CuteDSL NVFP4 backend requires SM 100 (B200) or SM 103 (B300)". The `cutedsl` forward branch always builds `CuteDSLNVFP4BlackwellRunner`.
- On SM107 the only NVFP4 CuTe DSL path in use is the locality-domain inplace op (`cute_dsl_nvfp4_gemm_locality_domain_inplace_rubin`), reached from `Linear` when `enable_locality_domains` is set.
- `cute_dsl_nvfp4_gemm_rubin` is registered but unreachable.

## Proposed work

- Add SM107 support to the `nvfp4_gemm` CuTe DSL dispatcher: SM gate, tactic collection, and a forward branch that uses the Rubin runner.
- Make sure the SM100/SM103 path is unchanged.
- Add a test covering SM107 selection through `nvfp4_gemm`.

## References

- Review thread: https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/19272 (comment on `cute_dsl_nvfp4_gemm_rubin`, where the author agreed to a follow-up PR)

items.title: [Tracking][SM100] CuTe DSL W4A16 MoE implementation and follow-ups
items.author: zianglih
items.body_excerpt:
## Scope

@humansand

Track implementation and follow-up work for the SM100-family CuTe DSL NVFP4 MoE path with BF16 activations (`quant_mode="w4a16"`). #4249 captured the original B200 W4A16 feature request; this issue consolidates the implementation, integration, and related follow-ups.

This tracker is limited to work with explicit W4A16 scope. General CuTe DSL / NVFP4 infrastructure and activation quantization are omitted unless they directly enable or modify this path.

Status last verified: 2026-08-22. Checked items are merged or concluded; unchecked items remain open.

## Tracked contract

- **Hardware:** SM100-family CuTe DSL path; validation in the linked PRs covers B200/SM100 and B300/SM103 where documented.
- **Precision:** BF16 activations and block-scaled NVFP4 weights.
- **Path:** `cute_dsl_fused_moe_nvfp4` / `CuteDslMoEWrapper`, including eager and CUDA graph execution plus fused and deterministic finalize modes.
- **Out of scope:** dense W4A16 GEMM implementation, SM12x/b12x kernels, and the TRT-LLM MoE backend. Related SM100 dense work is linked below for context.

## Shared foundations

- [x] #3976 — `feat(moe): add deterministic CuTe DSL NVFP4 finalize mode` — Adds the reusable deterministic `moe_unpermute` path that #4048 explicitly builds on.
- [x] #4192 — `fix(moe): serialize CuTe DSL autotune replay` — Fixes a shared CuTe DSL MoE runner deadlock hazard during selected-tactic replay; this is not W4A16-specific, but applies to the runner reused by W4A16.

## Core implementation

- [x] #4048 — `feat(moe): support BF16 activations in CuTe DSL NVFP4 MoE` — Adds the explicit W4A16 mode, dedicated online NVFP4-to-BF16 weight decode and kernels, runner/API integration, autotuning, fused and deterministic finalize, PDL/CUDA graph support, tests, and B200 evidence.

## Direct follow-ups

- [x] #4394 — `feat(moe): support GeGLU and SiTU in W4A16` — Adds GeGLU-tanh and SiTU, including parameter plumbing and autotune/compiled-kernel cache identities.
- [x] #4558 — `fix(moe): release W4A16 CuTe DSL scratch workspaces` — Removes per-runner scratch retention that can cause multi-GiB serving memory retention/OOMs while preserving eager allocator reuse and CUDA graph ownership. Open draft.
- [x] #4540 — `perf(moe): fold W4A16 SiTU reciprocals` — Replaces trace-time per-element divisions with FP32-rounded reciprocal multiplies and adds controlled B200 evidence. Open.
- [ ] #4366 — `feat(moe): support input-side router weights in CuTe DSL W4A4/W4A16 MoE` — Adds opt-in pre-FC2 router-weight placement for cross-stack numerical alignment. Open.
- [ ] #4678 — `perf(moe): prune score-routing compilation from moe_utils` — Uses source-owned post-topK wrappers to prune unreachable score-routing compilation from the shared SM10x CuTe DSL W4A4/W4A16 `moe_utils` JIT while retaining the existing routing/permutation kernels. Fresh B200 cold first-run wall time drops from 244.03 s to 121.28 s for W4A4 and from 245.19 s to 120.99 s for W4A16; open draft, built on merged #4082.
- [x] #5186 — `perf: reduce split W4A16 routing and output overhead` — Specializes top-k and physical-cluster feature bounds and improves non-fused expert scratch stores, preserving fixed-order FP32 combine. Includes separate fused/non-fused B300 performance tables for 1–8192 tokens. Open draft.
- [x] #5019 — `feat(moe): add CuTe DSL NVFP4 W4A16 MegaMoE` — Adds fused expert-parallel dispatch, FC1/SwiGLU, FC2 and token return with BF16 activations, online NVFP4-to-TMEM weight decode, and fixed-order FP32 combine. Includes CUDA 13.2/B300 performance results for 1–8192 tokens. Open, ready for review.

- [x] #5319 — `perf: optimize CuTe DSL W4A4 and W4A16 unfused finalize` — Shares a vectorized BF16 finalizer with ordered FP32 reduction and overlaps standalone finalize setup with FC2 through PDL. B300 simulated-EP8 results cover 1–16384 tokens: W4A16 improves at 14/15 points, with a 1.22% regression at 8192. Also fixes CUTLASS benchmark finalize-flag forwarding. Open, ready for review (verified 2026-09-18).

- [ ] #6277 — `Add small-shape W4A16 MegaMoE tactics and model benchmarks` — Adds N32 paths and a 16-tactic autotune catalog, plus Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM5 benchmark presets. Preserves activation numerics and deterministic combine. Open, ready for review (verified 2026-10-10).

## SGLang integration

- [x] [sgl-project/sglang#35120](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35120) — `feat: add FlashInfer CuTe DSL NVFP4 W4A16 mode` — Adds opt-in W4A16 dispatch through `CuteDslMoEWrapper(quant_mode="w4a16")`, supports no-A2A and FlashInfer A2A on SM100/SM103, and adds online-quantized Nemotron-3 plus serialized ModelOpt Qwen3 coverage. Open draft; depends on FlashInfer #4048, #4394, and #4558.

- [ ] [sgl-project/sglang#39210](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39210) — `[FlashInfer v0.7.1] Add opt-in NVFP4 W4A16 support to FlashInfer MegaMoE` — Adds opt-in NVFP4 W4A16 to `flashinfer_megamoe` for serialized ModelOpt weights and `nvfp4_online`, reusing [sgl-project/sglang#35120](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35120)'s W4A16 setting. Integrates BF16 activations/EP transport/combine, weight reload, startup autotuning and Kimi K3 SiTU wiring on top of FlashInfer #5019. Open, ready for review (verified 2026-10-10).

## Related dense W4A16 work

- [x] #4466 — `feat: sm100 cute_dsl w4a16 gemm` — Adds a dedicated SM100/SM103 CuTe DSL dense BF16-by-NVFP4 kernel, architecture-specific weight preparation and dispatch, and autotuning. The implementation adapts the W4A16 MoE TCGen05/dequantization design and tactic family while retaining a separate dense ABI and scheduler. #3597 established the earlier public dense API and cuDNN/SM12x foundation. Merged.

- [x] #4686 — `perf(gemm): optimize CuTe DSL W4A16 dense GEMM` — Compiles the SM100/SM103 kernel at O3 and expands all 15 structural tactics across both raster directions. Controlled B300/SM103 A/B/A measured `1.029759x` geometric-mean speedup across the #4

shortlist.title: [good-first-issue] tests: make flaky vllm_bench throughput comparisons reproducible
shortlist.author: maobaolong
shortlist.body_excerpt:
Parent tracker: #5313 · Onboarding: #3372

## Confirmed flaky behavior

`k3-multiprocess-test / vllm / vllm_bench / zmq` changes its throughput verdict without a source update:

| Build #5340, September 29, 2026 (UTC) | Result |
| --- | --- |
| [Original job](https://buildkite.com/lmcache/k3-multiprocess-test/builds/5340#01a0eab1-a517-4a38-8163-b0ec7cfaff63) | LMCache throughput **7.34% slower** than baseline; fails the 5% limit |
| [Retry](https://buildkite.com/lmcache/k3-multiprocess-test/builds/5340#01a0eaba-4671-4f79-a910-4a02cfa0cadf) | LMCache throughput **0.62% faster** than baseline; passes |

Both are `dev` builds of **`9e8226dd49728769843bf6f586b00b33ab616125`**, with no PR-base merge, vLLM **`0.30.1rc1.dev244+g0da126676`**, and torch **`2.13.0+cu130`**. Both baseline and LMCache completed all 50 requests with 500400 input tokens. This is an intermittent benchmark verdict, not an installation failure.

The inputs are not reproducible across those attempts: the original uses seed `1790644335`, the retry `1790645482`. Each attempt uses the same seed for its own baseline/LMCache pair, but the default `RANDOM_SEED` comes from `date +%s`. The seed change is a confirmed confounder; it is **not proven to be the sole cause** of the throughput fluctuation.

## Bounded good-first task

Make this benchmark's inputs reproducible across retries, and make the comparison auditable. This is the first test-harness improvement for the confirmed flake, not a production performance optimization.

1. Replace the clock-derived default seed with a documented stable default; continue honoring an explicit `RANDOM_SEED` override.
2. Save a small comparison manifest next to `baseline.json` and `lmcache.json`: effective seed, model, request count and lengths, actual checkout SHA, installed vLLM/torch versions, and the two throughput values/verdict. Keep any new diagnostics local to this workload.
3. Preserve separate attempt results when used in CI. Follow the existing result-directory/cleanup conventions, and ensure the manifest is accessible in the job log or a public Buildkite artifact rather than merely naming a container-local file.
4. Add focused CPU-only regression coverage using stub benchmark commands: default seed is repeatable, both sides receive it, an override is honored, and success/failure summaries retain the actual numbers.

Keep the 5% throughput limit, request/token checks, and cache-retrieval validation. Do not add blanket retries, remove assertions, or present a fixed seed as proof of a resolved performance issue. #5227 already added retry mitigation; this task addresses reproducibility within the workload.

Starting points, checked at `42be9c7439a1eb0b17bf6b7565a894a9743fd052`:

- [Workload seed and result comparison](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/42be9c7439a1eb0b17bf6b7565a894a9743fd052/.buildkite/k3_tests/multiprocess/scripts/workloads/vllm/vllm-bench.sh).
- [Result cleanup/copying](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/42be9c7439a1eb0b17bf6b7565a894a9743fd052/.buildkite/k3_tests/multiprocess/scripts/cleanup.sh).
- [Buildkite step and existing retry policy](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/42be9c7439a1eb0b17bf6b7565a894a9743fd052/.buildkite/k3_tests/multiprocess/pipeline.yml).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Default inputs are identical across attempts; explicit overrides still work.
- [ ] A reviewer can recover both results, the effective inputs, versions, and verdict from public job output/artifacts.
- [ ] Stubbed CPU coverage exercises default/override and passing/failing results.
- [ ] GPU validation reports first-attempt results with a fixed seed; remaining fluctuation is reported as unresolved rather than hidden.
- [ ] Existing behavioral assertions and thresholds remain effective.

## Reproduce the CI workload

The evidence below comes from CI; this issue does not claim a local GPU reproduction. Use a dedicated Linux x86_64 GPU test host with Docker and NVIDIA Container Toolkit, two available CUDA GPUs capable of running separate `Qwen/Qwen3-14B` servers, sufficient host RAM for the default 80 GiB LMCache buffer (plus the mock L2 storage for the L2 case), and disk/network access for the image, wheels, and model. CI uses CUDA 13.0, Python 3.12, and a 1 GiB `/dev/shm`. A maintainer can run the GPU validation for a contributor who only has a CPU machine.

These commands build the public CI image recipe, explicitly start Bash, and pin the historical LMCache and vLLM revisions. They are a reproduction recipe, not a fully locked copy of every historical dependency or GPU scheduling condition. Run from a fresh directory; make the actual PR against current `dev`.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache.git
cd LMCache
git checkout 9e8226dd49728769843bf6f586b00b33ab616125
docker build -t lmcache-flake-ci \
  -f .buildkite/k3_harness/ci-base.Dockerfile .
docker run --rm --gpus '"device=0,1"' --shm-size=1g \
  --entrypoint bash \
  -v "$PWD:/workspace/LMCache" -w /workspace/LMCache \
  -e MAX_JOBS=1 \
  -e INFERENCE_ENGINE=vllm \
  -e LMCACHE_REQUEST_TRANSPORT=zmq \
  -e LMCACHE_PR_BASE_MERGE=never \
  -e PINNED_VLLM_VERSION=0.30.1rc1.dev244+g0da126676 \
  -e PINNED_VLLM_ARCHIVE_INDEX_URL=https://wheels.vllm.ai/0da126676e38f5dc1b02b2c4f48dc85f90f5a79f/cu130 \
  lmcache-flake-ci -c '
    set -e
    source /opt/venv/bin/activate
    command -v git uv python3 nvcc gcc g++
    nvidia-smi
    git config --global --add safe.directory /workspace/LMCache
    .buildkite/k3_tests/multiprocess/run.sh vllm_bench
  '
```

Use the linked failed and passed jobs as the initial reproduction pair. For subsequent GPU runs, record the actual checkout SHA, installed package versions, GPU model, input settings, and first-attempt result. A green retry alone does not show that the underlying fluctuation was fixed.

## Claim and contribution rules

This is primarily for a new contributor. Claim **one active sub-issue at a time** by commenting `/claim` here; check existing comments and ass

shortlist.title: [Bug] Disconnected streaming client leaves a zombie request that decodes to max_tokens and floods "state was deleted in TokenizerManager" (regression from #34160 revert)
shortlist.author: wkgcass
shortlist.body_excerpt:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

> Submitted by GLM-5.3

When a streaming client disconnects mid-generation, the scheduler-side request
is never aborted and keeps decoding until `max_tokens`. Every output batch for
that request logs:

```
Received output for rid='...' but the state was deleted in TokenizerManager.
```

at a high rate (observed ~15 lines/s per request, sustained for the entire
remaining generation — in production two zombie requests burned GPU for 15+
minutes and occupied both `--max-running-requests` slots, blocking all new
requests from being scheduled).

Root cause (verified on current `main`):

1. `TokenizerManager.generate_request` has an `except BaseException` cleanup
   that calls `_discard_pending_req_states(obj)`. It was added for failures
   *before* the request reaches the scheduler (e.g. input-length validation),
   but a client disconnect raises `asyncio.CancelledError` — also a
   `BaseException` — so the state of a request that **is running on the
   scheduler** gets popped immediately at disconnect time.

2. The delayed safety net then doesn't fire: `create_abort_task` (attached to
   the `StreamingResponse` as a background task, runs ~2s after teardown)
   calls `abort_request(rid)`, which early-returns on
   `tokenizer_worker_num == 1 and rid not in self.rid_to_state`. The
   `AbortReq` is never dispatched, so the scheduler never learns the client
   is gone and decodes to `max_tokens`; each `BatchStrOutput` for that rid
   hits the deleted-state error path.

This is a regression of 71043b9dbb ("Revert parallel request lifecycle
tracking from #32588", #34160). Before the revert, #32588 handled this
correctly: `_discard_pending_req_states(obj, request_lifecycles)` dispatched
`AbortReq` for every rid whose state had `dispatched == True` **before**
removing the state. The revert deleted the `dispatched` markers and the
abort-then-remove ordering, leaving the orphan window. Presumably not covered
by CI because it requires killing a streaming client mid-generation.

(The `HEALTH_CHECK`-prefixed rid skip next to the error log is a different,
known race — unrelated, see #11925.)

Suggested minimal fix (verified in production, restores the pre-revert
invariant without reintroducing full lifecycle tracking):

1. In `generate_request`, treat cancellation separately and only discard
   state if the request was never dispatched:

```python
        dispatched = False
        try:
            ...
            self._send_one_request(tokenized_obj)
            dispatched = True
            async for response in self._wait_one_response(obj, request):
                yield response
        except (asyncio.CancelledError, GeneratorExit):
            # Client disconnect mid-request: keep the state of a dispatched
            # request so the delayed background abort still finds it; the
            # scheduler's abort echo deletes it cleanly. Discarding here
            # orphans the scheduler-side request, which then decodes to
            # max_tokens.
            if not dispatched:
                self._discard_pending_req_states(obj)
            raise
        except BaseException:
            self._discard_pending_req_states(obj)
            raise
```

2. Add a `force` flag to `abort_request` that bypasses the
   `rid not in self.rid_to_state` early-return, and pass `force=True` from
   `create_abort_task` (the scheduler's `abort_request` handler scans by rid
   prefix and no-ops unknown rids, so force-dispatching is safe — it just
   closes the window where the state was already deleted elsewhere):

```python
    def abort_request(self, rid: str = "", abort_all: bool = False, force: bool = False):
        if not abort_all and not rid:
            ...
            return
        if (
            not abort_all
            and not force
            and get_serving().tokenizer_worker_num == 1
            and rid not in self.rid_to_state
        ):
            return
```

With this patch: disconnect → decode stops within the 2s abort window, zero
error lines; normal streaming completions (`[DONE]`) unaffected.

### Reproduction

Any model; the bug is in the tokenizer-manager layer and is
hardware/model-independent.

1. Launch a server:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model <any-model> --port 30000
```

2. Start a long streaming generation, then kill the client mid-stream:

```bash
curl -sN http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"<any-model>","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Count from 1 to 5000, one number per line."}],"max_tokens":16000,"stream":true}' &
sleep 10 && kill -9 %1
```

**Actual**: `sglang:num_running_reqs` stays 1 and the request decodes until
`max_tokens`; the log floods with the message above (same rid, repeated many
times per second).

**Expected**: the request is aborted shortly after the disconnect (within the
2s background-abort window) and decode stops.

### Environment

- sglang `main` (regression introduced by 71043b9dbb / #34160, still present
  as of a1f9508dd4; no commit has touched `tokenizer_manager.py` since —
  `except BaseException` cleanup and the guard are at current lines ~825
  and ~1952)
- single GPU, TP=1, `--max-running-requests 2`; speculative decoding enabled
  (DSPARK) on our instance, but nothing here is spec-specific
- reproduced and root-caused on a fork whose `tokenizer_manager.py` is
  unmodified upstream code

comments.author: eug3
comments.body:
### Additional production evidence + a working workaround (2x DGX Spark, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4)

We hit this exact bug in production today on **SGLang TP=2 across 2 DGX Spark nodes** (`Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, speculative NEXTN, `--tokenizer-worker-num 1`). Sharing our numbers and a working mitigation in case it helps:

**Observed symptoms (identical to #36333 and #36876):**
- 3 zombie requests accumulated over hours (first at 11:58, then 13:02, then 14:41), each from a client that disconnected mid-stream.
- GPU pinned at ~95% for 2+ hours with **zero completed requests**; `sglang:num_running_reqs` stuck at 3.0.
- Log flooded with `Received output for rid=... but the state was deleted in TokenizerManager` — **~148,000 lines** sustained across hours.
- `POST /abort_request` returned 200 but had **no effect** (confirmed the `abort_request()` early-return: with `tokenizer_worker_num == 1` and `rid not in self.rid_to_state`, the `AbortReq` never reaches the scheduler — exactly as #36333 describes).
- New requests queued behind the zombies; spend/completion never logged for the zombies.

**Our workaround (patched `tokenizer_manager.py` in the running image, verified):**
1. `abort_request()`: removed the early-return when `rid not in self.rid_to_state` — always dispatch `AbortReq` to the scheduler (scheduler-side abort is safe for unknown rids; it scans queues and no-ops when absent).
2. `_handle_batch_output()`: when output arrives for an already-deleted state (orphan), proactively re-send `AbortReq(rid, abort_all=False)` to reap the scheduler-side task.

**Verification:** simulated client disconnect (kill curl 2s into a streaming responses call): `num_running_reqs` → 0 within 10s, GPU → 0%, subsequent requests unaffected. Concurrent test (3 streaming, 2 killed mid-stream, 1 completed): all slots reclaimed, the completed one finished normally. 60s observation window: zero growth of "state was deleted" after the initial reap.

**Note on #36876:** even with the AbortReq reaching the scheduler, `Scheduler.abort_request()` only sets `to_finish = FINISH_ABORT()` for requests found in `[running_batch, last_batch]` — during batch transitions (overlap scheduling / speculative decoding) a request can be in neither, leaving the same zombie. Our orphan-output reap (fix 2) happens to cover that window too, but the two fixes should ideally both land upstream. Happy to provide the full patch or a minimal repro script if useful.

comments.author: hellojiaru
comments.body:
Additional fixed-path validation on 2x GB10 TP2 is now available. We backported both commits from #36418 (`e95ed7b` + the normal-completion correction `6f1a65d`) onto a pinned Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 image.

Before the fix, a client timeout at about 1,205 seconds was followed by `state was deleted in TokenizerManager`, then invalid probabilities, CUDA asserts, Xid 43, and both TP ranks exiting. After the fix, two real TCP disconnects were reclaimed in 2.155 and 2.183 seconds; normal streams immediately afterward completed, and a 28,672-token generation crossed the previous failure point with both ranks at zero restarts/OOM false.

The public reproduction and exact evidence boundary are in `v0.1.2-canary`: https://github.com/hellojiaru/qwen38-flash-next-dual-gb10/releases/tag/v0.1.2-canary

comments.author: shashwat01kothari
comments.body:
**Validation datapoint for the suggested minimal fix: GB10 unified-memory ARM + 27B-NVFP4 + speculative decoding**

Applied the two-part minimal fix from the issue body (the `dispatched` flag + `force` flag on `abort_request`) as a read-only whole-file overlay on a dev build inside the broken window — `0.0.0.dev1+gf825d7293` (after `71043b9`, before `f478b2b`), confirmed broken pre-patch on this build. Nothing new to propose here; this is a datapoint from a topology I didn't see covered in this thread: **single NVIDIA GB10 (124608 MiB unified memory, ARM), TP=1, Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 with DFLASH speculative draft (incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2)**, `--max-running-requests 8`.

**A/B method (reproducible):**

1. Baseline: unpatched, count occurrences of the exact signature line `Received output for rid='...' but the state was deleted in TokenizerManager.` across the full server log — **2692** (4B first, same signature on 27B).
2. Kill-burst: fire 3 in-flight streaming requests, confirm `num_reqs = 3` via `/get_load` at t0, `kill -9` all clients mid-stream (~114 SSE chunks each at kill), watch drain:
   - unpatched: `num_running_reqs` held at 3 until `max_tokens`
   - patched: **3 → 0 in ~5 s**
3. Functional: short `stop|length`-terminated generations complete normally with `[DONE]`; 3/3 soaks clean, **0 Traceback / 0 ERROR** in full-log scans.

**Result: 2692 → 0 error lines, zero zombie decode time, MRR slots released within the 2 s abort window.**

Two notes for triage:

- Our overlay is a strict subset of [#35255](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35255) (merged to main at `f478b2b`) — we don't have the chunked-prefill deferred-abort retry or the abort dedup, which is exactly why we plan to **drop the overlay entirely and rebuild from main ≥ `f478b2b`** rather than keep the local patch.
- The only thing this environment adds is confirmation that the fix holds **with the speculative-decoding draft path active on unified memory** — the disconnect/abort window behaves identically to the non-spec case above.

Happy to share the raw log excerpts and the overlay diff if useful for #35255 or the backport discussion.

comments.author: uzunenes
comments.body:
**Update:** The report below was on v0.5.17, which predates the fix in #35255. We have since upgraded to v0.5.20, which includes it. We will report back only if the orphan request or the detokenizer hang recurs on v0.5.20.

---

We reproduced this issue in production on SGLang 0.5.17 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, TP=2, DSPARK, and 2x NVIDIA H200 NVL GPUs.

In our case, the impact progressed beyond a zombie request:

1. We received repeated `state was deleted in TokenizerManager` messages for an orphan request ID.
2. Approximately one minute later, the detokenizer heartbeat stopped.
3. The `/health` endpoint stopped responding.
4. Kubernetes liveness probes failed and restarted the container.
5. The container exited with code 137, but it was not reported as `OOMKilled`.
6. No CUDA, NCCL, GPU XID, eviction, or Kubernetes OOM event was observed.

Relevant log excerpt:

```text
[2026-09-22 09:31:23] Received output for rid='420d55af8fc244e39843f19ae598a1df' but the state was deleted in TokenizerManager.
[2026-09-22 09:31:23] Received output for rid='420d55af8fc244e39843f19ae598a1df' but the state was deleted in TokenizerManager.

[2026-09-22 09:32:51] Health check failed. Server couldn't get a response from detokenizer for last 20 seconds. tic start time: 09:32:31. last_heartbeat time: 09:32:31
[2026-09-22 09:33:01] Health check failed. Server couldn't get a response from detokenizer for last 20 seconds. tic start time: 09:32:41. last_heartbeat time: 09:32:31

[2026-09-22 09:34:39] SIGTERM received. signum=None frame=None. Draining requests and shutting down...
[2026-09-22 09:34:40] Signal SIGTERM received while health check failed. Force exiting.
```

Kubernetes events:

```text
Warning  Unhealthy  Liveness probe failed: Get "http://<pod-ip>:30000/health": context deadline exceeded
Normal   Killing    Container sglang failed liveness probe, will be restarted
```

This suggests that an orphan request may eventually make the detokenizer unresponsive and cause a full server restart under Kubernetes.

We can provide the launch arguments and full previous-container logs if needed.

comments.author: wangwxxwgnaw
comments.body:
### Additional pinned-v0.5.19 validation: disconnect can leave scheduler work running

Reported by **wangwxxwgnaw**.

Adding an isolated reproduction and before/after datapoint to this existing report. I also checked merged PR #35255: its merge commit is an ancestor of the official v0.5.20 and v0.5.21 tags. The results below concern the pinned v0.5.19 source, not a claim that this defect persists in those newer releases. No production B300/DP4/EP/MTP validation was performed.

#### Source and runtime

- SGLang source: v0.5.19, `0bcd822377da7b5718e674eaf9c870d349424dd1`.
- Original `tokenizer_manager.py` SHA256: `bdfaa4f4f214515f2138a3a82e8215882735490dfa85c271d2c41830b682ad33`.
- One RTX3060 12GB; Qwen3-0.6B; TP1/DP1; tokenizer worker count 1; Triton attention; CUDA graphs disabled; metrics enabled.
- KV/context limit 16,384, max-running 4, chunked-prefill 2,048.
- Compatibility environment: the complete v0.5.19 Python source was overlaid on existing v0.5.17 image dependencies. Torch `2.11.0+cu130`, sglang-kernel `0.4.5`, Triton `3.6.0`, FastAPI `0.141.1`, Uvicorn `0.52.1`; driver `580.178.04`.
- `SGLANG_SKIP_SGL_KERNEL_VERSION_CHECK=1` was required. Installing the required kernel `0.4.6.post1` into these dependencies failed with a Torch ABI mismatch. This is a lifecycle-mechanism experiment, **not validation of the stock v0.5.19 image or a supported upgrade package**. Both before/after runs used the same compatibility environment.

#### Reproduction protocol

The tested path was streaming client → HTTP gateway → native SGLang. An independent real-TCP test verified that the gateway closes its upstream connection approximately 25–28ms after the downstream client disconnects.

1. Submit eight concurrent streaming chat requests. Give each a distinct synthetic prefix of approximately 7K tokens; request `max_tokens=8192` and `ignore_eos=true` (actually forwarded to SGLang). Output is subject to the engine's remaining context budget.
2. Close each client one second after receiving nonempty content. After eight seconds, also cancel clients still waiting for content.
3. Sample engine running/queued request metrics and KV usage before, during, and for eight seconds after those closes.
4. Send a short non-streaming request asking for `OK`, with a 15-second client read budget.

Engine launch parameters used for this isolated experiment:

```bash
SGLANG_SKIP_SGL_KERNEL_VERSION_CHECK=1 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/Qwen3-0.6B --served-model-name repro \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18208 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.55 --context-length 16384 --max-total-tokens 16384 \
  --max-running-requests 4 --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \
  --attention-backend triton --disable-cuda-graph --enable-metrics
```

<details>
<summary>Tested bounded client probe (gateway at 127.0.0.1:18209, engine at 127.0.0.1:18208; requires httpx)</summary>

Save as `probe_gpu.py`, then run `python probe_gpu.py --route gateway --concurrency 8 --prompt-repeats 1000 --output result.json`. The probe never calls abort-all. Use a dedicated test instance and perform cleanup separately.

```python
"""Bounded client cancellation experiment. Only connects to this task's loopback ports."""
import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import time
from pathlib import Path
import httpx

async def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--route", choices=["native", "gateway"], required=True)
    p.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--concurrency", type=int, default=8)
    p.add_argument("--prompt-repeats", type=int, default=1000)
    p.add_argument("--n", type=int, choices=[1, 2], default=1)
    args = p.parse_args()
    if not 1 <= args.concurrency <= 16 or not 1 <= args.prompt_repeats <= 1500:
        p.error("probe load exceeds its bounded limits")
    if args.concurrency * args.n > 16:
        p.error("probe child request count exceeds its bounded limit")
    port = 18208 if args.route == "native" else 18209

comments.author: uzunenes
comments.body:
Production datapoint on v0.5.20 (includes #35255): DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, TP=2, DSPARK, 2×H200 NVL, ~97% streaming traffic, server running with `--log-level warning` (this warning is emitted at that level).

- Passive: ~28h / ~45K requests, 0 `state was deleted` warnings, 0 restarts.
- Controlled: 5 streaming `n=1` requests (`max_tokens=1024`) and 1 `n=2` request (`max_tokens=512`) against the live server, client socket closed ~2s after the first content chunk. 0 `state was deleted` lines in the pod log during the window, `/health` stayed 200, a follow-up short request returned 200 in 0.31s. Small sample on live traffic, so `num_running_reqs` could not be isolated per request; the absence of the log line is the signal.
- For context: on v0.5.19, under the same workload, a single orphan request produced ~39K warnings over 13.5 min without the detokenizer stalling. So the detokenizer-heartbeat/liveness-kill escalation I reported on v0.5.17 seems to need an additional factor beyond the warning flood.

Thanks for the fix.

shortlist.title: [Performance]: spec-decode boot-to-boot throughput dispersion on L4 (CV up to 13.92%), resolved in 0.30.0
shortlist.author: akshathtiwari
shortlist.body_excerpt:
### Proposal to improve performance

Not a proposal so much as a measurement suggestion. Speculative-decoding throughput on this stack is boot-dependent to a degree a single-boot benchmark cannot see: on 0.29.0 / L4, twelve boots of a byte-identical configuration gave CV 13.92% in one container and 3.73% in another. Anything comparing speculative configurations from one boot each is partly measuring which boot it got.

0.30.0 looks much better on this axis (0.99% and 1.61% across two containers on different physical cards), so this may already be resolved. I am reporting it mainly because the mechanism is not what I assumed, and the protocol seems worth having on record either way.

### Report of performance regression

Reporting this because 0.30.0 appears to resolve it, and the obvious explanation turns out to be wrong, so something else changed and I would like to know what.

**Setup.** Qwen3-4B target, `z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16` drafter, 5 speculative tokens, bf16 weights, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, FlashInfer pinned. GSM8K, concurrency 1, one fixed prompt set replayed on every boot. 12 boots per arm inside a single container, one physical GPU per session (UUID recorded). The harness speaks HTTP only and never imports vLLM.

Throughput at concurrency 1, output tokens/s:

| card | engine | session | default | --enforce-eager | ratio | default CV |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L4 (SM89) | 0.29.0 | A | 39.2 | 80.5 | **0.487** | **13.92%** |
| L4 (SM89) | 0.29.0 | B | 61.2 | 79.7 | **0.768** | **3.73%** |
| L4 (SM89) | 0.30.0 | C | 82.8 | 81.6 | **1.014** | 0.99% |
| L4 (SM89) | 0.30.0 | D | 78.2 | 77.0 | **1.017** | 1.61% |
| A10 (SM86) | 0.29.0 | E | 132.6 | 138.3 | 0.959 | 2.08% |

Each ratio is the default arm divided by the eager arm measured in the same container, so session and card effects cancel. On 0.29.0/L4 the CUDA-graph path runs at 49% and 77% of the eager path; on 0.30.0 it reaches parity. Acceptance length is flat throughout (tau 4.11-4.15), so this is throughput rather than a change in what the drafter gets accepted.

### Misc discussion on performance

Two observations, one related issue, and a question.

**1. The CUDA-graph fallback still fires on 0.30.0.** I had assumed the improvement was the speculative path gaining full graphs. It is not. The warning is byte-identical on both versions and capture proceeds under PIECEWISE in each:

> CUDAGraphMode.FULL_AND_PIECEWISE is not supported with spec-decode for attention backend FlashInferBackend (support: AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_SINGLE_TOKEN_DECODE); setting cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE

Backend selection is unchanged too: both versions log FLASHINFER for the target and FLASH_ATTN for the second selection. So neither graph mode nor backend choice explains the difference.

**2. On 0.29.0 the dispersion magnitude is itself not reproducible.** Two twelve-boot measurements of the identical configuration gave CV 13.92% and 3.73%, with means 39.2 and 61.2 tok/s. The effect is present in both; its size is not a property of the configuration. The eager arm is stable across every session measured (80.5, 79.7, 81.6, 77.0 on L4; 138.3 on A10), which is what makes it usable as a control.

**Related, but I do not think it is the same thing: #58677.** That reports the draft model's torch.compile cache identity flipping between exactly two values across restarts with byte-identical argv, attributed to the shared VllmConfig being mutated in-place during the main model's warmup and CUDA-graph-capture phase, before the draft head compiles. Two differences: the symptom there is startup recompile cost rather than steady-state throughput, and it reports 0.27.1 affected with 0.29 appearing immune, whereas what I measure is on 0.29.0.

Still, the shape is close enough that I would rather ask than assume: **if VllmConfig is mutated in place during graph capture and that mutation reaches what the draft compiles to, could the same mechanism produce a steady-state throughput difference and not only a cache-key difference?** My measurements begin after the server reports healthy, so any recompilation has finished by then.


**The question.** What changed between 0.29.0 and 0.30.0 on this path, given the fallback and the backend selection are identical in both? If a specific PR is responsible I would rather cite it than guess. I looked at #53867, #51700, #54646 and #52228 and could not attribute it from the release notes alone.

**Possibly relevant.** The effect is much weaker on an A10 (ratio 0.959) than on an L4 (0.487 and 0.768) at the same engine version. The A10 has 24 GiB against the L4's 22.03 GiB usable, and this configuration sits close enough to the memory ceiling that --enforce-eager alone decides whether an fp8_e4m3-KV variant boots at all. So capacity pressure may matter more here than architecture. I have not separated the two.

**Reproduction.** Harness, raw append-only records, analysis scripts and the engine logs are at https://github.com/akshathtiwari/spec-fp8-study (archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23033168). The boot-variance runs are one command each and the per-session numbers regenerate from the stored records. Happy to run further configurations if a specific one would help; the full sweep is a couple of GPU-hours.

### Your current environment (if you think it is necessary)

Not `collect_env.py` output: the engine runs in an ephemeral container on a rented GPU, so this machine's environment is not the one under test. These are the fields the harness records per measurement, read from nvidia-smi and from the running server.

```text
GPU         NVIDIA L4 (SM89, 22.03 GiB usable) and NVIDIA A10 (SM86)
            one physical card per session, gpu_uuid recorded per record
driver      580.95.05
CUDA        13.0
torch       2.13.0+cu130
vLLM        0.29.0 and 0.30.0, pinned by image digest. Version is read from
            the server's /version endpoint and checked against the declared
            value before any measu

comments.author: akshathtiwari
comments.body:
Correction to the "possibly relevant" paragraph in my original post.

I wrote that the A10 has 24 GiB against the L4's 22.03 GiB usable, and offered memory capacity as the likelier of two readings for why the deficit is weak on the A10. **That is wrong.** Both cards report **22.5 GiB** in my own records, and I had never checked the field before writing it. Capacity is not the difference between them.

What does differ, from the same records:

| | VRAM | arch | max SM clock | power limit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L4 | 22.5 GiB | SM8.9 | 2040 MHz | **72 W** |
| A10 | 22.5 GiB | SM8.6 | 1695 MHz | **150 W** |

So the card showing the deficit has less than half the power budget. That is a better fit for the symptom than capacity ever was: CUDA graphs run the work faster, faster work draws more power, and a 72 W part can hit its cap and clamp — variably, depending on thermal history, which would also explain why the dispersion magnitude itself does not reproduce between sessions. The eager arm runs slower, stays under the cap, and is stable in every session measured.

I want to be clear that this is a hypothesis and **my data cannot test it.** I was recording `clocks.max.sm` and `power.limit`, which are what the card is permitted to do, not what it did. A throttling explanation is precisely what configured limits cannot see.

I have since added sampling of achieved SM clock, power draw and `clocks_throttle_reasons.*` across the measurement window, and a run is in flight. If `sw_power_cap` is active during the default arm and not during the eager arm, that is the driver answering the question directly rather than me inferring it from a clock curve. I will post the result either way, including if it kills the hypothesis.

The throughput numbers and the ratio table in the original post are unaffected by this — they are measured, and the correction is to an explanation I attached to them.

shortlist.title: Restart-proof KV cache for llama-server: 40K-token TTFT 155s to 6s after reboot
shortlist.author: qqkzlm
shortlist.body_excerpt:
Every restart wipes your prefill. Server crash, box reboot, model reload — a 40K-token agentic prompt pays the full ~155s prefill again before the first token.

I patched llama-server to persist KV-cache prefix checkpoints to disk and auto-restore the longest matching prefix on boot. Same prompt after a restart: **first token in ~6s instead of ~155s** (2.1s disk read once + decode). No client changes, no re-architecture — the server just remembers.

Measured on GTX 1080 8GB, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, `-c 92160`:

- Cold: 151s prefill → first token at ~155s
- Warm (post-restart): 2.1s disk read (first request only) → first token at ~6s
- Checkpoints keyed by model + ctx + KV quant (wrong config = ignored, never corrupted); disk-budget eviction included

Single-commit patch (86KB): https://github.com/qqkzlm/llama-cpp-prompt-disk-cache — `git am` onto the PrismML `prism` branch, four flags (`--slot-save-path`, `--checkpoint-min-step`, `--ctx-checkpoints`, `--prompt-cache-disk-budget`).

One MoE lesson from the same box: keep experts on GPU, let KV follow the layers — pushing 20 MoE layers to CPU collapsed prefill 265→30 tok/s, which no cache can fix.

Happy to upstream behind a flag if maintainers are interested.

comments.author: qqkzlm
comments.body:
Update to the README since this went up — three things worth calling out for anyone trying it:

**1. Prebuilt CUDA binaries exist for both platforms.** The `v0.2.3` release ships `llama-server-win-cuda-v0.2.3.zip` and `llama-server-linux-cuda-v0.2.3.tar.gz`. The Linux package is built for `sm_61`/Pascal, so it also runs on GTX 10-series. No build needed:

```bash
./llama-server -m model.gguf -c 32768 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
  --slot-save-path /var/tmp/kvstore/model \
  --prompt-cache-disk-budget 20 --checkpoint-min-step 2048 --ctx-checkpoints 64
```

**2. Only one flag is actually required.** `--slot-save-path` is the only one you must pass — `--prompt-cache-disk-budget` and `--prompt-cache-disk-path` are silently ignored without it, and entries land in `<slot-save-path>/pdcache`. `--prompt-cache-disk` is **enabled by default**, so passing it is optional; use `--no-prompt-cache-disk` to turn the cache off.

**3. Cache hits require a byte-identical prompt prefix.** Only the common prefix from token 0 onward is reused. If you prepend a timestamp or a random ID, everything after it misses and the cache is effectively unused. Put stable content first (system prompt, tool definitions, long docs) and per-turn content last — opencode / Claude Code already do this, so it works out of the box.

The README now has a "when does the cache hit / when does it miss" section covering this, a flag-duty table, and a Chinese-first three-step guide (the repo README is now Chinese-primary). A Windows `start-llama-server.bat` is included in the zip if you want a prompt-driven launcher instead of a command line.

Still happy to upstream this behind a flag if maintainers are interested — the whole feature is one commit touching `tools/server/server-prompt-disk.cpp` (~900 lines) plus slot/task integration.

shortlist.title: [good-first-issue] tests: preserve phase timings for flaky long_doc_qa TTFT checks
shortlist.author: maobaolong
shortlist.body_excerpt:
Parent tracker: #5313 · Onboarding: #3372

## Confirmed flaky behavior

`k3-multiprocess-test / vllm / long_doc_qa / zmq` intermittently fails its time-to-first-token (TTFT) threshold on unchanged code:

| Build #5294, September 26, 2026 (UTC) | LMCache TTFT | Baseline TTFT | Verdict (at least 60% faster) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Original job](https://buildkite.com/lmcache/k3-multiprocess-test/builds/5294#01a0ddba-52b3-4ed4-8c7b-556bc2e41819) | 0.6464 s | 1.3012 s | **50.3% faster — FAIL** |
| [Retry](https://buildkite.com/lmcache/k3-multiprocess-test/builds/5294#01a0ddd3-60b4-40e2-aeda-af965c02a2b0) | 0.3950 s | 1.3337 s | **70.4% faster — PASS** |

Both jobs test `dev` commit **`dc68527c76fd08c5501e19097973938143f06348`**, without a PR-base merge, and install vLLM **`0.30.1rc1.dev193+gddd6fbca1`** and torch **`2.13.0+cu130`**. The query round-time check passes in both attempts.

There is a second independent same-build pair: [#5291 original](https://buildkite.com/lmcache/k3-multiprocess-test/builds/5291#01a0db7c-b789-4b24-bb2f-963ca51b94fd) gives 51.4% TTFT improvement, while [its retry](https://buildkite.com/lmcache/k3-multiprocess-test/builds/5291#01a0db9f-e858-4549-af74-a2f240bc0bf7) gives 72.6%. Both use `dev` commit `9a7b60501bc8ac3d0ab33b11dfd962ccfd02a5ae` and vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev142+g3a58aeb1a`.

These pairs confirm an intermittent test verdict. They do **not** establish whether the cause is cache readiness, runtime scheduling, or a performance defect.

## Bounded good-first task

Preserve separate per-request timings for the baseline and LMCache phases so this flake can be investigated without rerunning an entire GPU job blindly.

The benchmark currently writes `warmup_round.csv` and `query_round.csv` to its working directory. The wrapper launches baseline and LMCache sequentially in the same directory, so the second invocation overwrites the first phase's raw timings. The wrapper retains aggregate JSON but loses that raw comparison.

1. In the **L1 `long-doc-qa.sh` wrapper**, give baseline and LMCache separate output/working directories under the workload's existing `RESULTS_DIR`. Preserve each phase's CSVs, aggregate JSON, and text output on both success and threshold failure. Keep paths absolute when changing the child process's working directory.
2. Add a compact diagnostic summary that identifies the phase, effective workload settings, sample/success counts, and available timing distribution information. Keep the existing aggregate calculation and threshold semantics.
3. Make both phases' diagnostics accessible in public job output/artifacts. A container-local path by itself is not sufficient. Keep any artifact rule narrow to this workload; avoid a repository-wide artifact refactor.
4. Add CPU-only coverage with a stub benchmark writing distinguishable phase CSVs. Prove the baseline files survive the second invocation, and a failing threshold still leaves both phases inspectable and returns failure.

This is a diagnostic first step, not a claim that preserving CSVs fixes the TTFT variation. Do not loosen the 60% TTFT / 15% round-time requirements, add retries, or change cache semantics. Keep the L2 wrapper out of this issue so the sibling task remains independently claimable.

Starting points, checked at `42be9c7439a1eb0b17bf6b7565a894a9743fd052`:

- [L1 workload wrapper](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/42be9c7439a1eb0b17bf6b7565a894a9743fd052/.buildkite/k3_tests/multiprocess/scripts/workloads/common/long-doc-qa.sh).
- [Benchmark raw CSV output and aggregate calculation](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/42be9c7439a1eb0b17bf6b7565a894a9743fd052/benchmarks/long_doc_qa/long_doc_qa.py#L551).
- [Existing result cleanup/copying](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/42be9c7439a1eb0b17bf6b7565a894a9743fd052/.buildkite/k3_tests/multiprocess/scripts/cleanup.sh).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Baseline and LMCache raw timings coexist and are clearly attributed.
- [ ] CPU regression coverage proves phase isolation and preservation on failure.
- [ ] A GPU job exposes both phases' data through public output/artifacts, including a failing comparison.
- [ ] Threshold failures retain a nonzero exit status; no assertion is removed or weakened.
- [ ] The PR distinguishes completed diagnostics from any remaining cause of the intermittent timing result.

## Reproduce the CI workload

The evidence below comes from CI; this issue does not claim a local GPU reproduction. Use a dedicated Linux x86_64 GPU test host with Docker and NVIDIA Container Toolkit, two available CUDA GPUs capable of running separate `Qwen/Qwen3-14B` servers, sufficient host RAM for the default 80 GiB LMCache buffer (plus the mock L2 storage for the L2 case), and disk/network access for the image, wheels, and model. CI uses CUDA 13.0, Python 3.12, and a 1 GiB `/dev/shm`. A maintainer can run the GPU validation for a contributor who only has a CPU machine.

These commands build the public CI image recipe, explicitly start Bash, and pin the historical LMCache and vLLM revisions. They are a reproduction recipe, not a fully locked copy of every historical dependency or GPU scheduling condition. Run from a fresh directory; make the actual PR against current `dev`.

cd LMCache
git checkout dc68527c76fd08c5501e19097973938143f06348
docker build -t lmcache-flake-ci \

  --entrypoint bash \

  -e INFERENCE_ENGINE=vllm \
